An insurance executive is suspected of fatally shooting his wife and daughter before taking his own life inside their New Jersey mansion.

Montgomery Township Police responded to a welfare check last Thursday at the family’s mansion, according to the Somerset County Prosecutor’s Office.

Police were initially unable to contact the family, and a day later, they gained access to the home — listed on the real estate marketplace Zillow for more than $1.7 million — and found two women in two separate bedrooms dead from gunshot wounds to the head. Officers also found a man with what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound to the head, prosecutors said.

On Tuesday, the man was identified as David Grodnick, 61, and the women were identified as Grodnick’s 62-year-old wife, Lora Grodnick, and their 24-year-old daughter, Sloane Grodnick.

Grodnick was the senior vice president and underwriting counsel at Land Services USA, a real estate title insurance company, according to a report from The Montgomery News and a LinkedIn page that matches the description.

open image in gallery David Grodnick, a 61-year-old insurance executive, has been accused of shooting his wife and daughter before taking his own life inside their New Jersey mansion ( Google Earth )

The Montgomery News first reported the suspected murder-suicide. The Independent has reached out to Land Services USA for comment.

Neighbors reportedly said Grodnick and his wife had been members of the elite Bedens Brook Country Club in their hometown of Skillman.

Solane Grodnick graduated from the private Hun School of Princeton in 2020 and then Savannah College of Art and Design in 2024, according to The Montgomery News and her Instagram. She was set to graduate from the Rhode Island School of Design with a Master of Fine Arts degree next year.

The investigation into the Grodnicks’ deaths remains ongoing.

“The homicide deaths of both Lora and Sloane Grodnick were an isolated incident, and there are no threats to the public from this tragic occurrence,” the Somerset County Prosecutor’s Office said.

Local officials have asked anyone with information relating to the probe to contact the Somerset County Prosecutor’s Office Major Crimes Unit at (908) 231-7100 or the Montgomery Police Department at (908) 359-3222.

News.title: Thomas Tuchel hails ‘brilliant, brilliant’ Harry Kane after landmark double
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Thomas Tuchel says Harry Kane deserves all of the accolades after marking his record-equalling England appearance with a decisive display in the Nations League defeat of Czechia.

The skipper continued his wondrous form on Tuesday at Wembley, where he scored a brace having forced Vladimir Coufal into an own goal as he joined Peter Shilton on 125 caps.

Kane was given a standing ovation as he was taken off towards the end of a 3-0 victory that all but assured England of a place in the Nations League quarter-finals.

“Brilliant, brilliant,” boss Tuchel said. “I think the team performance was very good, and Harry’s performance was very good.

open image in gallery Harry Kane starred against Czechia on his record-equalling night (Adam Davy/PA)

“He was again decisive for us and on this very special day for him, to equal the record of Peter Shilton, puts him on this kind of level.

“Amazing. He deserves the stage, he deserves the praise.”

Kane is set to move clear as England’s most-capped men’s player next month against Croatia, who Tuchel’s team thumped 7-0 in Rijeka on Saturday.

That swashbuckling win and 2-0 victory in Prague last week helped make amends for the helter-skelter 3-2 loss to Spain the Group A3 opener as they continue to move on from the World Cup.

Asked if he feels the side are a step further ahead than they were at the end of the summer, Tuchel said: “Yeah, of course, and that’s what we have to do.

“That is our goal, to constantly improve and develop. We have these experiences together, and we had a big tournament together.

open image in gallery England enjoyed another victory (John Walton/PA)

“It was very positive and still it’s necessary to move forward and to improve, especially in sports and this is what we’re trying to do.

“We adjusted some details in our structure, and we didn’t compromise on the effort and the intensity and on the togetherness of the team.

“The players who were with us in the World Cup took care of these standards and of the culture within the team, off the pitch and on the pitch.

“I think that’s what you could see and you just could see the positive on a long camp is that you have time for debriefs, that you have time for meetings, you have more time for training, you spend more time.

“And together you can develop something because the common language sinks in, the patterns sink in, and, again like after a big victory in Croatia, we put in the things that we don’t want to compromise on.

“The intensity, the effort and we created a good momentum throughout the match, created chances, scored beautiful goals, so it was a very good camp overall.”

News.title: Harry Kane equals Peter Shilton record as most-capped England player
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Harry Kane became England’s joint highest cap winner after starting and netting a brace in their Nations League win over Czech Republic at Wembley.

The 33-year-old joins Peter Shilton on 125 appearances as he captains a side featuring four changes from the 7-0 win over Croatia on Saturday.

Kane also edged closer to the magical 100-goal mark, moving his total to 91 goals with six in four during the current international window.

“Brilliant, brilliant,” England boss Thomas Tuchel said of his striker. “I think the team performance was very good, and Harry’s performance was very good.

“He was again decisive for us and on this very special day for him, to equal the record of Peter Shilton, puts him on this kind of level.

“Amazing. He deserves the stage, he deserves the praise.”

Kane’s bow came against Lithuania in March 2015 aged 21, when he scored the first of his many goals for the national team.

The England captain registered an assist as Vladimir Coufal poked his cross into his own net before bagging a brace either side of half-time, the first finishing off a superb team move after Elliot Anderson threaded a brilliant ball to Morgan Rogers.

Kane’s second was a header from a Lewis Hall corner, before England sat back to see out another comfortable win after a 3-0 victory in the reverse fixture.

The result sees them needing just one point from the November international window to book their place in the Nations League quarter-finals in March.

Additional reporting from PA

News.title: Trump reveals why tariff is only his ‘fifth favorite word’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Donald Trump went on a largely aimless rant to a group of Navy midshipmen and a handful of members of the armed forces’ top brass on Tuesday as he announced the construction of a new submarine shipyard in Baltimore, Maryland.

The president spoke in front of a combat vessel at Sparrows Point, Maryland, where he announced that defense contractor Anduril would build the facility to support the construction of the Navy’s new autonomous submarine craft. But the point of his visit was once again obscured by an unfocused diatribe about the war in Iran, the U.S. strike on Venezuela, and the tariff policies his administration has used to reshape global trade frameworks.

Trump repeated a refrain about tariffs becoming his “fifth” favorite word, after others such as “wife” and “God”, to a mostly silent batch of bored Navy undergrads who came up from the Naval Academy in Annapolis to stand and hear the president talk. The president claimed that tariff was actually his favorite word, but under pressure from his critics, he lowered its importance.

“We're building more car plants than we ever have in history,” the president told his audience. “It's all because of my favorite word, my fourth favorite, maybe my fifth-- tariff. Without tariffs, we wouldn't be doing that.”

”The word tariff for us has made us a rich country again, and rich in a lot of ways,” Trump added.

open image in gallery The president addressed a group of midshipmen in Baltimore as he announced the construction of a new shipbuilding facility ( AFP/Getty )

Anduril is partnering with the Navy on the project, which will see a $3.7bn, 2 million square foot facility built at Sparrows Point, just steps away from the site of the destroyed Francis Scott Key Bridge that once crossed Baltimore’s Patapsco River. Construction of a new bridge is set to be finished in late 2030. Anduril promises that the new shipyard will be home to approximately 3,100 new jobs.

Absent from Tuesday’s announcement ceremony were Baltimore city officials and the state’s governor, Wes Moore. A Democrat, Moore said through a spokesperson on Tuesday that the White House initially invited him to speak at the event, then moved him to a non-speaking role at Trump’s intervention. The White House denied this, claiming that Moore was only invited as a guest to the ceremony.

Typically, the announcement ceremony for such a facility’s groundbreaking would include statements from at least a few local officials. That didn’t take place on Tuesday for one reason: Trump’s political opposition to Moore and city leadership in Baltimore, who are all Democrats and were denied the spotlight on Tuesday. The president was joined by Iowa’s Republican governor one month ago when he announced the development of a new steel plant in Lee County.

White House officials have Trump on the campaign trail stumping for Republicans across the country in October, with the midterm elections now just a month away. The president’s party is in dire polling straits, with the Cook Political Report announcing Tuesday that it was moving Senate races in favor of the Democrats once again, declaring Texas a likely flip and Kansas a toss-up. Driven by Trump’s own polling and woeful economic conditions spurred by the war in Iran and conflict in the Hormuz Strait, Republican popularity is at an all-time low at a moment when the party is trying to defend majorities in both the House and Senate.

open image in gallery The president has attacked news reporters for talking about issues like affordability and fuel prices ( Getty )

As part of that push, Trump is hard at work selling the core of his economic agenda, which was carried out through his tariff policies at the executive level after slim GOP congressional majorities proved unable to pass most policy legislation. The Trump administration levied so-called “reciprocal” tariffs on dozens of countries, aimed at forcing companies involved in the U.S. market to reshore manufacturing or risk steeper penalties.

U.S. manufacturing has grown under Trump’s second term as a result. The growth, though, has been overshadowed in many Americans’ eyes by spikes in gas and food prices alongside the general chaotic nature of the Trump presidency, which has slashed tens of thousands of federal jobs and pursued an erratic foreign policy that has angered close U.S. trading partners and geopolitical allies.

With just weeks to go until the midterm elections, gas and diesel prices remain at their highest points since the Covid-era supply squeezes pushed prices to extreme levels. Other areas of the U.S. economy continue to see persistent inflation as well, which many economists have linked to the tariff agenda pursued by Trump since he returned to office.

Trump has tried to reassure Americans of the economy’s strength as the home stretch of the midterm campaign season nears, and has faulted the media for not painting a rosier picture of voters’ feelings about their financial futures.

News.title: Personal information for over 1 million people stolen in a cyberattack on Arizona's court system
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A cyberattack on Arizona’s court system stole personal information for more than a million people and is believed to have started when a court employee clicked a malicious link in an email.

The Arizona Supreme Court said the information was copied for 1.3 million people with unpaid court fees, fines and restitution payments for traffic and criminal violations dating back as far as 30 years.

Those leading the attack also took records of nearly 30,000 active and inactive orders of protection and 150,000 reports dating back to 2010 from a foster care board that makes recommendations in cases where parents are alleged to be unfit or unable to care for a child.

The court’s technology staff shut down the attack on a backup server about two hours after spotting it on Sept. 24. Since then, the court has notified those affected by the breach.

“We don’t have any evidence it has been used or shared” after the attack, state Supreme Court spokesperson Alberto Rodriguez said Tuesday.

The attack, which is under investigation, hasn’t affected or delayed any court cases, Rodriguez said.

No records were altered or deleted, and the attackers didn’t steal information about jurors, witnesses or court employees.

News.title: Jaguar finally unveils the most talked-about car of the decade – and its eye-watering price
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

After nearly two years of arguments about logos, pink paint, what’s woke and what’s not, and what a Jaguar really should be, here’s the car customers will actually be able to buy. The new Jaguar Type 01 has been revealed in New York and its vital statistics are as striking as the production car’s looks.

This is an all-electric four-door GT with up to 1,016bhp, an expected maximum range of 450 miles and prices expected to centre around £125,000.

Jaguar’s advertising campaign in November 2024 featured brightly dressed models, but no car. Then came the Type 00 concept at Miami Art Week that December, shown in pink and blue. Supporters welcomed a bold change; critics questioned what was left of the Jaguar they knew.

Now, fully revealed, the Type 01 turns that two-door design study’s ideas into a four-door production car. I’ve seen it in the metal a few times now, already ridden in a disguised prototype, and we showed you the interior in August. With the whole car uncovered, the long bonnet, huge wheels and missing rear window have all survived the journey. So has the Jaguar leaper, now found on the side finishers.

open image in gallery Plenty of the Type 00 Concept from 2024 has found its way onto the Type 01 production car, including the strikethrough graphic at the back of the car ( Jaguar )

The price jump is deliberate, too. Managing director Rawdon Glover describes that expected £125,000 centre of gravity as “double where we were”, although it isn’t a confirmed starting price – he sees an opening between premium cars costing up to £120,000 and the luxury market at £300,000 and above.

But why not a big-selling SUV? That will come, for sure, but the GT was chosen to introduce the new Jaguar because it could better change perceptions, not because it’s expected to be the biggest seller.

Glover said: “Jaguars should be objects of desire and culturally relevant – that’s their natural habitat and where Jaguar is returning.”

Orders are expected to open in early 2027, with the first customers getting their cars in the second half of the year.

There’s been a change from the figures discussed alongside the Type 00, too. Jaguar originally targeted a maximum claimed range of 478 miles for its production GT; the expectation now is up to 450 miles from a 118kWh usable battery. The charging claim has improved, though: a 200-mile top-up is now a little quicker at 13 minutes, against the 15 minutes discussed in 2024.

For all the talk of starting again, there are some familiar Jaguar ideas beneath the new look. Take the Luxury Gap. I know it as an album by Heaven 17, but to a car designer it’s the distance from the centre of the front wheel to the leading edge of the front door. Here it’s 898mm, or 17 per cent of the car’s length – almost the same proportion as it is on an E-type.

Proportions came up repeatedly in my conversations with the people behind the car. At 5,235mm long, with around 3,200mm between the front and rear wheels, the Type 01 is big, but stands just 1,403mm tall. There’s very little bodywork ahead of the front wheels and an extended tail. The standard 23-inch wheels and tyres measure 763mm across, more than half the car’s height, although a smaller, 21-inch alternative is available.

open image in gallery The Jaguar Type 01 is a sizeable car at 5,235mm in length ( Jaguar )

The four-light signature across the nose will become a Jaguar calling card, with the brand’s slimmest headlights yet, at 84mm high. Each has 17,000 pixels to control its beam. At the back, the lights hide within horizontal bars until switched on, beneath those broad shoulders.

Making that rear end has taken rather more than a designer’s pen. The sharply folded bodywork around the rear side window required what Jaguar calls the Impossible Panel. Engineers spent more than 1,500 hours working out how to produce it, eventually using six stages of pressing in a machine four storeys high at Halewood. The frameless doors close directly against the body without visible seals or extra trim, while the flush handles can apparently push through 4mm of ice.

Inside, that low roof becomes rather more personal. Chief engineer Jon Darlington told me: “It’s important to sit in a Jaguar, not on a Jaguar”. The Type 01 has Jaguar’s slimmest seats yet, and although I usually lower a seat as far as it will go, here I was inclined to raise it, otherwise it felt a bit like sitting in a deep bathtub. A central spine divides the cabin into four individual spaces, with brass-effect trim running along it and the tops of the doors.

open image in gallery The interior of the Jaguar Type 01 is almost as striking as the exterior with no buttons, just touchscreens ( Jaguar )

The missing rear window has a practical answer, and one that works particularly well even with my ageing eyesight. Jaguar hasn’t put a camera-fed screen where a rear-view mirror would normally sit, its ClearSight display is further away, at the base of the windscreen and level with the door mirrors. I’m long-sighted and usually need glasses for close-up screens, so that extra distance made the image easier to see.

The screen sits within a soundbar containing 13 of the Meridian audio system’s 38 speakers. The other 25 are tucked around the cabin, including the roof lining, rear doors and headrests, leaving the front doors free of speakers. The front seats can pulse with the music, while the headrest speakers help cancel road noise. There’s a bespoke Jaguar soundscape, too.

Jaguar worked with Aachen University in Germany on how people interact with the cabin. A 24-inch OLED display puts driver information on its outer section, with media and navigation towards the centre. Separate seven-inch portrait touchscreens front and rear handle temperature, seats and music with familiar taps, swipes and dragging gestures. Jaguar says most functions are available within two taps, and conversational voice control can even open the charging flap.

open image in gallery Seven-inch portrait touchscreens front and rear handle temperature, seats and music with familiar taps, swipes and dragging gestures ( Jaguar )

The Nvidia-powered computer is claimed to be ten times faster than Jaguar’s previous generation and supports over-the-air updates. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, alongside charging for two phones and a hotspot for eight devices. There are streaming and gaming apps, with video on the front screen available when parked. Some connected services will require renewed subscriptions after the vehicle warranty expires, though.

Cupholders and air vents stay hidden until needed, storage compartments reveal flashes of colour and the standard panoramic glass roof has an electronic shade. All four seats are heated and cooled, with 12-way electrical adjustment and hot-stone-style massage in the front. Four-zone climate control, air purification, a fragrance diffuser and cabin mood settings are included, too.

There’s room for luggage as well as people. The powered tailgate opens onto more than 450 litres of boot space, increasing to 1,000 litres when the rear seats fold in a 50:50 split. Further storage sits beneath the floor, with space for emergency kit under the bonnet.

open image in gallery A huge amount of engineering effort went into creating this 'impossible panel' at the back of the Jaguar Type 01 ( Jaguar )

As for how it should drive, engineers went back to the classic V12-engined XJC for inspiration, to study its blend of performance and comfort. The Type 01 is Jaguar’s most powerful road car yet, with 0–62mph taking 3.2 seconds, but the team is particularly keen to talk about its ability to go from 62–112mph in four seconds. The intention is to have plenty of power left when you’re already moving, rather than concentrating only on getting away from the traffic lights.

Three electric motors provide all-wheel drive and 1,365Nm of torque, with one motor at the front and two at the back. Power delivery favours the rear in a 30:70 split, rising to as much as 87 per cent rearwards in Dynamic mode. Weight is shared evenly between front and rear, with double-wishbone front and integral-link rear suspension, variable air springs and twin-valve adaptive dampers. Pirelli has developed tyres specifically for the car.

When I went for a ride in the Type 01 with Jaguar’s chassis guru Matt Becker, I was surprised how nimble the car felt for something so large and so heavy, yet even on the roughest roads around JLR’s test track, it still had a good degree of comfort – just as that XJC did all those years ago.

open image in gallery For a car so big and heavy, the Jaguar Type 01 rides and handles impressively well ( Jaguar )

For the less glamorous business of turning the Type 01 around, the back wheels steer by up to six degrees. That gives this large GT an 11,500mm wall-to-wall turning circle, comparable to a compact family car. Surrounding cameras work with the rear-view display for tighter manoeuvres; the assistance systems use ten external cameras, five radars and 12 ultrasonic sensors, with the front radar behind a heated Jaguar badge.

Drivers get Jaguar, Dynamic, Efficient and Ice & Snow modes, plus their own combination in Curated mode. There are three levels of energy-recovering braking, too, and a separate one-pedal setting.

Beyond the headline range figure, Jaguar is being bold enough to quote up to 320 miles at a steady 75mph, not that I’d be doing that, obviously. And Jaguar’s analysis of journeys by 920,000 JLR vehicles found 99.7 per cent covered no more than 303 miles.

open image in gallery The Jaguar Type 01 claims a total range of 450 miles, but will apparently travel for 320 miles at a steady 75mph ( Jaguar )

At a suitable rapid charger, the Type 01 can take up to 350kW, with a 10–80 per cent charge taking around 22 minutes. Its 850-volt system can also charge the battery in two sections, allowing up to 250kW from a suitable 400-volt charger. Jaguar says US cars will have NACS compatibility for Tesla Superchargers, too.

One of the simpler ideas could save some parking shuffles: there are AC charging sockets on both sides, behind powered flaps, accepting up to 22kW. As you’d hope, there’s a suitably stylish Jaguar home wallbox available, while the new Jaguar app can cover scheduled charging, route planning and public charger availability, with participating public networks in the UK and Europe brought together on one monthly bill. The car is smart enough to prepare its battery temperature before a charging stop and recycles warmth from the motors to heat the cabin or battery.

Getting that large battery into such a low car helps explain why Jaguar developed entirely new underpinnings. Rather than stacking more cells beneath the seats and raising the roof, engineers put 32 of the 200 nickel-rich cells ahead of the passenger compartment, protected by a new front crash structure. Those extra cells contribute up to 70 miles of range and 148bhp, while gaps in the pack under the floor leave foot space for rear passengers.

open image in gallery The Luxury Gap is not a Heaven 17 album, it's the space between the centre of the wheel and the front door on a Jaguar Type 01. It features a brass embellishment with a Jaguar leaper in it ( Jaguar )

Such was the no-compromise approach to the Type 01, Jaguar had to develop its own platform. The new Jaguar Electric Architecture is 73 per cent aluminium, with the battery helping form the brand’s stiffest body-and-battery structure yet – even the electrical junction box doubles as a brace for the front suspension.

The design team clearly set their engineering colleagues some tough tasks, but they’re still talking. And the end result is the purest of looks with some clever engineering solutions. For example, there’s just 133mm between the front wheelarch and bonnet, 100mm less than on the F-Type sports car, yet there’s still 22mm more room for the wheels to move up and down. It’s no surprise, then, that more than 360 patent applications came out of the development work.

The motors borrow control technology from Jaguar’s championship-winning Formula E programme, with gearing chosen for efficient high-speed cruising. When their performance isn’t needed, the rear motors can be switched off, contributing up to 18 miles of range.

open image in gallery Jaguar's Clearsight digital rear-view screen sits at the base of the windscreen in the centre of a 13-speaker sound bar ( Jaguar )

Small changes to the body have helped, too. More than 7,000 wind-tunnel tests produced a drag figure of 0.23, Jaguar’s lowest yet, without any individual aerodynamic change to the shape exceeding 8mm. Tweaks around the front corners and sides added 12 miles of range; opening vanes across the nose contribute up to 27 miles. All wheel designs have lightweight aerodynamic inserts, and a three-stage rear spoiler works with a 15mm drop in ride height when cruising.

The clever aerodynamics even generate a small forward push from air pressure at the back of the car, equivalent to 4kg at around 87mph, helping reduce overall drag.

Buyers get eight paint finishes, including satin blue and copper, and three interior colour schemes combining wool-blend textiles with leather or an Ultrafabrics NeoGrain alternative. The launch Design Vision edition pairs satin silver paint with its own 23-inch wheels, brass-effect side finishers with the Jaguar leaper embossed in them, plus an Orchid White or Dusk Grey cabin. The Chromatic Moments collection will be limited to 60 cars worldwide, in French Ultramarine Blue or London Red.

open image in gallery The Jaguar Type 01 has been wholly designed and engineered in the UK and will be built in Solihull, West Midlands ( Jaguar )

The thinking behind the car predates the public arguments. Project Pantera began in 2021, following an explorative Project Renaissance, when three design teams produced a total of 18 models to explore a new direction. Glover says powertrain type was only eighth on potential buyers’ list of priorities, with just 20 per cent rejecting a car without a combustion engine. The Type 01 name links Jaguar’s new Type models with zero tailpipe emissions plus it’s the first car of a new generation.

Having been totally designed and engineered in Britain, the Type 01 will be built at Solihull alongside the Range Rover and Range Rover Sport – which might be a bit of a concern as neither of those models have the best reliability reputation. However, after all the debate about Jaguar’s appearance and ambitions, Glover has been clear about another priority for the car customers will take home. “We must get the quality right,” he said.

Whether all that adds up to a winning formula for Jaguar remains to be seen, while plenty of effort has gone into the way the car is sold at those Jaguar retailers that stayed with the brand over the recent fallow years.

Of course, one car doesn’t make a company, and the Type 01 will undoubtedly be followed, at least, by Type 02 and Type 03 – one of which is likely to be a more practical crossover type car and the other an SUV, of course. But the Type 01 lays down a marker for what comes next, and has to do the heavy lifting of repositioning this famous old British car brand into more esteemed, and more profitable circles.

News.title: Woman faked being a substitute teacher just to go into class and berate the teens
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Read our Privacy notice

A Wisconsin woman has been accused of pretending to be a teacher — not to uplift and inspire — but to level her gripes with kids these days.

Amy Jones, 23, went to her alma mater on September 24 under the guise of a substitute teacher and spent nearly three classroom periods berating and cursing at the students, as well as asking them lewd questions, before she was escorted out of the school, according to Milwaukee County officials.

Students at Rufus King International High School told a school resource officer that Jones was “using profane language, racial slurs, sexually derogatory statements and organizing students by race and gender in class,” according to a criminal complaint obtained by local outlet WISN.

She allegedly called one student “fat boy,” asked another student “if she wanted to be a stripper or a hooker,” and allegedly told two white students that “they were the type of people to start school shootings,” a 16-year-old boy told authorities.

Jones also allegedly asked if any students had a vape or weed because class was “so f***ing lame and annoying,” Fox6 News Milwaukee reported, citing the complaint.

open image in gallery Amy Jones, a 23-year-old Wisconsin woman, has been accused of pretending to be a teacher, not to uplift and inspire — but to level her gripes with kids these days ( Milwaukee County Sheriff's Office )

Jones was escorted from the school by police after the principal, Doreen Badillo, became aware of the situation.

Badillo told authorities that eight teachers called in sick that day and only seven positions were filled, so she believed Jones “got lucky.”

When questioned by police, Jones allegedly said she went to her old high school “because she was bored” and that she “hates kids and she just wanted to f*** around."

Jones was taken into custody last Thursday, according to local jail records.

She is facing six felony charges, including one count of impersonating a public employee and five counts of exposing a child to harmful descriptions. If convicted, she could be sentenced to a maximum of 21 years in prison.

open image in gallery Students at Rufus King International High School told a school resource officer that Jones was 'using profane language, racial slurs, sexually derogatory statements and organizing students by race and gender in class,' according to a criminal complaint ( Google Earth )

Her defense team has argued that she is managing bipolar disorder and had a problem with her medication delivery on the day she allegedly posed as a substitute teacher, WISN reported.

In a statement to the school community Tuesday, Badillo said Jones “did go through the school’s daily safety scan” but that the office “did not follow proper district protocol in validating the individual as a substitute teacher.”

Badillo said the office workers must check that the person coming to fill in for a teacher is in a system of substitute teachers called Frontline and is “assigned to the school based on a specific teacher’s absence” before allowing them in the classrooms.

“This should happen every time a substitute visits a school. There is no excuse for it not occurring, and we take this matter seriously,” Badillo said. “We understand how disturbing this is, and we are taking every step to address where errors happened.”

Badillo said the matter is still under an internal investigation.

Jones has a preliminary hearing scheduled for October 20.

News.title: Christa Pike awake, speaking — and shackled to her bed days after botched execution
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Christa Pike, an inmate who survived Tennessee’s botched attempt to execute her, is awake and speaking as she receives treatment at a hospital, her attorneys said Tuesday evening.

Pike, now 50, was 18 when she and her boyfriend tortured and killed a classmate, Colleen Slemmer, in 1995, making her one of the youngest women sent to death row in modern U.S. history. Her execution was delayed for more than eight hours last Wednesday as the U.S. Supreme Court considered, and ultimately overturned, a federal appeals court ruling to halt her lethal injection so judges could review claims regarding childhood sexual abuse.

“Against all odds, Christa Pike is conscious, speaking, and continues to receive critical medical care. Despite the severe damage she endured to her arms, she is still handcuffed and shackled to the bed,” attorneys for Pike said in a statement. “Her recovery is medically unprecedented. Her prognosis remains unclear but, at a minimum, we expect a long recovery.”

Her attorneys said they are grateful for the first responders and the medical team at the hospital “who treated Christa like a human and have provided exceptional care to her.”

The statement was the first indication that Pike has improved since an ambulance carried her away from a Nashville prison last Wednesday. Pike survived two doses of pentobarbital as Tennessee officials attempted to put her to death on September 30. Although the lethal injection drug failed to end her life, her defense team said the procedure left her arms burned and blistered.

open image in gallery Defense attorneys say 50-year-old death row inmate Christa Pike is off a ventilator but remains handcuffed to her hospital bed nearly a week after a botched execution in Tennessee ( Reuters )

On Sunday, her lawyer, assistant federal defender Stephen Ferrell, told CNN, “She's still in the hospital on a ventilator, critically ill. We don't really know the prognosis yet and may not know for several days.”

Asked at the time if she had regained consciousness, Ferrell replied: “Not that I’m aware of,” adding that doctors were still trying to clear the high barbiturate dosage out of her system.

Dr. Joel Zivot, an anesthesiology and surgery professor in Atlanta who consulted as an expert for Pike’s legal team, said her recent progress “bodes well for a good recovery.”

However, Zivot cautioned that it could be weeks or months before the full extent of her recovery is known, including whether her mental competency could be restored to a level that would allow the state to attempt another execution, as reported by the Associated Press.

open image in gallery Christa Pike was 18 when she was sentenced to death for the 1995 killing of her 19-year-old Knoxville Job Corps classmate Colleen Slemmer ( Knoxville News-Sentinel )

“She’s still in the ICU,” Zivot said. “She has recovered to a certain degree that she’s able to be off a ventilator and able to speak, but in no way would I announce her free of further serious risk. There’s still a lot of bad things that can happen here, even when everyone is doing their job well.”

A spokesperson for the Tennessee Department of Correction said she could provide no information other than confirming Pike remained hospitalized Tuesday.

Pike’s defense team is scheduled to appear in court Wednesday morning for a status conference before Chancery Court Judge I’Ashea Myles. The attorneys are seeking a court order requiring state correction officials to preserve evidence from the execution attempt, including drug lot numbers and administrative records.

open image in gallery Emergency vehicles arrived at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville, Tennessee, after Pike’s execution was suspended — medical experts caution that although Pike is conscious and speaking, her long-term prognosis and mental competency remain uncertain ( AP )

In their Tuesday statement, her lawyers renewed calls for outgoing Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee to commute Pike’s sentence to life in prison without parole.

“Christa is a survivor and will take recovery one day at a time,” they said.

Following Pike’s hospitalization, Lee halted all further executions and ordered a comprehensive third-party review into the execution attempt. U.S. Sen. Marsha Blackburn, the Republican candidate running to replace Lee, urged the state to explore alternative execution methods to ensure capital punishment continues in Tennessee.

The failed execution has raised complex constitutional questions regarding whether Tennessee can lawfully attempt a second execution.

open image in gallery Outgoing Gov. Bill Lee has ordered a comprehensive third-party investigation and halted all future executions in the state ( AFP/Getty )

Deborah Denno, a Fordham Law professor who has studied execution methods for 36 years, told the Associated Press that Pike faces unresolved issues regarding her competency, double jeopardy, and cruel and unusual punishment.

“She has satisfied this very, very high standard for cruel and unusual punishment,” Denno said. “She also has a very good double-jeopardy argument. They carried out every aspect of the execution. She didn’t die, but every process they intended, they did it.”

Other legal experts expressed skepticism that higher courts would bar a second attempt. Seattle University Law Professor Michael Russo, a former Los Angeles public defender in capital cases, acknowledged the unprecedented nature of the case.

“There’s nobody else in the history of the death penalty in this country who has gone through what she’s been through,” Russo said. But he added, “I think what this Supreme Court would say is, her sentence was to die — to be executed — not to suffer an attempt at execution.”

News.title: Kane’s record-equalling cap was no different to his first
News.content:
One expects that when the end comes it will not be as rancorous as the final exit of Cristiano Ronaldo from Portugal, a drama playing out elsewhere. At some point, Kane will take his leave and it is likely to be as unassuming as the rest of it. He will be back at Wembley, injury permitting, for cap No 126 next month against Croatia. He talks like a different person to the one he was even five years ago – with a confidence and certainty about his place in the world. As opposed to the younger Kane, who seemed to regard everything outside his goalscoring tunnel vision with a general sense of bemusement.

“Availability,” he said, “is one of the biggest strengths you can have at this level for any coach.” He was keen to emphasise his “all-round leadership” too, “a lot of assets off the pitch”. He still measures himself in goals, of course, and perhaps there will be a Ballon d’Or too later this month – a prize that has eluded generations of England players before him who have won much more for their clubs than Kane has done. The good news for Kane is that his last England years will be spent in a very good England team – one which was on another level to its opposition on this occasion too.

No team in the top tier of the Nations League has scored more goals than England – 14 in the last four match days. Tuchel’s name was sung at Wembley and even if the World Cup semi-final collapse in Atlanta in July has not been entirely forgotten, the roughest edges have been taken off somewhat. Another great performance from Jude Bellingham and also from Morgan Rogers, in place of Bukayo Saka. Another dominant Elliot Anderson performance in midfield. They left Wembley to applause and a sense of optimism renewed.

England kept the ball with such authority, and none more so than Bellingham. Trent Alexander-Arnold came back at right-back. Myles Lewis-Skelly returned for another bite at a Wembley midfield job. As in Prague last week, there was a self-inflicted Czech calamity in the first half. The captain Vladimir Coufal appeared to lose his cool at the threat of the England attack all over the Czechs’ half. No other reason for this Premier League experienced full-back to fling himself at Kane’s cross and drill the ball past Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek on 27 minutes.

News.title: UK not prepared for food shortages, experts warn
News.content:
Britain has no way to feed its population of 66 million people in a crisis, a letter addressed to the Prime Minister has warned.

Climate change, cyber-attacks, geopolitical shifts, and energy shocks could put Britain’s food supply at great risk – and the UK is “complacent”, the letter says.

The document was delivered to Andy Burnham on Monday and was signed by 180 experts including academics, farmers, local council leaders, and foodbank workers.

Britain’s food supply is now heavily globalised, with roughly 45-50 per cent of food imported from countries like Spain, the Netherlands and France, as well as South Africa, Columbia and Brazil.

The system provides a cheap and constant supply of food – seasonal or not – but if international supply chains are disrupted, the UK’s home production is “woefully inadequate in [being able to produce] many different food types” , the letter argues.

It adds that “international food supplies can be weaponised”.

Crucially, the UK operates a ‘just-in-time’ food system – meaning hardly any food is stocked and stored in reserves, but is constantly moving from farms and ports directly to supermarket and wholesale shelves when needed.

“When you go to a supermarket and check out, you think, well, ‘it’s adding up the bill’ – it is, but what it’s also doing is reordering,” Tim Lang, emeritus professor of food policy at City University, a signatory of the letter and author of the Just in Case report – a major review that analysed the UK’s food system for the National Preparedness Commission, previously told The Telegraph.

News.title: Kenya confirms first ever case of Ebola after man dies in Nairobi
News.content:
Kenya confirmed its first ever case of Ebola on Tuesday after a Kenyan citizen who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo died in Nairobi.

Kenya is the third country to record a case linked to the Ebola epidemic in eastern Congo, the second largest on record. Uganda reported 20 cases and two deaths earlier in the year but was declared Ebola-free in August.

The patient had been ill for about a month before travelling ‌by road ‌from Congo to ⁠Uganda’s capital, Kampala, and then flying to Nairobi on Saturday, health minister Aden Duale told a news conference.

After arriving at Nairobi’s international airport, he passed through health screening and was later taken by a relative to Nairobi ⁠Hospital. He was admitted with fever, chills and bleeding beneath the skin and was quickly placed in isolation, Duale said.

He died late on Monday.

News.title: Tories promise to scrap Labour’s mansion tax
News.content:
The Tories have pledged to scrap Labour’s “mansion tax” on homes worth more than £2m.

Andrew Griffith, the shadow chancellor, pledged to abolish the “vindictive levy” in his keynote speech to the Conservative Party conference, warning it would hit people living in “ordinary homes”.

Under the tax, which was announced by Labour last year, properties valued at more than £2m face an extra levy on their council tax from 2028.

The shadow chancellor said: “They pretend it’s a mansion tax, but it will hit people here in Birmingham, in Manchester, and those living in ordinary homes making long commutes to our capital city. For many, it will be simply unaffordable.”

He pledged to follow in the footsteps of Nigel Lawson, Margaret Thatcher’s chancellor, and cut one tax at every Budget if the his party returns to power.

Elsewhere in his speech, Mr Griffith promised to scrap a net zero “grocery tax” which pushes up the cost of the weekly shop and cut the cost of a new build by £50,000.

The shadow chancellor also accused previous Tory leaders of failing to govern as free market conservatives, and said Andy Burnham and John Healey want to take Britain back to a “socialist fever dream of the 1970s”.

News.title: How worried should we be about the Russian plague lab leak?
News.content:
A fire breaks out at a laboratory in Siberia where secretive research into infectious diseases is taking place. A technician, racked with guilt over the accident, disappears into the tundra and shoots himself. Hunters discover his body, but what they don’t realise is it is infected with a manipulated version of the plague bacterium. The pathogen quickly spreads around the world, wreaking death and destruction at a scale unprecedented in human history.

This is the plot of Biological War: A Scenario, a recent book by US author Annie Jacobsen which imagines what could happen if a weaponised bacterium escaped from a laboratory.

The book describes an absolute worst-case scenario but the beginnings of this fictionalised pandemic share an eerie similarity with events in Russia over the last week. Reports have emerged about the death of a 28 year old female worker at the Antiplague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East in Shelekho, a city in Irkutsk. Rospotrebnadzor, the country’s infectious disease agency, said the woman was diagnosed with a “pneumonia of unknown origin”.

However, according to reports in Russian media the woman, identified as Daria Shipilova, died of pneumonic plague after dropping a test tube filled with live samples of the pathogen, Yersinia pestis. She was taken to hospital on Tuesday September 29 but died two days later. Nearly 200 contacts are now being monitored for signs of the disease, according to media reports.

So how worried should we be?

News.title: Extreme heat is increasing risks for pregnant women and babies, experts warn
News.content:
Soaring temperatures are increasing birth complications and defects in newborns, a new report has warned.

The report, which surveyed 1,000 doctors and midwives, found that at least 73 per cent of healthcare workers across Australia, Brazil, Britain, India and Zimbabwe had seen an uptick in heat-related complications in pregnancy and birth.

High temperatures can cause surface-level blood vessels to dilate, which in pregnant women can significantly decrease blood flow to the placenta and reduce oxygen and nutrients reaching the foetus.

This phenomenon can increase the risk of stillbirth, premature births, and low birth weight, the report, released by the Wellcome Trust, said.

Heat can also make it hard for newborn babies, whose bodies are already extremely fragile, to regulate their internal temperatures – which can significantly impact both their ability to breathe properly and feed from their mothers.

Extreme heat can also severely affect the health of a pregnant woman, placing heavy demands on the cardiovascular system and inadvertently increasing the risk of gestational diabetes, dangerously high blood pressure, and pre-eclampsia.

The effects are more severe on women who live in places where temperatures are newly or rapidly increasing, as opposed to women who have always lived in hot climates and whose bodies have acclimatised to the heat over time.

Insufferable heat can also impact women’s access to critical healthcare during pregnancy.

More than a quarter of healthcare workers surveyed by Wellcome said they had seen first-hand how fewer women travel to hospitals and clinics during heat waves, particularly in the developing world where millions access healthcare on foot.

The world experienced its hottest August on record in 2026, when the average global surface air temperature reached 16.96 degrees Celsius – roughly 1.65 degrees above pre-industrial levels.

Britain also saw its hottest summer since records began, with five heatwaves recorded over the course of just 40 days, and temperatures reaching 38 degrees in some parts of the country.

A Wellcome-funded project studying pregnant women in Wales, known as MAGENTA, has found that women in the UK have experienced negative birth outcomes as a result of the persistent heat.

Initial research has linked exposure to elevated temperatures exceeding 25 degrees with higher rates of premature births and stillbirths. A 1-degree increase in heat exposure can boost the chances of a preterm birth by around 5 per cent, the research found.

Climate change has been identified by the World Health Organization (WHO) as the greatest threat to global public health.

Between 2030 and 2050, experts project climate change will cause an additional 250,000 deaths every year.

The deaths will be due mostly to heat stress, malnutrition, and an increase in the prevalence of infectious diseases like malaria, which is spreading into new areas where mosquitoes can now more easily survive and spread disease, according to the WHO.

Dr Madeline Thomson, head of climate impacts and adaptation at Wellcome, said: “Extreme heat, fuelled by climate change, is impacting our way of life and our health - and yet many countries are not prepared. With El Niño pushing temperatures higher, the failure to act is costing lives.

“We already know many of the solutions to protect people - from early warning systems to cooler buildings.

“But the challenge is providing solutions to those who need them most, including pregnant women and newborns, who face serious risks but often receive inadequate information and support.”

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: ‘The dogs were eating their bodies’: Thousands of Yemenis flee war across the sea
News.content:
The Houthi militiamen had barely chased the government forces out of Alia Mohammad’s coastal village when the bombing began in a Saudi-backed attempt to recapture it.

Caught in the middle were Ms Mohammad, her family and their neighbours near the town of Dhubab, overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb strait, or ‘Gate of Tears’.

As the roar of planes split the sky over their heads and explosions shook their village, it took little time for them to decide what to do.

Born from generations of fishermen, they resolved to take to the sea and flee their homes in Yemen, to seek refuge across the strait in Djibouti.

More than 4,000 Yemeni refugees have arrived in the coastal Djibouti town of Obock in the past month, fleeing an offensive which has redrawn Yemen’s battle lines and strengthened Tehran’s hand in the Middle East energy crisis.

The offensive last month saw the Iranian-backed Houthi advance around 90 miles along the Red Sea coast in a 48-hour blitz that delivered what analysts have called the most consequential shift in Yemen’s front lines in years.

Sports.title: Kane sums up England legacy on special night - but can he make that final step?
Sports.content:
Some things are inevitable in life. Harry Kane delivering for England is always one of those inevitabilities. On his momentous, milestone match, he stuck to the script perfectly.

On his 125th cap, Kane did what Kane does best under the Wembley arch - stealing the show, leading the way, winning the game for England.

Everyone knew he would score in this match. It's the same feeling you get in every match. But he still gets the buzz.

"I think this is even beyond my wildest dreams," he said after the game. "To be now at 125, it's just an extreme privilege."

This match - and the three goals he contributed to England's cause on his special night - was a perfect summary of Harry Kane's England career.

The first goal saw him venture out to the right wing, highlighting Kane's ability to pop up anywhere on the pitch. Quarterback, out wide, it doesn't matter. It's classic Kane.

But his two goals were classic centre-forward strikes. Right in the heart of the penalty area, almost a throwback to the classic No 9.

Image: Harry Kane stole the show on his 125th England cap

"He's playing at a level that is unmatched," said Jude Bellingham on Kane's record-breaking night. "He's scoring goals for fun, he's dropping deep and playing passes in behind and contributing, making tackles and everything. He's only getting better."

What makes Kane's achievement even more incredible is he has reached 125 caps despite making his England debut at 21. For a generational talent in the modern game, that's somewhat rare. Bellingham, for example, was 17 when he played his first game.

Kane did not have the teenage sensation moment Wayne Rooney or Micheal Owen had. Bukayo Saka and Rio Ferdinand were also 19 on their England debuts. Declan Rice and Phil Foden were 20. Kane was the slow starter who forged his way up through the EFL and became a national hero.

And what has followed is 125 caps in 11 years. The remarkable consistency is summarised by his availability. He's always there for England.

In England's last 101 competitive matches - which spans a decade - Kane has been available for selection for all but one of them: the Nations League loss to Greece in 2024.

Every single other game, he has been able to be called upon for the Three Lions. A century of near-perfectly consistent England performances over the span of a decade.

"For sure there's times I've played through the pain", he said. "I think every player at some stage plays through the pain or niggles or some sort of injury.

"I think the last six years or so I've been extremely consistent in that sense and been available. I think availability is one of the biggest strengths you can have at this level."

Now it's important to recognise that Kane hasn't always been 100 per cent fit in those 100 matches. The Euro 2024 campaign and final spring to mind where he was clearly carrying something but playing through the pain.

Image: Kane hasn't always been at 100 per cent fitness during his 125 caps

But his predecessor at the England elite level in Rooney was riddled with injury sagas through his career - Euro 2004 and the 2006 World Cup especially.

The main image of his 2010 World Cup highlight reel was him shouting down the TV cameras to England fans, then he faded out of form in 2012, 2014 and 2016 - to the point where he was no longer the main man. Kane has shown the consistency Rooney never could.

Now Rooney, Owen and Co were part of a different generation where playing for England was not as attractive as it is now. Turning up regularly for international duty was not as common, with the 'club first culture' well-documented on many levels.

But then again, Kane's big night came on the same evening that Cristiano Ronaldo revealed his reasons for leaving the Portugal camp. Even the very best can easily turn away from the national team for any reason. Kane has never even given a glimmer of that attitude in his 11 years.

"To reach the highest level on a consistent basis you've always got to be hungry, you've always got to be striving for more," he said.

"I think sometimes players or people can reach the top and think it's time to take their foot off the gas and that's when you see players maybe fall.

"For me it's the opposite. When I'm at the top it's to do even more, find even more improvement. That's what I'm doing right now."

Kane is the exemplary player England needed for this generation - but all that remains is for him to confirm his place as the greatest player in any generation.

Is he already England's best? Quite possibly. Record appearance maker and goalscorer is hard to top and argue against. But the one thing Ronaldo, Bobby Charlton and Bobby Moore have over him is silverware at international level. "For sure I'd swap all [the caps and goals] to win something with England."

Image: Kane still needs the silverware at the top of the international game

But Kane also said: "Every player has a ceiling." What is his? Has he already reached it? "I hope not. I hope there's still more to go. I guess only time dictates that, where everyone's ceiling is.

"Right now I still feel like I've got room to improve. I just said that I've come off the back of my best season ever at 32 years old and right now I feel even in a better place."

There is still plenty for him to get. Kane is first eyeing up 100 goals at international level, joining a very elite club of strikers to manage that feat. He will surely get there.

"I try not to think about it too much," he said, with a sense of humility. "It's like being a cricketer in the 90s, the more you think about the 100, you don't know where to get there.

But in this all-time great innings - as well as the upcoming Ballon D'Or trophy, which he surely has more than half a chance for - delivering a first major international trophy since 1966 is the ultimate prize.

Kane has at least one more bite at the trophy cherry. He looks set to appear at Euro 2028 and possibly he can squeeze out one last crack at the World Cup, following this summer's disappointment.

"I'm in great shape," he said. "Some of the players I've played with went into their late 30s and are still at the highest level and are even in their 40s now. It's season by season with me.

"As long as I feel like I can help the team and be valuable for the team I'll be around. At the moment I feel like I can't help the team, I won't and that's the way I am. We'll have to see."

For now, one message stands with Kane. "Don't give yourself any regrets." He has done so much - but it's time for the last, big challenge. Win it all. Win what remains.

Sports.title: King Kane marks milestone match with star display as England beat Czech Republic
Sports.content:
Harry Kane marked his record-equalling 125th cap with a sensational display as he led England to a 3-0 win over Czech Republic at Wembley.

The England captain's century and a quarter of caps is now level with Peter Shilton's all-time record that stood for 36 years - and it was a fitting display as he was involved in every single goal on the night.

Kane set up the first - his versatility to peel off to the right wing was rewarded as his cross was comically put into his own net by Czech defender Vladimir Coufal. Wembley almost unanimously laughed at the former West Ham man as the replays were shown on screen.

Image: Vladimir Coufal's comical own goal put England in front

And Kane's moment came five minutes before half-time, as a sumptuous move involving Elliot Anderson and Morgan Rogers resulted in the latter crossing for his captain - who had all the time and space to finish.

It wouldn't be long until Kane sought to double his tally after the break. He struck the bar from distance but he eventually made it three when he headed Lewis Hall's delivery into the bottom corner at the far post.

Thomas Tuchel's England end the lengthy international break with three wins from four and 14 goals to show for it. Even though Spain beat Croatia 2-1 with a late comeback win to lead the group, England are all-but assured of a quarter-final spot anyway - needing one point from their last two games to qualify.

But this was Kane's night. No hat-trick for him as he was taken off with 10 minutes left - but he's now passed the 90-mark for international goals. He wants a century of goals to add to his appearance - and he's definitely going to get it.

Image: Harry Kane doubled the lead before half-time

The big moments from Wembley

5: CLOSE! Alexander-Arnold whips a free-kick over the Czech wall and it's tipped away by Hornicek.

27: OWN GOAL! Kane's cross is put into his own net comically by Coufal, who was under no pressure as he tried to clear.

30: OVER! Anderson misses a great chance to double England's lead but blazes over.

40: GOAL! Kane gets the goal on his big night as Anderson chips the ball over for Rogers down the right, who finds the England captain with acres of space to smash home.

54: OFF THE BAR! Kane is denied a second as his effort from the edge of the box clips the bar after great work from Myles Lewis-Skelly to start the free-flowing attack.

56: NEARLY! Rogers crosses for Bellingham whose deft flick is smartly denied by goalkeeper Hornicek.

57: GOAL! Kane heads in Hall's corner to double his tally on England's special night.

81: KANE OFF! The England captain is substituted for Dominic Calvert-Lewin, getting a standing ovation from Wembley. It won't be his last.

Kane: It's beyond my wildest dreams but it's not about me!

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After a record-equalling 125th cap in a 3-0 victory against Czech Republic, England captain Harry Kane says that achieving the milestone was beyond his wildest dreams.

England captain Harry Kane:

"It's right up there. There's so many milestones throughout my career, looking back to my England debut and how much of a dream come true that was, I think this is even beyond my wildest dreams.To be now at 125, it's just an extreme privilege.

"I love coming to every England camp, I love playing in every game and representing the country in the best way possible. Tonight was a special night.

"The most important thing was the victory and the win. It's not about me, it's about the team. To help the team achieve it with a couple of goals and a good team performance and finish the week strong, it's been a perfect night for me."

Does Tuchel think England have moved forward from the World Cup?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at Thomas Tuchel's frosty response to a reporter, over England's World Cup exit reaction earlier this year.

England head coach Thomas Tuchel:

"Yeah of course and it's what we have to do.That is our goal, to constantly improve and develop. We have these experiences together and we had a big tournament together and it was still very positive and still it's necessary to move forward and to improve, especially in sports. And this is what we're trying to do.

"We adjusted some details in our structure and we didn't compromise on the effort and the intensity and on the togetherness of the team.

"The players who were with us in the World Cup, they took care of these standards and of the culture within the team, off the pitch and on the pitch. And I think that's what you could see and you just could see the positive on a long camp is that you have time for debriefs, that you have time for meetings, you have more time for training, you spend more time together."

Tuchel's first post-World Cup camp assessed

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz at Wembley:

This is Harry Kane's night, no doubt about it. But has Thomas Tuchel earned back a few more fans after this lengthy international camp?

Fourteen goals in four games against decent opposition. Croatia, Spain and Czech Republic are major tournament regulars.

There's a bit more clarity in certain England positions. Alexander-Arnold and Hall have had very good camps - when so many questioned whether they were right for this level. When was the last time England had two fixed, natural right-backs?

Jude Bellingham looks up for it and all the headlines for him are positive again. Anderson, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Alex Scott have added depth to midfield.

And Kane keeps on doing the business. This set-up is built for him to thrive in. Are England back?

Sports.title: Who are the winners and losers of England's international break?
Sports.content:
It's been a long international break for England. But it could be a pivotal one in Thomas Tuchel's thinking.

England's four-game Nations League camp started with a defeat to Spain but ended with two wins over Czech Republic and a 7-0 demolition of Croatia.

But after countless withdrawals and changes to the squad, who is feeling more confident about their England squad status - and who is starting to look over their shoulder?

Here are the winners and losers of the latest England squad...

Winners

Anthony Gordon

Image: Anthony Gordon looks reborn after his move to Barcelona

It turns out that Anthony 'Barcelona' Gordon is a thing after all. For so long, England's left wing position was left open to debate. Nobody really claimed it as their own, even at the World Cup just gone.

Now the debate is over. That spot is Gordon's for as long as he stays fit and firing.

Three goals and one assist during this international break means the 25-year-old is at the peak of his powers. That form is even more surprising given he is yet to get off the mark for Barcelona this term.

Image: Do England have the best front four in the world?

Alex Scott

Image: Alex Scott looked the part when he started the 7-0 win over Croatia

It seems slightly odd to claim this international break a success for someone who has suffered a two-month injury during it. But Alex Scott is here to stay.

In the 7-0 win over Croatia, Scott showed he belonged at that level, playing the Declan Rice role to perfection.

His understanding with Elliot Anderson also shone through. That will be crucial for him going forward, given the pair were the midfield pivot for the most recent Euros-winning England U21 team.

It has worked for England at a major tournament before, it can work in the future. Scott's emergence has given Tuchel a real rotation option in that role.

James Trafford

Image: James Trafford was given a shock start against Spain

Tuchel's first post-World Cup team selection had one major talking point. For the first time in nearly a decade, England played a big game without Jordan Pickford in goal.

Was the decision to start James Trafford in goal against Spain the first sign of a changing of the guard in the England goal? Never before has an England goalkeeper had this big an opening to usurp Pickford.

After Trafford started the Spain and the Czech Republic games, Pickford returned to Tuchel's line-up for the last two internationals. The No 1 shirt is not Trafford's, but the fact this role is now somewhat shared is a huge plus for the Leeds 'keeper.

Lewis Hall

Do England finally have a left-back?

Part of the Three Lions' recent spike in form at left wing has a lot to do with Lewis Hall's form down that flank. After so many tournaments of inverted options and waiting for Luke Shaw to be fit again, England have a natural option on that side again.

The Newcastle defender deserved the assist for Kane's second goal against Czech Republic at Wembley. England look balanced on that side again, and if Hall can stay fit then the head coach has one less thing to worry about.

Trent Alexander-Arnold

So it turns out Trent Alexander-Arnold can play at right-back for England.

Two starts against the Czech Republic have got people talking about the much-maligned Real Madrid man in a more positive light again.

Alexander-Arnold looks back to his best, showing his creativity in Prague but the way he stretched Czech Republic at Wembley was also impressive.

He can play behind Bukayo Saka and impress. He can do the same with Morgan Rogers and also impress. Is this the camp where Alexander-Arnold's international career turned a corner?

And no, we haven't forgotten Harry Kane

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England head coach Thomas Tuchel says he can't find any more words of praise for Harry Kane, with the England captain set to equal Peter Shilton's all-time appearance record.

This wasn't a standout camp from the England captain, but it's not gone unnoticed how Harry Kane just keeps on winning in an England shirt.

That's 91 goals in 125 England caps now. He has scored in nine out of his 14 matches for England in 2026.

But delivering in every game has become normal for him now. Just give him the Ballon d'Or.

Losers

Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo

Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo were among the first players to pull out of this England squad. Their withdrawals came not even 24 hours after they played most of the 1-1 draw with Fulham.

Is there a way back for either of the Manchester United players?

Not only is their form at United under scrutiny, but others have stepped up in their absence. For Rashford, Gordon has now pulled clear of the United man in terms of the left-wing battle. And with Morgan Rogers and Eberechi Eze among Tuchel's favourites, is there still a spot in the squad for Rashford?

For Mainoo, the performance of Scott against Croatia risks putting the United midfielder further down Tuchel's pecking order.

He was already pretty low on that list after a minute-less World Cup, with the likes of James Garner and Morgan Gibbs-White putting further pressure on both he and Rashford.

You wonder if either Rashford or Mainoo regret pulling out of this England picture so swiftly.

Cole Palmer

Image: Cole Palmer has only played in two of eight England camps under Thomas Tuchel

Chelsea's Cole Palmer was another player who pulled out of this England set-up early, with load management deemed to be the reason for his withdrawal.

But this international break has proven that Palmer is no closer to breaking the attacking midfield mould that Tuchel has in Jude Bellingham and Rogers.

Bellingham scored or created four out of the seven goals for England against Croatia. He remains untouchable in this team as a world beater. Rogers also scored in that game and is another Tuchel favourite.

After getting back to some form with Chelsea, this was a perfect window for Palmer to muscle his way back in. But he seems further back than ever in Tuchel's plans.

Reece James

Image: Could Reece James lose his England spot to Trent Alexander-Arnold?

Reece James started out as England's first-choice right-back. When he was fit, he started, no questions. But has he ended up much further down the right-back pecking order now?

Alexander-Arnold's displays at right-back during this England camp have brought him back into the right-back equation. That spells trouble for James' starting hopes for England.

And after Jarell Quansah impressed against Croatia, England's right-back situation is becoming crowded. Could James be the one to make way from Alexander-Arnold's form?

Why Tuchel is both a winner and a loser from this camp

This was always going to be a sticky camp for the England head coach, who came into the Nations League campaign needing to earn trust and confidence back after those substitutions against Argentina.

Because of that, this was branded a 'lose-lose' for Tuchel. Any standout win and people will question where that performance was in the World Cup semi-final. Any defeat would have sparked more doubts about his credentials and potential at this level.

There are still concerns about Tuchel's England. His confession that England are still a "danger" to themselves while in possession of the ball echoed his controversial 'DNA' comments from the summer. The Three Lions still feel a long way off Spain's level where they are efficient in both boxes at the same time against the very best.

But the 7-0 win over Croatia - which caught everyone by surprise - has breathed fresh momentum into the Tuchel England era. That would have got the world of football talking.

There's also a bit more clarity in certain positions. England have two natural full-backs again, the left wing position is sorted. Players like Rice and Saka can be managed more with adequate replacements such as Lewis-Skelly, Scott and Rogers.

After clarity though, must come consistency. Tuchel has picked these players - they must stay there. Only that creates cohesion ahead of Euro 2028.

Are England back?

Sports.title: Ronaldo breaks silence over Portugal walkout in extraordinary statement
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has broken his silence over his Portugal walkout in a lengthy statement in which he says he is not retiring from the national team.

The 41-year-old, whose actions had raised doubts over his international future, accused Portugal's new head coach Jorge Jesus of broken promises in a near 2,000-word statement to his 679 million Instagram followers.

Addressing the uncertainty over his Portugal future, the Al Nassr forward said: "If I am physically well, playing for my club, with goals I hope, after serving the suspension that may be applied to me, I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team."

Portugal boss Jesus, who previously denied there was a rift between him and his captain, said on Sunday the door was still open for Ronaldo to return to the national team.

However, the future of Portugal's record goalscorer and appearance-maker, whose 146 goals in 234 international caps is the most of any men's player in history, is far from clear following his decision to air his grievances in public.

Ronaldo, who reveals in his statement that he wrote his international retirement letter after the World Cup, has apologised for his actions but asked the Portuguese Football Federation to punish him and spare him any leniency.

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner delivered his statement, which spanned 11 slides on Instagram, a matter of hours before his great rival Lionel Messi was due to bid farewell to international football in an emotional send-off in Argentina.

Sky Sports News has approached the Portuguese Football Federation for comment.

'The manager had broken his word to me' - Ronaldo
