Sports.title: Too nice: do Arsenal lack the grit and tenacity to end WSL title drought?
Sports.content:
Arsenal, 10 points adrift of the Women’s Super League leaders, are poised to undertake a “big review” of their season during this international break to try to determine where things have gone so horribly wrong – again – in the early stages. After their 4-2 loss at Manchester City on Sunday, it felt as if the agenda needs to include an unusual but potentially critical question: is this team nasty enough to win a WSL title?

The technical ability throughout the world-class squad Arsenal have assembled could hardly be higher but the levels of grit, resilience and tenacity need examining in a group that appears unable to match Chelsea and Manchester City when it comes to the mental aspects of a title race. Arsenal last won the WSL in 2019.

When speaking to sources close to the Arsenal players, it is common to hear of the squad being like a “family”, very supportive of each other and full of “great people”. Those admirable traits, and a general sense the club is full of nice characters, often come across when watching games or during player interviews. Arsenal have built a team of good eggs; polite, courteous and professional individuals who people would be glad to call friends. In the vast majority of scenarios in life this is, quite obviously, a good thing. But are they too nice to beat City?

It is quite hard to imagine many of the Arsenal squad raising their voices in anger. It is equally hard to recall the last time anybody at the club engaged in so-called “housery”; perhaps not since Katie McCabe’s hair pull against Chelsea in last season’s Champions League quarter-final. The irony is that McCabe is one of the senior, influential players who left this summer – in her case to join Chelsea – and McCabe, regardless of what fans might think of her, is someone Arsenal could rely on to roll up her sleeves and get stuck in, to raise her game in a hostile atmosphere and be combative.

Last term, no Arsenal players – not even McCabe – registered in Stats Perform’s list of the top 20 WSL players for percentage of duels won. Only one Arsenal player has been shown a red card in a WSL game since 2021-22. Admirable discipline, yes, but are they lacking that fire in the belly?

This season, the team appear to be without a dogged, refuse-to-lose type of character in the mould of Lucy Bronze, whose never-say-die attitude has frequently come to England’s aid in crucial moments at major tournaments; or the gritty battling spirit of Erin Cuthbert, who has helped Chelsea lift seven league titles; or – to take an Arsenal example – a leader such as Gabriel Magalhães, a rock for others to lean on during tough games.

It is possible to be successful without a Roy Keane in your squad and Arsenal do have Leah Williamson, who has led England to two European titles, so it would be wrong to imply there is no leadership in this group. Leaders can step up in different ways but recently Renée Slegers, when praising her senior players’ reactions to their disappointing draw in Paris, mentioned there had been “lots of hugs” and praised how supportive everybody had been for each other. That sounds like the sort of unified workplace culture millions would envy, but to win titles sometimes you need to fall out, yell, be angry and demand higher standards.

View image in fullscreen Only one Arsenal player has been shown a red card in a WSL game since 2021-22. Photograph: Molly Darlington/WSL/WSL Football/Getty Images

On Friday I asked Slegers whether Arsenal had enough of a nasty edge to win the league, and she replied defiantly: “I think so, and nastiness or that grittiness, that can express itself in different ways, and I think we have certain ways in which we express that and [in] which we can do that. But of course, with our performances where we haven’t been at our best, you maybe don’t see those moments as much which we can bring, but we’re convinced that we can bring that to games as well, in our way, the Arsenal way, because it’s definitely there.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

That was not evident on Sunday in the little – but important – moments, such as shortly after Arsenal had twice taken a lead they would surrender. City seemed unfazed and carried the resolve of a team who had no doubt they would win.

Part of the way that belief has been instilled into the defending champions was evidenced in a clip, released by Sky Sports, of Andrée Jeglertz’s pre-match team talk, which he concluded with the words: “The most important thing: we are Manchester City, we are playing at home and we are winning this game.” The matter-of-fact, defiant instruction was not easy to imagine hearing in this Arsenal dressing room with any real conviction right now, not from the players and not from Slegers, who has many excellent qualities as coach, and is, by all accounts, an intelligent, detail-oriented coach of whom the players are very fond.

In decades to come, all the nice characteristics this Arsenal squad demonstrate will no doubt stand them in good stead in the real world, with their friendships, but the cliche “nice guys finish last” is starting to feel increasingly appropriate for this amiable side.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi's wife Antonela joined by his mother Celia for Argentina icon's emotional farewell... two months on from father's tragic death
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi's family gathered at Estadio Monumental for the final game of his international career on Tuesday night.

The 39-year-old's wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, was joined by their children and Messi's mother, Celia María Cuccittini, for the friendly against Benin.

They wore Messi jerseys and were seen filming and clapping as the No 10 emerged for warm-ups before being introduced to the 85,000-strong crowd in Buenos Aires. Messi's three sons - Thiago, Mateo and Ciro - then accompanied him as he walked out of the tunnel for before kickoff.

The Argentina icon will bring the curtain down on his international career after 21 years, 125 goals, two Copa America titles and a World Cup victory.

In Messi's 208th Argentina appearance, Lionel Scaloni's team face West African minnows Benin but the otherwise-unremarkable friendly has become a seismic moment for Argentine soccer.

The game also comes almost two months to the day since Messi's father, Jorge, died at the age of 68.

Lionel Messi's wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, is in Buenos Aires for his final game for Argentina

She was joined by Messi's mother, Celia María Cuccittini, for the friendly against Benin

Messi's three sons - Thiago, Mateo and Ciro - joined him as he walked out of the tunnel

Messi's father Jorge, pictured at the 2022 World Cup final, died in August at the age of 68

Back on August 7, Jorge Messi reportedly died in a hospital in Rosario, close to the family home, a couple of months after the family revealed he had been rushed to hospital with an ongoing 'health situation'.

Jorge Messi served as his son's agent and business manager, and following his death, the 39-year-old admitted he was unsure how much longer his career would last.

'All I ever did was play football, and now I have a fair few doubts as to whether I'll carry on doing it for much longer,' Messi said.

'You were by my side from the start, we were so close to the end (of his career). Why didn't you hang on just that little bit longer so we could finish it together?'

He added: 'Dad, I still can't believe you're gone. I can't get my head round it — or rather, I don't want to. It's so hard for me to imagine that I won't see you ever again, that we won't talk anymore. I know you were suffering and that this is for the best, but you left us far too soon. We still had so much left to enjoy together.

'You kept asking me to play in the last World Cup, and it was just days before it started that you took a turn for the worse.

'It was the first time you weren't going to be at a tournament, but Mum kept telling me you'd get better and that you'd be well enough to travel. I'd tell you that we'd make it to the final so you could travel.

'Every time a match ended, I'd wait for your message and miss it. That's when I realised the situation was really bad.'

Fans poured on to the streets of Buenos Aires ahead of Messi's final ever game for his country

The friendly was played at Estadio Monumental, the 85,000-seater home of River Plate

Fireworks exploded in the skies above the capital of Argentina ahead of kickoff on Tuesday

Following Tuesday night's swansong, Messi will continue to play for Inter Miami in Major League Soccer but on August 31, he announced he would be retiring from international football.

That decision came just weeks after the World Cup final at MetLife Stadium near New York, where Spain beat Argentina and Messi's World Cup journey ended in tears.

On Tuesday in Buenos Aires, fans let off flares and carried giant banners in honor of their retiring hero, while others showed off Messi tattoos or painted images of the 39-year-old on their face.

In Messi's hometown, Rosario, a giant jersey carrying his No 10 was flown by helicopter.

The Argentine soccer federation has turned Tuesday's game - Messi's 208th for his country - into a national homage dubbed 'the last tango.'

Around 85,000 tickets to Buenos Aires' largest stadium sold out in 90 minutes, while members of Argentina's 2022 World Cup-winning squad and their families were invited back to join the tribute.

Four years ago, Messi led Argentina to victory in Qatar, securing the country's third World Cup triumph and landing the one trophy that had eluded him for so long.

Sports.title: Argentina fans display 'Malvinas' banner laying claim to the Falkland Islands in the stands at Lionel Messi's emotional farewell match
Sports.content:
Argentina fans displayed multiple 'Malvinas' banners in Lionel Messi's farewell match, laying claim to the Falkland Islands.

In an emotionally charged atmosphere at 85,000-capacity Estadio Monumental, the biggest stadium in South America, some supporters took their chance to send a political message.

One banner read: 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas,' while another showed the outline of the Falkland Islands coloured in with the blue and white of the Argentina flag.

Plenty of fans brought plastic Messi masks but even though everyone was there to celebrate arguably the greatest footballer of all time, some still chose to put the controversial topic front and centre.

The contention around the banner follows Argentina's World Cup semi-final victory over England at the FIFA World Cup and fans of their rugby team holding up similar regalia during a match against South Africa in August.

After the World Cup semi-final triumph, Argentina's players used it as an opportunity to assert their claim over the Falklands, the self-governing British Overseas Territory in the South Atlantic Ocean located around 300 miles east of Argentina.

Some fans hung banners claiming that the Falklands Islands belong to Argentina

Argentina supporters hung one image of the Falklands decorated in the national colours

Britain has ruled the Falklands since January 1833 and in 2013 in a referendum, 99.8 per cent of citizens voted to remain as a British territory. The islands were the subject of a conflict between the two nations in 1982.

The lifting of the original banner – which also read 'Los Malvinas son Argentinas' – triggered a fierce backlash in the UK.

Former Prime Minister Keir Starmer insisted that while 'the World Cup might not be ours, the Falkland Islands definitely are. Self-determination rests with the islanders and our commitment to the Falklands will never waver.'

FIFA subsequently opened an investigation, with the governing body's rules forbidding the use of any political messaging at the World Cup.

They had, however, previously turned a blind eye to continued references to the 1982 conflict in a song sung by the players – and posted on social media by the country’s association – in the dressing room throughout the tournament.

Argentina President Javier Milei described the players' celebration with the banner as 'perfectly valid', and said the message 'reflects a sentiment shared by all Argentines'.

'I know that for Argentinians, we won the World Cup the moment we beat England because that's really what everyone wanted,' he said.

The banner at the rugby game came after the Pumas tried to mock England by wearing a kit paying homage to Diego Maradona's World Cup win in 1986, en route to which he scored the infamous 'Hand of God' goal against the Three Lions.

It came after their footballers did similar after beating England in the World Cup semi-final

Argentina rugby fans held up a 'Malvinas' banner laying claim to the Falkland Islands

Fans snapped up tickets to pay tribute to Messi at his final international match

The British governance of the Falklands remains a sore point for many Argentinians and continues to rear its head during sporting clashes.

Argentina's farewell to Messi against Benin was a chance for the nation to say goodbye to their beloved football icon.

He called time on his international career after his side fell short against Spain in the World Cup final this summer.

The farewell fixture is his 208th and last appearance and tickets sold out in 90 minutes. Elsewhere in the country, a giant replica of his No10 shirt, emblazoned with the word 'Gracias' was unfurled in his home city of Rosario.

And in Patagonia, an 85ft, 70-ton statue of him kneeling with the World Cup trophy looms over motorists, with adulation for the former Barcelona superstar reaching new heights.

Sports.title: 'We're not going to mark Messi, we're just going to enjoy the match': Benin star admits team will roll out the red carpet for Argentina legend ahead of emotional swansong in Buenos Aires
Sports.content:
The man tasked with defending against Lionel Messi for his final match with Argentina has admitted he has no plan to mark the icon.

Argentina are hosting Benin at midnight UK time in Buenos Aires in what is a slightly bizarre swansong for the 2022 World Cup winner.

The South Americans scheduled low-budget friendlies against Bolivia, Burkina Faso, and Benin for the international break, but have refrained from playing Messi so he is fit for his historic farewell against the latter.

An Argentinian TV channel called C5N tracked down members of the Benin squad walking around the capital city, and centre-back Tijani Mohamed said: 'You don't mark Messi. We are just going to enjoy this match.

'I'm going to look at him like this: "Messi, you are God".

'Yes, yes I've watched the matches and that's it, a match with Messi and for me he's the best in the world, as I'm telling you.

A Benin defender says there is no plan to mark Lionel Messi in his final game for Argentina

The legendary forward is preparing for a farewell match in front of 85,000 fans in Buenos Aires

'Spain was a very tough team to play against, but I wanted Argentina to win because I really like Messi.

'Benin is a very, very good team to play with, and I can't talk about Benin right now because we have to enjoy this match, and we're going to give everything so that this celebration goes really well.'

The team's doctor chimed in: 'He's the best in the world!'

Messi has played 207 times for Argentina, scoring 125 goals and winning the World Cup alongside two Copa Americas.

The 39-year-old announced his intention to retire in August, but he had made the decision just two days after losing to Spain in the World Cup final weeks before.

'It was a decision that hurt, and still hurts, to my core, but I understand that it's the right time,' he wrote on Instagram.

'I swear that I always gave my all, not just in the last few years when we won everything, but before that too. I always fought and gave everything for this jersey, to bring you joy and make you proud to be Argentinian through football.'

More than 85,000 fans are set to attend Messi's goodbye at the Estadio Mas Monumental, where members of their 2022 World Cup-winning squad will pay tribute.

But the build-up to the clash with Benin has been marred by controversy.

Messi's penultimate match against Burkina Faso had to be played against the nation's under-23s.

The first team's charter flight from Morocco – paid for by Argentina – was cancelled and the players then refused to travel over financial compensation concerns and extreme fatigue. Argentina hammered the unsuspecting youth 7-0.

Now Benin arrive on the back of a 23-hour flight during which their video analyst Jonas Bide reportedly blacked out.

They got into their hotel only to find there is no hot water, while the artificial turf and gym were deemed too low-standard for a professional team.

Sports.title: Chelsea star Moises Caicedo is hit with eight-point penalty and fine for driving £160k Audi supercar without valid licence or insurance
Sports.content:
Chelsea star Moises Caicedo has been given an eight-point penalty and hit with a fine for driving his £160,000 Audi RSQ8 without a valid licence or insurance.

Caicedo, who is understood to earn £250,000-a-week having signed from Brighton for £115million in 2023, was pulled over in April 2025.

He was caught near Chelsea's Cobham training ground in Surrey and appeared at Crawley magistrates' court this week.

In addition to the eight points, the fine came to £1,444 and he is now nearing a driving ban. Drivers who receive 12 points in three years are not allowed behind the wheel for six months. People with international driving licences can use them in Britain for 12 months.

The Ecuadorian has been ordered to obtain the valid licence and insurance for his supercar, which can reach 155mph and hit 60mph in just 3.8 seconds.

At the time the car was seized, Chelsea dismissed it as a 'personal matter'.

Moises Caicedo was given an eight-point penalty and fine for driving without a valid licence or insurance

The Audi RSQ8 (pictured on display in Mumbai in February) is valued at around £160,000

Driving incidents among Premier League stars have been in the headlines in recent weeks, with two Hull City players flipping their cars in the same spot.

Daily Mail Sport's Lewis Steele even visited – and drove – the dangerous spot this week.

The 24-year-old, who is no longer the most expensive footballer in British transfer history, has been injured this season and only played 14 minutes for Xabi Alonso's side.

Chelsea have missed the 65-cap international, who is one of the first names on the team sheet when fit.

The midfielder was not called up by Ecuador for games against South Korea, Japan and Panama in an effort to help him fully shake off the persistent calf issue that has been dogging him.

Alonso suggested before the international break that Caicedo is not far from a return to action and he could be involved in some capacity when the Blues face Bournemouth

Sports.title: Harry Kane is England's 'best player EVER', insists Jude Bellingham after Three Lions captain's historic night
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham hailed Harry Kane as England's greatest-ever player after he marked his record-equalling 125th cap with a Wembley double, describing the striker as 'unmatched' worldwide.

After Kane's cross forced an own goal out of Czech Republic defender Vladimir Coufal, the 33-year-old made this a night to remember by scoring twice. Remarkably, this was the 18th time that the Three Lions talisman has netted two or more goals in an England game.

'We're running out of superlatives,' Bellingham said of Kane, who drew level with Peter Shilton on 125 caps. 'He is the best England player that has ever worn the shirt and it is an honour to play with him. He is playing at a level which is pretty unmatched when you look across the world.

'He is scoring goals for fun. He is still dropping in deep and delivering those passes in behind and wide and contributing in so many areas of the pitch and getting back as well with tackles.

'And he is only getting better.'

Kane himself described his 125 caps as 'beyond my wildest dreams' and now that he is on 91 goals for England, he does not feel he has reached his ceiling as he chases his century.

Jude Bellingham (left) has hailed Harry Kane (right) as England's greatest ever player

'I hope not,' Kane said. 'I hope there's still more to go. I guess only time dictates that. I still feel like I've got room to improve. I've just come back off my best season ever at 32 years old and right now I feel in an even better place. I'm not going to stop. I'm going to keep pushing and see where it takes me. Maybe in 10 years or so, we'll see where that ceiling is at.'

On whether 100 England goals is his next target, Kane added: 'I got asked this question by a few of the staff before the game – what would mean more between the 125 (caps) and 100 goals.

'Obviously I'm getting closer to the 100 now. I'm in the nineties. I try not to think about it too much. It's like being a cricketer in the nineties – the more you think about the 100, you don't always get there. I'm just going with the flow right now. I'm coming off the back of my best season ever. I'm just pushing myself and seeing how far I can get.'

Kane did concede he would swap his personal achievements for a major trophy with his country. 'For sure,' he said immediately. 'Without a doubt. I'd swap all that to win something with England.'

Thomas Tuchel said of Kane: 'Brilliant. He deserves this stage. He deserves the praise.'

At 33 years old, Kane also became the oldest player to score a back-to-back brace in competitive fixtures for England. This victory over the Czech Republic ended the three-week international break. Tuchel's side also beat Croatia 7-0 in Rijeka, the Czechs 2-0 in Prague, and lost 3-2 to Spain at Wembley with Kane scoring at least once in every game.

Sports.title: Scotland 1-2 Slovenia: Pocognoli's honeymoon ends as Scotland suffer damaging defeat
Sports.content:
The elongated international break is plainly not to everyone’s liking, but there are some for whom the new arrangement offers no grounds for complaint.

Newly appointed as Scotland manager, Sebastien Pocognoli has spoken positively of the opportunity to get his ideas across in the fortnight since his new-look squad travelled to La Manga.

With four Nations League games in which to assess the fruits of those labours, the Tartan Army will also have welcomed the chance to examine the wide shot of the Belgian’s impact.

With two-thirds of the campaign ticked off, it’s fair to say that the jury remains out on the amiable Belgian and what he’s trying to do. Progress, it must be said, has been painfully slow.

Pocognoli’s side didn’t deserve anything from this rematch against Slovenia and remain third in Group E.

Beating North Macedonia at Hampden next month was always taken as a given. To stand any chance of finishing in the runners-up spot in the section, Scotland will also now need to beat Switzerland in St Gallen three days later. That’s going to be an extremely tall order. And even that is unlikely to be enough.

The implications of failing to finish second in the section would be considerable: Not only would Scotland miss out on a play-off in March for a possible return to the top tier, they would slip from pot two to pot three for the Euro 2028 draw in December.

Notwithstanding the fact that this is a new manager and new-look squad trying to play in a different style, results are what anyone is always judged on. And four points from a possible 12 falls way short of expectations. Already, the manager has an awful lot of ground to make up to vindicate his appointment.

Two home games and not a point taken. If there was a degree of mitigation about the manner of the loss to the Swiss, then there was nothing to be said here.

Bowie and Robertson look stunned after Scots surrender a half-time lead to lose to Slovenia

Scotland were ahead at the interval through Ryan Christie – somewhat fortuitously – and simply didn’t turn up for the second period.

Just as alarming as the manner in which Slovenia struck twice was the way in which Scotland lost their composure. They turned the ball over time and again and looked weary and lacking in ideas.

While it would be patently ludicrous for anyone to press a panic button, Pocognoli has a lot to ponder in the coming weeks.

Although Slovenia are evidently a nation with greater pedigree than North Macedonia, this was a game Scotland had to win.

A week after his Hampden bow against the Swiss proved to be a damp squib as a result of Jack Hendry’s early red card, Pocognoli sought to build on an improved display in Skopje.

Hendry returned and filled the central role in the back-three caused by Scott McKenna’s suspension. Billy Gilmour earned his 50th cap alongside Lewis Ferguson with John McGinn and Christie tasked with providing the support for Oli McBurnie.

Seeking his first goal on his 20th Scotland appearance, the Hull forward was something of a surprise inclusion ahead of Kieron Bowie. Bluntly, he did not justify being given the nod as his 1,000th minute in a Scotland shirt came and went without a goal.

Ben Gannon-Doak retained his spot at right wing-back. Before getting down to business on the other flank, Andy Robertson’s century of caps was fittingly recognised by a presentation from Gordon Strachan, Alex McLeish, Steve Clarke and Pocognoli.

Danijel Sturm evades Jack Hendry's challenge to score the winner for Slovenia

Scotland actually looked like they might pick up where they left off in Ljubljana. Robertson pinged the ball to Christie who fed McGinn. His hopes of a breakthrough were dashed by an outstretched leg.

One thing we do know already from Pocognoli is that it’s unlikely to be dull. Going man for man at the back, they go forward in numbers but invite risk.

When Daniel Sturm ran in behind and cut the ball back, Scotland were short on numbers. Hendry did well to spread himself on the line and prevent Adam Cerin from scoring.

After another Scotland attack broke down, Gannon-Doak had to show his worth defensively to take the ball off the toe of Sturm.

Scotland were struggling to get control of the game at the midway point in the first half. It needed someone special to find the spark. Step forward Gannon-Doak.

His run inside was met with a crude a tackle by Erik Janza which earned a booking. But the set piece the wing-back earned would provide a double punishment.

In a clearly rehearsed routine, Ferguson rolled the ball to Gannon-Doak and watched him make for the line and stand the ball up at the far post. Hendry met it firmly, struck the post and took Jan Oblak out of the game. McBurnie looked certain to break his international duck but fluffed his lines from three yards.

Christie took one touch to retrieve the situation then converted with a backheel. Without exactly being exhilarating to watch, Scotland were ahead.

What a debt they owed to Robertson for keeping it that way at the interval. His block to deny Zan Vipotnik was incredible.

Pocognoli could have done with seeing his players move the ball a shade quicker. There was a clear attempt to introduce greater tempo at the outset of the second period.

A lovely flick by Gilmour found McGinn who sent Gannon-Doak on his way. The winger bobbed and weaved, thought about going himself then played in Christie who saw his left-foot strike fisted away by the keeper.

But the increased sense of urgency did not last. The manner of Slovenia’s equaliser was dreadful from Scotland’s perspective.

It stemmed from a throw-in which Robertson launched towards Christie and was mis-controlled by the goalscorer. Slovenia pounced on the unforced error with Sturm playing a straight pass up the middle to Aljosa Matko. With Luis Binks unable to get his shoulder in, Matko placed the ball in the corner from just outside the box.

As with two of the concessions against the Swiss, Angus Gunn could have done better.

For a few minutes, Scotland were overrun and repeatedly undone by a ball over the top. First, Sturm fired over with the goal at his mercy. Then Binks had to stand up tall to prevent Mark Zabukovnik from lashing home the visitors’ second. It was in danger of becoming a tough watch.

Pocognoli reacted by withdrawing Stephen Welsh and McBurnie and introducing Aaron Hickey and Bowie in a revised 4-1-4-1 formation.

While the offside flag came to the rescue after Cerin had netted, there was a growing sense of foreboding among the home supporters.

Oli McBurnie challenges Slovenia defender Erik Janza at Hampden

The visitors’ second felt like a matter of time. It arrived on 71 minutes with the space vacated by the advanced Robertson exploited. Matko dragged Binks out of position and delivered a measured cross. Sturm met it first time. This time Gunn was blameless.

The further introductions of Findlay Curtis and Josh McPake – for his debut – lifted the crowd but not the performance. Although both subs had claims for penalties, Scotland lost their way with elementary errors creeping in all over the park.

Bowie’s shot on the turn following fine wing play from McPake at least worked Oblak, but it was the one real moment of promise in a grim closing period. This is not how it was meant to be.

Sports.title: England look like the powerfully dangerous team Thomas Tuchel wants them to be - this kind of energetic, intelligent and versatile football can offer a route to Euro 2028 glory, writes IAN LADYMAN
Sports.content:
England look like the powerfully dangerous team Thomas Tuchel wants them to be - this kind of energetic, intelligent and versatile football can offer a route to Euro 2028 glory, writes IAN LADYMAN

Thomas Tuchel began this extended international break saying he wasn’t a fan. Too long, he said. It is unlikely the England manager feels that way now.

England have grown stronger and better and more convincing with each passing game. An 11-day spell that began with an error-strewn defeat to Spain has ended with England starting to look like the powerfully dangerous team Tuchel wanted them to be when he took the job two years ago.

A fortnight ago, as England’s players gathered at St George's Park, we badgered Tuchel about his team’s style of play.

What exactly was it? Did he know? Could it work?

At times, his answers were a little tongue-tied. He talked of embracing chaos. It wasn’t convincing. Slowly, though, his players have spoken for their manager. There has been no chaos, only progress.

England have motored through their last three games – admittedly against modest opposition – scoring 12 unanswered goals and playing the kind of energetic, intelligent and versatile football that may yet offer them a route to real glory in the home Euros of 2028.

Record-breaker Harry Kane scored twice for England against Czech Republic, who have progressed since the World Cup

Thomas Tuchel's side won 3-0 at Wembley in their final game of the three-week long international break

Front and centre has been captain Harry Kane. The 33-year-old made his record-equalling 125th England appearance here and scored his 90th and 91st goals. Of course he did. Kane continues to set extraordinary standards.

Jude Bellingham was magnificent once again and is now having the kind of influence on team-mates that simply can’t be bought. Bellingham is developing into a truly elite footballer. For England’s best player, there currently appears to be no horizon and, crucially for England, he is now dragging others along with him. It has been quite a turnaround for a player who was not selected for his country just 11 months ago.

With Trent Alexander-Arnold affecting this game like he once did for Liverpool, the Czech Republic couldn’t cope. England carried threat from all angles and all areas. It was lovely to watch. A proper team.

An own goal from Vladimir Coufal helped them along and by the time we had reached the hour England were three to the good thanks to two Kane goals. Unexpectedly, there were to be no more.

Tuchel craves consistency with this England team. He has seen some of that in two defeats of the Czechs and the pounding of Croatia sandwiched in between.

In terms of his selection, it was a little harder here. The three-day turnaround from the weekend forced his hand. He felt compelled to relieve Anthony Gordon and Bukayo Saka and that gave Morgan Rogers and Eberechi Eze opportunity.

Alexander-Arnold’s selection and performance was also pivotal to a first half England performance in particular that bristled with energy and intent.

Tuchel had been impressed with the Czech performance in losing to Spain on Saturday and had anticipated challenges here.

England are starting to flow - Kane scored a fine third goal following great play from his team

Former West Ham defender Vladimir Coufal (left) had a hard night and scored an own goal

But so dominant were his team that the visitors were never allowed to get going. England suffocated them in midfield with the intensity of their football and their hustle and the key play of the opening 45 minutes was clear.

Win the ball in central areas and switch it quickly to the right, most often to Alexander-Arnold. The Real Madrid full-back had 30 touches in the first half an hour and the majority of them were deep in the Czech half.

England didn’t actually score until the 28th minute but it was always coming. Alexander-Arnold’s early free-kick was touched round the post while there were other close calls.

Rogers – also on that right side – was a persistent threat while Elliot Anderson’s passing range was exemplary. Occasionally England over-played and their finishing was not as sharp as it may have been but eventually the Czechs put the ball in for them.

The move flowed down the right, of course, and this time it was Kane who drifted wide to cross low.

Eze had actually stopped running by the time Coufal smashed it past his own goalkeeper under no pressure from six yards. It was strange. But all we can perhaps offer the West Ham defender by way of mitigation is that England’s football had by that time placed his team under such stress that mistakes were becoming inevitable.

Once ahead, England sensed opportunity the way good teams do. Two minutes later a sublime move involving Anderson, Alexander-Arnold and Rogers ended with Anderson appearing on the end of it to shoot over. Then, five minutes before half-time, England scored a goal of truly beautiful simplicity.

Another searching ball from Anderson landed on Rogers’ instep and his first time cross found Kane unmarked. The finish was as clinically straightforward as we would expect. That, in a single movement, was how Tuchel wishes this team to play and shortly after striking the bar from distance, Kane rose highest to meet a 57th minute corner and headed a third England goal down into the net at the near post.

The Three Lions are playing in a way that could offer them a real shot at glory at Euro 2028

Tuchel loves his set piece goals and that would have pleased him. England, though, were in the mood to entertain. The days of the Wembley paper aeroplanes and the Mexican waves seem to be behind us, for now at least.

There was, perhaps inevitably, a slight drop in intensity as the game wore on and Tuchel’s substitutions arrived.

It was hard not to feel some sympathy for Dominic Calvert-Lewin who has been in the form of his life at Leeds but had previously been afforded only seven minutes against Spain during this whole period.

Does Kane really need another hat-trick so badly that he cannot be sacrificed with the team leading 3-0?

Tuchel perhaps feels he has earned the right to make those decisions and his captain was hunting a third right until he was eventually replaced by Calvert-Lewin with ten minutes left.

England were not to score again and Wembley felt a little flat by comparison towards the end. Disappointed even.

That in itself shows just how far a team has come in such a short time. The next significant test is Spain in Madrid next month. England, at the very least, should travel in hope.

Sports.title: Liverpool star Milos Kerkez listed as an 'enemy of Ukraine': Hungary's foreign minister is forced to step in after defender and his father are accused of 'supporting Russia's aggression'
Sports.content:
Liverpool star Milos Kerkez listed as an 'enemy of Ukraine': Hungary's foreign minister is forced to step in after defender and his father are accused of 'supporting Russia's aggression'

Milos Kerkez is at the heart of a political storm after being included in a list of 'enemies of Ukraine' alongside his father.

It comes following an incident involving the Hungary defender and Ukraine during their first Nations League encounter in this current international break.

Ukraine won 1-0 in Budapest on September 25 in a match that did have some feisty encounters.

One moment saw Kerkez's Hungary, and Liverpool, team-mate Dominik Szoboszlai involved in a scuffle with Ukraine's Victor Tsygankov.

As those two made their feelings known, Kerkez ran over and promptly grabbed Tsygankov by the collar.

In defence of his son, Kerkez's father Sebastijan - who is of Serbian descent - is reported to have uploaded a picture of the incident to his Instagram story with the song Russian Paradise by rapper AK-47 accompanying it. Some have interpreted that to be a reference to ongoing conflict in Ukraine.

Hungary defender Milos Kerkez (centre left) is in a list of 'enemies of Ukraine' after this incident with Victor Tsygankov (right) during a UEFA Nations League encounter last month

Kerkez rabbed Tsygankov by the collar after the latter confronted Dominik Szoboszlai

As a result, both Kerkezes are believed to be included on Myrotvorets, a database of 'enemies of Ukraine' which includes pictures and details on the individuals included.

It must be noted though that the list, which also includes Hungarian MP Balazs Hidveghi, is not run by or affiliated with the Ukrainian government.

The incident though has turned the sporting matter into a political one, with the Hungarian deputy prime minister and minister of foreign affairs Anita Orban stepping in and condemning 'possible threats' aimed at the left back.

She wrote on social media: 'I strongly condemn the stigmatisation, any form of blacklisting, and any potential threats directed at Hungarian citizens Milos Kerkez and Balazs Hidveghi.

'Throughout the weekend, alongside the government meeting, I was in constant consultation with Ukrainian government representatives, the Hungarian Football Federation (MLSZ), the embassy, ​​and my colleagues to ensure that all parties involved took action within their respective spheres to resolve the situation.

'Sport should be about performance, community, and respect. I thank the two national associations for their cooperation.'

Kerkez missed the reverse fixture on Monday night, which Hungary won 2-1, due to suspension, but downplayed any ill-feeling to his opponents after September's scuffle.

'Personally, I have never supported and I do not support any aggression in my life,' he told Hungarian outlet Telex. 'I am not a person who considers anything that harms others acceptable.

'At the same time, there is always tension in a football match, and in the match against Ukraine, all I did was defend our captain, my friend, and I would have done this even if any other country had been our opponent.'

Sports.title: Harry Kane moment at Wembley speaks volumes as England captain marks historic night
Sports.content:
Harry Kane moment at Wembley speaks volumes as England captain marks historic night

ENGLAND 3-0 CZECHIA: Harry Kane equalled the all-time caps record for England with his 125th appearance, and he marked the occasion by notching two goals in a comfortable victory

View 2 Images Harry Kane scored twice as he made history (Image: Eddie Keogh - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

These days Harry Kane often has to put up with second billing behind Jude Bellingham in the popularity stakes with England fans. The Wembley crowd gave Bellingham’s name a huge cheer when it was read out before kick-off - but this time Kane got an even louder reception.

‌



‌



They had come to pay homage to an England great who loves pulling on the shirt, representing his country and takes such pride in being captain. Incredibly, it was 4,211 days - March 27, 2015 - since Kane made his debut against Lithuania.

‌



Of course he scored that night - just 79 seconds after coming on as a substitute - and has been doing so ever since. This night was always going to belong to Kane because, quite understandably, he made it all about himself. That has been the story of his England career.

‌



Kane is 33 but as hungry as ever and he just leads by example. When the team needs a lift, he provides it. When they need a goal, he is always on hand.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Captain Marvel Kane is England’s greatest-ever goalscorer and he was determined to enjoy his big night which also as good as clinched qualification for the Nations League knockout stages next March. The top two qualify and the Groups are decided on points, then head-to-head and it would be hard to see Croatia bettering England’s 7-0 score line in Rijeka last weekend.

It was also going to be impossible to emulate that result and the early stages felt like a bit after the Lord Mayor’s show. There were four changes - Trent Alexander-Arnold, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Morgan Rogers and Eberechi Eze - to the starting line-up and it felt a bit disjointed.

Alexander-Arnold went close with a free kick and Rogers tried to tee-up Kane when he should have gone for goal himself. But that is when Kane came into his own as he changed the game. The breakthrough came after 27 minutes. Kane put over a cross from the right and, inexplicably, Czech captain Vladimir Coufal slid in and smashed the ball into his own net.

‌



Will England win the Nations League? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Harry Kane has six goals in four Nations League matches (Image: Robin Jones/Getty Images)

What a bizarre goal. It was a striker’s finish from close range rather than a defender’s clearance. Surely Kane deserved an assist.

‌



But we should have known. Kane marked his big night with a goal. Of course he did. Rogers - who really grew into the game - did well down the right, sent over a low cross and there was Kane galloping in to steer home.

That took him to 90 goals. And his 91st came soon enough. Kane skimmed the crossbar with an effort after find work by Myles Lewis-Skelly. But Czech Republic’s defence was on a warning. Lewis Hall sent over a deep corner and there was Kane lurking at the back post to head home.

What a way to finish his night. Two goals, played a part in the other and Kane’s record-equalling night will live long in the memory for another milestone and an unforgettable performance. No wonder he went off to a standing ovation when he was eventually substitute with his job done well and truly done.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel has finally found the answer to two England dilemmas after near-perfect break
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel has finally found the answer to two England dilemmas after near-perfect break

OPINION: Thomas Tuchel's side eased to a comfortable 3-0 victory over the Czech Republic at Wembley, and the win provided the England manager answers to two problems

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel might have found some new England undroppables (Image: Getty Images)

If you wanted a reminder of the folly of reading too much into UEFA Nations League football, it came when Harry Kane sent over a routine cross to no-one in particular during the first half of a relatively enjoyable game against the Czech Republic.

‌



‌



Perhaps as a gesture of respect for the England captain’s record-equalling cap, Vladimir Coufal smashed it past his own goalkeeper with absurd gusto.

‌



It was bizarre. For the most part, these Nations League games are competitive but they can also be knockabout.

‌



There was an element of knockabout in this latest England victory but Thomas Tuchel will still consider the four-game series - two victories over the Czech Republic sandwiching a hammering of Croatia after the opening defeat to Spain - to be reasonably instructive.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Of course, he did not need three wins on the spin against under-performing opposition to tell him that Jude Bellingham is frighteningly good, a supreme footballer and athlete. He did not need a hat-trick of bloodless successes to tell him that Kane remains untouchable and peerless in front of goal.

He probably did not need the win treble to tell him Elliot Anderson is the best option in that midfield position, even when he has a club crisis on his mind.

But he might have needed one or two of these past four games to convince himself that Trent Alexander-Arnold and Lewis Hall could be the full-back future of this England team.

‌



Look, you still have to wonder about Tuchel’s faith in Alexander-Arnold. Jarell Qaunsah was preferred to the Real Madrid player for the games against Spain and Croatia.

View 2 Images Trent Alexander-Arnold and Lewis Hall have forced themselves into Thomas Tuchel's England thinking (Image: Getty Images)

And in both contests against the Czechs, Alexander-Arnold had precious little in the way of defensive obligations to fulfil. But it was not his fault that all he could do was showcase his ball-striking, his attacking adventure and his eye for a show-stopping pass.

‌



That is what he did to an extent that should have eased Tuchel’s doubts. And with Hall at left-back, England had a natural balance.

Tuchel did not take either Hall or Alexander-Arnold to the World Cup. Even without hindsight, that was an odd decision. There is surely little chance of the pair being frozen out again.

Hall was making his third England start in succession and was pretty much immaculate. He is such a tidy player.

‌



His assist for Kane’s second goal of the night was fairly standard - a routine corner-kick that should have been dealt with before it reached the skipper’s head - but having Hall delivering with his left and Alexander-Arnold with his right is a nice blend for Tuchel to have.

Again, this was a match - and these are matches - that come with a caveat when it comes to making meaningful judgements. And considering neither featured in the loss to Spain, it would be interesting to see the two line up for England in Madrid next month.

But in this unusual international break, they have done their causes no harm at all. Maybe Tuchel will finally trust them.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo says he must be PUNISHED for Portugal walkout and issues two apologies
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo says he must be PUNISHED for Portugal walkout and issues two apologies

Cristiano Ronaldo has issued a lengthy statement in the aftermath of his decision to walk out on the Portuguese national side, and he's claimed that he should feel the consequences of his actions

View 2 Images Cristiano Ronaldo has acknowledged his mistakes (Image: Getty Images)

Cristiano Ronaldo has claimed that he should be punished for his Portugal walkout, having issued a grovelling apology to fans and team-mates. The veteran forward turned his back on the national team last week after perceived broken promises by boss Jorge Jesus over his playing time.

‌



‌



Ronaldo explained his perspective on things with a lengthy statement on Tuesday night. And within it, he issued an apology to supporters of the country for not acknowledging fans following a clash with Norway.

‌



Instead, he walked straight down the tunnel. But Ronaldo has now claimed he was in the wrong. Ronaldo said: “At the end of the match I only wanted everything to finish with the victory and to be alone. I did not go to greet the fans.

‌



"A failing that is solely my responsibility and that should not have happened. I apologise to the Portuguese who supported us intensely there, I apologise to the fans, and I apologise to those who, without being Portuguese, may have travelled there to see me and whom I may have disappointed."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Meanwhile, Ronaldo has also apologised to his Portuguese teammates - and suggested that his action of walking out should see him met with consequences.

Ronaldo's statement added: "I also owe an apology to my national team teammates for having left the camp. Despite the absolute breach of trust in the coach’s word, as those who witnessed these conversations can attest, I should not have done it.

"The responsibility is exclusively mine. I apologise to the Portuguese people once again, but the breaking of one’s word has, for me, a defining impact. I felt that, from that point on, my remaining would only harm the working group, and I did what I have always said I would do if I did not feel useful: I packed my bags and left.

‌



View 2 Images Ronaldo's complaints centre around a row with boss Jorge Jesus (Image: Getty Images)

"The consequence of this act of mine must be assessed and punished by the Portuguese Football Federation. I understand that the punishment should have no mitigating factors. I am not just any player; I am team captain, and that constitutes an aggravating factor.

"I have already apologised, but I know that attitudes must have consequences. Anyone who is in football as I am knows that, regardless of each person’s status, the rules are the same for everyone.

Sports.title: Roy Keane and Ian Wright forced to rush off screen before England clash
Sports.content:
Roy Keane and Ian Wright forced to rush off screen before England clash

ITV pundits Roy Keane and Ian Wright were previewing England's clash with Czechia in the Nations League alongside presenter Mark Pougatch and took a soaking thanks to Wembley's sprinklers

View 2 Images Roy Keane and Ian Wright were caught by the sprinklers (Image: ITV)

Both Roy Keane and Ian Wright had to make a quick getaway after they were SOAKED by the sprinklers ahead of England's game against Czechia. The pair were on punditry duty for ITV alongside presenter Mark Pougatch and were previewing Tuesday's Nations League match at Wembley.

‌



‌



But things took an unexpected turn when water started raining down on the trio. It came from a sprinkler that was watering the pitch little over 10 minutes before kick-off. "You might be getting a shower," Pougatch said.

‌



"Oh, mate, I gotta go this way," Wright replied, as he, Keane and Pougatch all scarpered and went off screen, hoping to avoid getting drenched. But their swanky outfits were still left sodden by the water.

‌



ITV quickly cut to a graphic and the sprinkler soon changed direction, allowing them to return. Keane and Wright had been analysing Thomas Tuchel's decision to make four changes to his starting line-up.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Out came Ezri Konsa, Alex Scott, Anthony Gordon and Bukayo Saka, and they were replaced by Trent Alexander-Arnold, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Morgan Rogers and Eberechi Eze. It was also a special night for England captain Harry Kane, as he reached 125 caps.

The Three Lions came into the game off the back of a record-breaking 7-0 win away to Croatia, boosting their chances of reaching the quarter-finals of the Nations League in March. "It was a very, very good 90 minutes," Tuchel hailed.

"Very impressive performance on and off the ball. During the match, I had a moment after three minutes and I thought that's a good start and after six minutes it was still a good start and it just kept on going until 40 minutes.

‌



Will England beat Czechia? Give us your score prediction in the comments section.

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel spoke to ITV pre-match (Image: Robin Jones/Getty Images)

"We scored the fourth one and just kept on going. We felt from the start it was a good performance."

Article continues below

The England boss went on to say: "We're getting there, I think the front four love to play with each other and they're very decisive. Anthony Gordon and Bukayo Saka have stepped up. These front four at the moment are very dangerous. I hope Morgan Rogers can prove a point today."

On newcomers into the squad, Tuchel added: "We made them responsible that they have a good experience with us and they don't feel like outsiders. They straight away are welcomed and feel comfortable enough to be at their best. I am very happy with Lewis Hall he made a big impression and opened up the competition for sure."

Sports.title: Manager accused of 'doing a Ten Hag' on Cristiano Ronaldo after going back on 'secret agreement'
Sports.content:
Manager accused of 'doing a Ten Hag' on Cristiano Ronaldo after going back on 'secret agreement'

Cristiano Ronaldo and Jorge Jesus are at odds with one another after a 'misunderstanding' on international duty

View 2 Images Cristiano Ronaldo left the Portugal squad last week after a falling out with Jorge Jesus. (Image: (Photo by Octavio Passos/Getty Images))

Piers Morgan has blasted Portugal boss Jorge Jesus for going back on a 'secret agreement' he had with Cristiano Ronaldo following a fallout on international duty. Ronaldo left Portugal's international camp after being snubbed by Jesus during their win over Norway.

‌



‌



It's understood there was an agreement in place for Ronaldo to come on for the final half hour of the game, but he was left as an unused substitute, prompting the superstar to hold emergency talks with the Portuguese FA and leave the camp on a private jet.

‌



Morgan has accused Jesus of 'doing a Ten Hag' referring to the former Manchester United head coach calling out with Ronaldo during his second stint at Old Trafford.

‌

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Speaking on the Sports Uncensored podcast, Morgan said: "What this comes down to, it's nothing to do with money, fame or any of these things. He was given absolute guarantees about how he'd be used.

‌



"It was one of the reasons he decided to continue his international career. The new guy, Jorge Jesus, who knows him from Saudi Arabia, said to him 'With the Nations League this is what I want you to do.'

"They agreed he'd play the first two games, then he'd rest for the next two. In the first game he was told 'You'll get 90 minutes.' This is manager to player. It's Cristiano Ronaldo, it's important to remember the stature of the person you're talking about.

"He gets yanked off [the pitch] after 67 minutes. So he's a bit p***** off and afterwards, the coach apologised to him. Repeated that apology to the president and said he would go out and he would explain this shouldn't have happened.

‌



"He goes out and does the opposite. What he does, is he pulls a Ten Hag where he goes out and tries to belittle and embarrass Ronaldo, put him back in his box and say all the players are as important to me blah, blah, blah.

"Which also p***** off Ronaldo. He then goes to Ronaldo and says 'I know we said you'd rest for the next two games but I want you for 30 minutes against Norway.'

‌



"He went 'right, okay if that's what you want, I'll do it.' It is good of him because they'd agreed something else. He sits there and then gets warmed up for 25 minutes and he never gets on the pitch.

"Again, he's p***** off by the lack of respect, the going back on his word. You're probably going to say Portugal won the game. They won the Nations League last year, who scored in the final? Cristiano Ronaldo. So don't give me the 'they're better without him.'

"Here's my point, for him, it's a question of respect, being promised one thing then the opposite happened. Being warmed up and not used which he felt was very disrepsectful. Eventually he went 'f*** you' and got on a plane and left.

‌



"His argument is, this coach kept going out in press conference and saying the opposite."

View 2 Images (Image: Watch the full interview on Piers Morgan Uncensored, YouTube)

Fellow host Simon Jordan interjected and asked: "Do you know this to be true?"

‌



Morgan ignored the question and replied: "You may not like that his coach is offering him deals. Saying play this, play that, but that happens in top-level football with the older players.

"He was made guarantees, he then offered to help and play against Norway when he was told he was going to rest that game. Ultimately, this coach has repeatedly gone out in press conferences and said, 'I'm in charge. I'm the big dog, this guy is just another player.'

"I'll refer you back to Ancelotti and Modric, where he said you don't do that to a top player."

Article continues below

Sky reporter Kaveh Solhekol would outline the difference between playing in Saudi Arabia where Ronaldo is the main man, compared to the national team, before Jordan took a swipe at his fellow host.

"You haven't hear what he's said to Cristiano," Jordan replied to Morgan. " What you're doing is you're being subjective because of your admiration for Ronaldo. You know you do it, I know you do it, be objective."

Sports.title: Man Utd launch new role to stop ticket touts after fan protests at Old Trafford
Sports.content:
Man Utd launch new role to stop ticket touts after fan protests at Old Trafford

Manchester United have faced a problem of ticket touts for some time and the Red Devils are now taking action, despite a prominent supporters group having spoken out

View 2 Images Manchester United have advertised a new position on their official website (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United are hiring a specialist as part of their bid to stop ticket touts at Old Trafford once and for all. The Red Devils have regularly been blighted by the issue, with perpetrators hoovering up tickets and selling them at inflated prices.

‌



‌



But now United are stepping up their attempts to combat touting. The club have advertised the role of a Supporter Escalations Executive, who will be tasked with leading a number of investigations when it comes to tickets and the distribution of them.

‌



The advert, launched on United’s official website reads: “This role is key to support the Club's mission to tackle ticket touting by independently managing a high volume of complex supporter investigations, sanctions, appeals and escalations.

‌



“Use AI, technology and spreadsheet-based data analysis to identify patterns, trends and emerging risks, while applying excellent judgement and delivering clear, empathetic communication. Ensure every case is handled efficiently and consistently, upholding Club policy, values, legal obligations and fairness across the whole fanbase.”

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Based at Old Trafford, the new executive will act as a ‘primary point of contact for supporters’ and will largely lead investigations into perceived instances of touting. Another key responsibility includes building ‘trust and confidence by ensuring supporters feel heard, informed and respected throughout their appeal or escalation, regardless of outcome, while protecting consistency and fairness across the whole fanbase’.

United’s move to introduce a new face comes after they chose to ban 685 season ticket holders that the club thought were involved in touting, albeit some maintain their innocence. That decision left fellow fans feeling disgruntled, with some supporters choosing to stage a protest in last month’s Manchester derby against Manchester City.

A statement from fan group The Red Army read: “This isn’t a ‘TRA’ message, it’s a message on behalf of every genuine fan group, match-going supporter, supporters’ club and fan representative who has either contacted us directly or been negatively impacted by the recent behaviour of the club.

‌



View 2 Images Manchester United fans protested when they faced Manchester City last month (Image: Getty Images)

“It’s an honest, heartfelt cry for recognition from the maligned, vilified, and misrepresented beating heart of our football club – the generational match-going supporters.

“Neither is this solely a ‘Manchester United’ problem, this is a league-wide crisis that should be addressed at every club, regardless of rivalries and history. Without drastic changes, there will be no rivalries in the future vision for football shared by the decision makers.”

Sports.title: Ex-Arsenal star Gabriel Jesus gives honest verdict on Barcelona transfer after exit
Sports.content:
Ex-Arsenal star Gabriel Jesus gives honest verdict on Barcelona transfer after exit

Gabriel Jesus brought an injury-hit spell with Arsenal to a close in the summer as he opted to join Spanish giants Barcelona on a permanent deal, and he's already off the mark for his new employers

View 2 Images Gabriel Jesus has scored twice for Barcelona following his summer switch from Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Gabriel Jesus is relishing his time with Barcelona after completing a shock move to the Spanish giants. The Brazilian opted for a move to the Camp Nou in the summer, with a £8.6million deal being agreed.

‌



‌



Jesus, 29, has enjoyed a bright start to life with his new club, scoring twice in four appearances in all competitions.

‌



In an interview with Sport, he has now opened up on the efforts that he went to to ensure he adapted to life in Spain. He said: “They gave us a plan for the days off and I trained a lot.

‌



“I have felt very good. It was a month to adapt. I already knew some players I had played with, so it was good to get to know everyone. We have incredible players and a great coach. We are going in the right direction.”

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



On his move to Barcelona, Jesus added: “I feel very good to be at a club like this. All the fans remind me that I used to miss some classes to watch Barça in the Champions League.

“To end up wearing the Barça shirt is something I thank God for. It is his doing. And here I am.”

Jesus also opened up on his best friend with his new club and it was no surprise to see him select one of his former Manchester City team-mates.

‌



He said: “The funniest player in the team is [Joao] Cancelo because of the way he talks, the way he is. He is a good guy. I have a very good relationship with him.

View 2 Images Gabriel Jesus has enjoyed a productive start to life with Barcelona (Image: Getty Images)

“I get on well with all my teammates, but I have a long history with Cancelo. We talk a lot, so I will go with Cancelo.”

‌



Both Jesus and Cancelo spent three years as team-mates with former side Man City, winning three Premier League crowns and helping the club reach the Champions League final. Jesus left the Etihad in 2022 to join Premier League rivals Arsenal.

He endured an injury-hit spell with the North London side, scoring 32 goals in 123 appearances. Jesus rounded off his stint with Arsenal on a high, having claimed yet another Premier League winners’ medal.

Jesus will be back in action for Barcelona this weekend as they take on Getafe. Hansi Flick’s side currently sit top of La Liga and five points clear of nearest challengers Atletico Madrid after winning each of their opening seven games of the campaign.
