Sports.title: How FIA software bug caused chaos in Bahrain GP in Malaysia – and the emergency fix that saved the race
Sports.content:
The start of the first wet-weather race of the 2026 Formula 1 season descended into chaos. Leader Max Verstappen was the first to suffer from a lack of power while driving slowly during the formation laps behind the safety car, after which Lewis Hamilton came to a standstill and several other cars followed.

Race control was forced to stop the formation lap with a red flag, after which there was a 40-minute delay before fans actually got to see some F1 action.

Read Also: Formula 1 FIA explains software glitch that caused Bahrain GP in Malaysia race delay

FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis confirmed to media including Autosport that a bug in the software supplied by the FIA and developed together with the teams over the course of multiple years was responsible for the chaos.

“We didn't manage to test the software as extensively as we would have liked because there's been very little wet running this year. There was a bit of a combination of circumstances which caused this bug to kick in,” Tombazis said during an impromptu media session post-race.

“Basically, on the formation lap, some cars went very slowly and almost came to a standstill. There was a bit of a concertina effect between cars and some cars almost stopped completely. That bug prevented then the power to be redeployed and for the cars to start again.”

This is closely related to the reduction in electrical power to 250kW in wet conditions.

Although the software required for this was tested by several teams, including Red Bull and Racing Bulls, it was not tested in the conditions behind the safety car – and therefore not at these extremely low speeds.

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

At the Sepang International Circuit, those low speeds were reached in certain minisectors, with all the consequences that followed.

“It was mainly in some sectors where the full power was reduced. I don't know exactly what speed that was, but some cars reaching this very low speed somehow entered into a loop, which meant they couldn't re-accelerate and then it looked as if they came to a stop.”

In practice, this left drivers feeling as though the throttle pedal was no longer responding, something Oliver Bearman told the media with some surprise.

“I've never seen or felt anything like that. I was shocked that… I didn't even know that the FIA could control our throttle pedal. That was quite scary, actually,” the Haas driver said.

“My throttle pedal just stopped working. It was like it was not connected and the engine was just idling. It was so weird, I mean, shocking.”

One of the questions is why the internal combustion engine was also affected, when that should not be the case at extremely low speeds. The FIA does not yet have a formal answer to that question, but the initial suggestion is that the bug caused all throttle input to go towards recharging the MGU-K, which explains why drivers felt there was no response from the throttle pedal at all.

At first glance, it appeared as though the Mercedes-powered cars were less affected by the issue than other manufacturers, but Tombazis explained that there is no technical reason for that. It was simply related to the speeds reached in certain minisectors.

Nikolas Tombazis, FIA Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

“Not all cars reached the same low speeds on the formation lap. There was a bit of a concertina effect. I think Max slowed down quite a lot, being at the front, and then some cars braked harder as they were surprised and so on. That caused some cars to experience the problem and some others to not experience it.”

How the FIA provided F1 teams with an emergency fix

The FIA then had to react quickly to get the race near Kuala Lumpur under way after all, as Tombazis explained when asked by Autosport.

“Fortunately, our guys understood the issue very, very quickly. I think the update was done very competently. It was obviously a rush job. The priority was to get running as quickly as possible again, so I think the reaction time was quite fast,” he said.

“It wasn't a perfect job and, clearly, we didn't test the updates, but I think it was the way to handle such a case.”

In practice, the update meant that the FIA lifted the energy limit constraint – the restrictions associated with the 250kW limit – for the minisectors in which the low speeds had triggered the bug. Logically, this is not a watertight solution going forward, but it was an emergency measure to ensure the race could go ahead.

“In some of the sectors, some of these reductions of power were overridden,” Tombazis confirmed. “Clearly, we didn't have five days to do the updates. We only had a few minutes, but fortunately, I think we managed to do it without compromising any safety, any racing or fairness.”

How could this happen in the first place?

After the FIA update, all the teams still had to install the modified software, which explains the delay before the restart. The Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia was saved as a result, but that still does not explain how the FIA could have missed this issue throughout all its preparations and why it only surfaced in round 16 of the championship.

“The software was tested. It just wasn't tested in those specific conditions,” Tombazis replied. “What caught us out was the fact that cars went in that very, very low speed, which was not normally contemplated.”

FIA Safety Car Photo by: Rudy Carezzevoli / Getty Images

During the tyre tests in which the software was tested, the extremely low speeds were understandably not reached. Nevertheless, there is a crucial counterargument to that: in the rain, the likelihood of a safety car – and therefore low speeds – is very high. Should the FIA not have anticipated that, and was that the governing body’s biggest mistake?

Asked that question by Autosport, Tombazis responded: “Well, any bug is a product of a mistake. I don't know of any software that doesn't have bugs and updates. Your computer probably gets updated every three days and those are all bugs.

“Of course, anticipating these things is what one hopes to do, but sometimes some very combination of events isn't properly anticipated and causes the problem. I think if we had had a bit more testing, we probably would have managed to catch it in time and not to have such a situation.”

Although the cause of this problem is now known and a temporary fix has been introduced, the FIA still has many questions to answer internally – also to ensure that it does not happen again.

“We would all like it to be simpler, but the fact is when you have as much electrical energy, it does make it more complicated. I think you appreciate that the race has now finished about one hour ago and we haven't done a full debrief of the situation to see how we can avoid such an issue.

“Every race, we have a long debrief afterwards where we identify criticalities. Obviously, that was a major criticality and we need to make sure we avoid it.

“But can I guarantee it will never happen again? This specific problem, yes. A problem, no. But we will do our best to avoid it, of course.”

Sports.title: The slick tyre gamble that hurt McLaren and Ferrari's chances in Bahrain GP in Malaysia
Sports.content:
When the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia eventually got going after an hour and 33 minutes of delays, it became apparent that the intermediate was the tyre to be on among the opening laps - even if the Sepang circuit had looked like it was drying out.

At the front of the field, Ferrari and McLaren chose to go all-in on the dry tyres for the restart; Ferrari opted for the soft compound, while McLaren went for the mediums. When the race got underway behind the safety car, both teams were left to rue their choices as the circuit was still too slippery.

McLaren bailed on the plan early, stopping before the standing start to ensure Oscar Piastri could get a set of intermediates back onto the car, but Lando Norris and the Ferraris stuck with their choices. Charles Leclerc duly fed into the pitlane at the end of the lap, as the slick-tyre runners were swamped and then left behind by those who'd stuck with the intermediate for the start.

Lewis Hamilton and Norris surmised that, since they'd made their beds, they'd lie in them. Hamilton was asked if he wanted to stop again, but the seven-time champion reasoned that Ferrari might as well stick with the gamble given that the team was well behind - and pitting would only cost more time.

By the end of the eighth lap, the slick times were now equal with the intermediate runners; Valtteri Bottas' subsequent off then presented the inter-shod drivers with the chance to switch to slicks.

Speaking about the decision, Norris stated that the idea of starting on the slick was "quite convincing" and that he was unsure of the performance of the inter; on his recon lap to the grid, the Briton reported that the green-walled tyre was already feeling the pain on Sepang's rough surface.

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Joe Portlock / Getty Images

"It felt maybe a little bit of a risk, because a slick on a wet track is always a bit of a risk," Norris said. "There was enough people on it that it was quite convincing at the time that it was possibly going to be the right decision.

"The laps to the grid on the inter when it was a similar kind of condition, they had so much grip and my Inter was completely shredded after one lap.

"I was convinced a slick tyre would work, but I think it was just the fact I've never really been on the inter before. Things just felt a lot better than they should have done in a way.

"If we would have had a read on an inter from a previous weekend, maybe I would have been able to understand it more. But that convinced us and it clearly convinced a lot of people.

"Oscar probably made the right decision in boxing and we got it wrong today, that's all."

Leclerc theorised that the roughness of the tarmac made it more difficult to read the track surface, as water pooled up in the gaps - and the drop in temperature that accompanied the rain ensured that the circuit took much longer to dry out than expected. Given the length of the downpour, any residual circuit temperature was swiftly extinguished.

Even though the Monegasque switched tyres, the time loss involved in pitting after the start kept him behind Hamilton, who ran longer on his set of soft tyres and quickly began to make up positions.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Carlos Sainz, Williams Photo by: Joe Portlock / Getty Images

Hamilton joked that he wasn't going to "go to the casino with the guys" after the team's gambles didn't pay off, although praised his team's strategy in keeping him out on the road. The Briton was ultimately less enamoured with the medium after making a stop on lap 31, but the late-race VSC (later a full safety car) presented a chance to return to the soft - which he put to use with a pass on Isack Hadjar for third.

"As we pulled out [of the pits], all the spray came out the back of Max’s car and I was like, 'okay, I’m done. My race is really in trouble,'" Hamilton recounted.

"We just had to stick with it. As everyone’s overtaken me, they [the engineers] were like, 'we stop.' I know we’ve already made another 26 seconds. What’s the difference from that with one minute 40 or whatever I was down? So I was just, 'Let’s just wait it out for the track to dry.'

"And once it did, it felt good that I was catching people. The car felt great then after that. Really good pitstops from my guys in the garage and then good strategy. But for us to get back to the podium, I never thought that that was going to be the case. Of course, I’m really, really grateful that we managed to get back here.

"We’ll definitely have an open dialogue, and I’m really so proud of my team. The mechanics every weekend, just the work they’re putting in, the engineers that accompany here every weekend, the catering, everyone really, really comes and gives it their best.

"Their heart’s all in the right spot. We’ve definitely got areas that we need to improve and we know that, and we’re not in any denial of that. So I think we’ll have a constructive chat, we’ll regroup, we’ll take the positives from this weekend, which the car was really good, and we’ll come back next week fighting."

Sports.title: FIA explains software glitch that caused Bahrain GP in Malaysia race delay
Sports.content:
The FIA has given insight into why Formula 1 cars experienced technical issues ahead of Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

The start of the Sepang race was delayed by 40 minutes due to a downpour; then a chaotic formation lap saw the likes front-row starters Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton suffer from a glitch which rendered throttle input ineffective, with numerous cars coming to a standstill. The red flag was waved.

The situation was branded “unacceptable” by Sergio Perez, who likened it to ‘being in a rental kart and running out of time’; Lando Norris described it “just horrible” and evidence that “we shouldn't have any of that stuff, the electronic side”, given this was linked to Formula 1’s new machinery, which features 47% electrical power.

FIA single-seater Nikolas Tombazis has now explained that, given F1 had never had competitive running in actual wet conditions this season, it was caught out by the power unit’s reaction to cars driving extremely slowly at that time. A software update therefore had to be carried out, hence a 53-minute delay to get the race restarted.

“We didn't manage to test the software as extensively as we would have liked, because there's been very little wet running this year, and there was a bit of a combination of circumstances which caused this bug to kick in,” Tombazis said.

Nikolas Tombazis, FIA Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

“Basically, the formation lap, some cars went very slowly, almost came to a standstill. There was a bit of a concertina effect between cars, and some cars almost stopped completely. And that bug prevented the power to be redeployed and for the cars to start again. I think if we had had a bit more testing, we probably would have managed to catch it in time and not to have such a situation.”

Tombazis praised the FIA’s reaction when it came to fixing the issue as swiftly as possible.

“Once the problem happened, our guys realised very quickly what was happening and had to work under a lot of time pressure for an update to the software, which was issued to the teams, and the teams had to install it on their cars,” he added.

“So all of that took about 20 minutes. It may have felt like five hours for spectators waiting [for] a race and for everybody else, which is understandable, and we are sorry about that. But I think it was quite a fast reaction given the problem.”

Not everyone was so upset about some cars running into trouble, with eighth-placed Fernando Alonso joking at the end of an unusually good day for Aston Martin-Honda: “I had 50% DNFs this year, they never stopped the race for us.”

Sports.title: Russell: “You’ve got to laugh” at bad luck as F1 title drifts away
Sports.content:
Mercedes driver George Russell labelled his misfortune as laughable following Formula 1’s Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, where a power unit failure cost him a podium finish late on.

Russell was a lowly seventh on the grid at Sepang, but the correct choice of intermediate tyres on a damp track and a lightning getaway saw him surge to second into Turn 1, behind team-mate Kimi Antonelli.

Russell was however passed by Max Verstappen as early as lap six, but the first safety car period gave him a chance to sweep past Antonelli around the outside of Turn 5 at the restart as the race leader dropped down to third – though the Italian youngster found a way back into second place just eight laps later.

Further drama did not disrupt the status quo in the top three, but a late safety car meant Russell had a chance to challenge his rivals for victory. However, the chance never came as a power unit failure took him out of the race before the final restart.

“You've almost got to laugh,” Russell told Sky Sports F1 after his third retirement this season – his second purely technical DNF. “It's beyond disappointment. It's just, so many times this season it's happened.

“Of course, it's a real shame, but… Just keep on fighting. Just keep on trying to go.

“The podium, of course, looked very certain. Solid race, not amazing race, but solid race.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Alex Bierens de Haan / LAT Images via Getty Images

“Not the first time, so I'm pretty used to this feeling and these questions, let's say.”

As he said, Russell will “keep on fighting”, but is equally aware of his deficit to championship rival Antonelli reaching an unprecedented 84 points.

The Briton steered clear of any sensational comments – he won’t say the title is out of reach – but his assessment is bleak nonetheless.

“I don't need to say I think it's gone or whatever,” he added. “But, of course, it’s exceptionally unlikely, and that's just the reality.

“I knew if I wanted to come back I needed luck on my side. Unfortunately, I've had luck not on my side. So, you know, a three-point loss today being behind Kimi turned into an 18-point loss. Of course, if the issue was on the other side, it would have been an 18-point gain.

“So, yeah, it's a real shame. It's a real shame, but that's just how it is.”

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff said the Bahrain GP in Malaysia had been one of his “worst experiences” personally, as Red Bull claimed its first victory of the year over the Silver Arrows and Russell suffered that setback.

“I'm so massively annoyed,” Wolff told Sky. “I'm not in a happy place.

Toto Wolff, Mercedes Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

“We didn't have the speed that we were hoping to have before the weekend, so there's a lot of homework to be done in order to recover, which I'm sure we will. Then the race literally went, if you consider the fight with Lewis [Hamilton] behind, went against us. We had such an advantage, one VSC, two safety cars. I mean, you couldn't be more unlucky. And to make things worse, PU failure with a few laps to go to the end with George, which is terrible for his championship and not good at all for our constructor points.”

After praising Antonelli for ‘doing the job’, the Austrian added: “It's just this overarching topic, the DNFs, that could cost us dearly also for the remaining seven races. A championship is quickly turned around against you or for you if you have a DNF, and that's why that can't continue.”

Perhaps Wolff was overdramatic there. At Sepang, Mercedes was outscored by Ferrari for just the first time since the summer break, and the Scuderia still is 151 points in arrears in the constructors’ championship. Meanwhile, Hamilton’s deficit to Antonelli in the drivers’ standings is up to 106 points.

Asked how to pull the team together after such a result, Wolff replied: “I think we have a good action plan. James [Allison, technical director] is really fully on top of it with his leadership team.

“That lifts my mood because I know we have such a tremendous group of people. In the same way as we have with HPP, they're going to sort it out. But that gives me real relief for the moment to know they are the best and they are going to find a solution. And I think we will come back strong.”

Sports.title: “F*** this s***”: Stroll’s frustrations began before he even left the grid in Sepang | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lance Stroll has struggled to reach the chequered flag in his Aston Martin so far this season.

He did get to the finish in Malaysia but it was a frustrating affair which prompted terse comments from the driver before he even left the grid to start the race.

Here are some of his exchanges with race engineer Gary Gannon on his way to 12th place in Sepang.

Team radio highlights from Stroll during the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia

Sports.title: Stats: Verstappen avoids first win-less season since 2015, Red Bull-Ford’s first win and more | 2026 Bahrain GP in Malaysia stats and facts
Sports.content:
Before the unusually-named Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia began, Max Verstappen made it clear he wanted to avoid ending the season without a victory.

He put that right on Sunday, ensuring he claimed a victory for the 11th season in a row. He only failed to win a grand prix in his debut season at Toro Rosso (now Racing Bulls) in 2015.

But Verstappen needs to keep winning every year until 2030 to equal Michael Schumacher and Lewis Hamilton’s joint record of 15 consecutive winning seasons (from 1992 to 2006 and 2007 to 2021 respectively).

Verstappen claimed the first victory for car number three since his former team mate Daniel Ricciardo won the Italian Grand Prix for McLaren five years ago. Two other drivers on the grid today have won with that number: Fernando Alonso twice in 2013 at Ferrari and Hamilton three times for McLaren in 2011, both in seasons before the FIA introduced ‘career numbers’.

This was the 72nd victory of Verstappen’s career. It came in Malaysia’s first grand prix in nine years, which Verstappen also won, taking the second win of his career at that point.

The race carried the title ‘Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia’ as it took the place of April’s cancelled race in the Middle East. It is by no means unique for one country to hold an event named for another: San Marino, Luxembourg and Switzerland all gave their names to races in other nearby countries: Italy, Germany and France respectively.

But there were a few noteworthy differences. Those latter cases were all events held in addition to rounds which took place in those countries, while F1 is not racing in Bahrain at all this year as it was considered too unsafe due to the proximity to the conflict in Iran. Precisely because of that, the distance between the event and the country it was named after was much greater than those earlier cases, being some 6,000 kilometres.

So instead of the Bahrain International Circuit holding its 23rd race, the Sepang International Circuit held its 20th. In theory Bahrain will hold the first round on the 2027 F1 calendar, but watch this space.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Verstappen’s success vindicated Red Bull’s decision to build their own power unit, in conjunction with Ford. The latter last contributed to a grand prix victory in 2003, when Giancarlo Fisichella won the Brazilian Grand Prix for Jordan (now Aston Martin) powered by a Ford-Cosworth RS1.

The same power units ended Mercedes’ monopoly on pole positions this year. After 15 consecutive Mercedes-powered poles, Verstappen claimed the first for a (partly) Ford-badged engine since Rubens Barrichello put his Stewart at the front of the field for the 1999 French Grand Prix at Magny-Cours.

However a substantial amount of credit must also go to Red Bull, who had already committed to building their own power units before teaming up with Ford. Although they previously ran their Honda-designed units successfully, they deserve to be regarded as a new engine constructor in their own right, and those don’t appear very often.

If we accept this was the first victory for a new engine built by a new constructor, when was the last time this happened? Red Bull’s other wins since 2022 have been credited to ‘Red Bull Powertrains’ and Honda RBPT but all involved the same Honda-derived power units.

Other new names which appeared on the winners lists in previous years were often due to branding exercises. Red Bull previously won races with Renault engines badged as TAG Heuer. Engines produced by Honda and Porsche won races labelled as Mugen-Honda and TAG-Porsche respectively.

Using a strict definition, avoiding all rebranded engines and those related to previous designs by constructors who had already won races, Red Bull-Ford’s win is the first for a new F1 engine constructor since BMW in 1982. That win came courtesy of Brabham’s Nelson Piquet in the Canadian Grand Prix. In an extremely unusual result, his team mate Riccardo Patrese finished that race in second place powered by a different engine: his Brabham was powered by Ford.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

The others manufactures on the grid today are either yet to win (Audi) or scored their first wins long ago: Ferrari in 1951, Mercedes in 1954 and Honda in 1965.

A week ago, George Russell grabbed the eighth win of his career, in Baku. Verstappen served notice of Red Bull’s potential there, chasing his rival across the line, the pair separated by just 0.196 seconds. This was the closest finish to a grand prix since the rigged conclusion to the 2002 United States Grand Prix, where Schumacher attempted to contrive a ‘dead heat’ with team mate Barrichello, but instead was beaten to the line by 0.011s.

Finally, Fernando Alonso took advantage of the conditions in Sepang to claim Aston Martin’s best finish of the season with eighth place. Those four points leave his team just five shy of Williams.

Over to you

Have you spotted any other interesting stats and facts from the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia or Azerbaijan Grand Prix? Share them in the comments.

Sports.content:
Confusion reigned when Formula 1 drivers headed out to begin yesterday’s grand prix.

A software glitch struck much of the grid, causing some cars to slow to a crawl and others to stop entirely. Some power units sprang back into life while others stubbornly refused to work again.

Eventually race control abandoned the attempt to start the race and summoned the field back into the pits so the FIA could issue a software update. The process took the best part of an hour.

The problem was widespread throughout the field and affected drivers in different ways. Here’s how several of them experienced the fault.

1st: Max Verstappen

Verstappen’s car almost came to a stop at the front of the field. However a switch change on his steering wheel solved the problem for him.

The car accelerates away Lambiase Looks like maybe Lewis has a similar problem to you. He’s still struggling between turn 11 and turn 12.

Expecting the start to go ahead, Verstappen was unhappy that the side of the grid he was due to start from was wetter than the opposite side.

Sports.title: Fan’s video shows moment software glitch slowed F1 cars to a crawl on formation lap | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1’s 2026 engine regulations faced fresh criticism yesterday following the farcical start to the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

The race, which had already been delayed by rain, was postponed by almost an hour more after a software problem struck cars during the formation lap.

Pole-winner Max Verstappen and several drivers behind him slowed to a crawl as their power units would not allow them to accelerate. The cause was a software parameter set by the FIA, which required the governing body to apply new settings to the cars.

Verstappen said he had as much power as he did when the drivers raced in Lego cars in a promotional event.

“It was like the Lego race,” he said. “Same speed. It was insane, it’s the Lego power.

“At some point we were five-wide on the straight because we couldn’t understand what was going on. Then we did a lap and then I see eight other cars crawling still.

“That’s not what you want, right, for the sport.”

The FIA said the cars’ loss of power was due to “an unprecedented combination of low engine speed, low-grip conditions, wet-weather energy management settings and the Sepang circuit’s sector configuration.”

Sports.title: Mercedes ‘don’t know if upgrade made us faster or slower’ – Antonelli | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The long-awaited upgrade package Mercedes introduced last weekend may have made them less competitive, Andrea Kimi Antonelli has admitted.

Antonelli led the opening stages of yesterday’s race ahead of team mate George Russell . However both were overtaken by Max Verstappen , who went on to win the race.

Mercedes originally planned to introduce their new parts for the W17 at this weekend’s race in Singapore. They brought the upgrade forward after Formula 1 added last weekend’s round in Malaysia to replace the cancelled event in Bahrain.

However the unusually abrasive track surface at the Sepang International Circuit complicated the team’s efforts to understand the performance of its upgraded car. Antonelli qualified half a second slower than Verstappen.

He said the performance of the upgrade is “the question we need to answer because we don’t really know if it made us go faster or worse.”

However he pointed out the team has been less competitive at tracks which share some traits with Sepang. “It’s fair to say that this season, whenever we went on really old Tarmac, we’ve struggled. For example, in Zandvoort, McLaren was much quicker than us, especially on the older Tarmac.

“So I think maybe it’s just a fact that the Tarmac is very old and that for the tyres it’s very, very hard, and maybe we just struggle on this kind of Tarmac.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“But, of course, the track and the Tarmac made our life difficult in understanding whether it made us improve or not.”

The championship leader expects the team will have some answers before this weekend’s race. “I’m sure the team – they have a lot of data, especially after this weekend – and I’m sure for Singapore we will come with a much, much better view on the package and hopefully we can extract the full potential out of it.”

Sports.title: Spotlight: ‘Who decided these rules were best for F1?’ asks Sainz | Brief
Sports.content:
The farcical scenes during yesterday’s formation laps which delayed the start of the race by almost an hour prompted criticism from several drivers.

Grand Prix Drivers Association director Carlos Sainz Jnr was among those questioning why Formula 1 committed itself years ago to rules which have proved so problematic.

“[F1] needs to have a hard look at themselves and see how we ended up in this situation,” he said after the race. “It is clear the regs are extremely complicated for the drivers, for the teams, for the power units, for the manufacturers. It is too complicated.

“Again, my only question mark is who five years ago decided that this was the direction to go?”

F1 confirmed its current engine regulations in 2022, though the majority of the changes were substantially agreed before then. Mohammed Ben Sulayem became FIA president in December 2021.

Sainz’s father, multiple world rally champion Carlos Sainz, considered opposing Ben Sulayem in last year’s election, but chose not to. Ben Sulayem won re-election and subsequently moved to end presidency term limits, allowing him to serve as president as long as he likes.

Sports.title: Hamilton suspects he could have fought for win had he not started on slicks | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton believes he could have fought for victory at Sepang had he started on the right tyres.

The Ferrari driver qualified on the front row of the grid alongside Max Verstappen

“We were having a good weekend,” he said. “The car felt great in qualifying. It felt amazing to get to second.

“Me and my engineers were here ’til 11:30 last night just going over everything and I really, really felt today was the opportunity to have at least a good battle with Max.”

The original start was delayed due to rain. A further delay followed after a software problem caused several drivers, including Hamilton and Verstappen, to slow to a crawl during the formation lap.

“My power didn’t come back and I had to stop on-track and restart the car and then we all ended up in the pit lane,” said Hamilton. “Thankfully, we all got back to our positions.”

By the time race control were ready to start the race, the track had dried considerably, though it was still damp. Hamilton and his team chose to start the race on slick tyres.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“There was such a long wait and we were debating what tyre to go on to. And I said, ‘look, there was a lot of spray on the laps to the grid.’

“I went into the pit lane, I looked at the ground, I was like, ‘It’s still wet.’ I went to the pit wall and I was like, ‘It’s still wet.’ And they’re like, ‘Yeah, but because it’s been so long, it’s definitely going to dry up real quick and maybe we’re already in the crossover.’

“So, anyway, as a team we ended up taking that soft and when we were at the end of the pit lane and these two took off their blankets and they were on inters [I knew] we were in trouble.”

The track took a long time to dry and those who opted for intermediates gained a significant advantage at the start. Hamilton urged the team not to bring him into the pits for another change.

“As everyone had overtaken me, they’re like, ‘we stop.’ [But] I know we’ve already [lost] another 26 seconds, what’s the difference from that with one minute 40 or whatever I was down? So I [said] ‘let’s just wait it out for the track to dry.’ And once it did, it felt good that I was catching people.”

Hamilton began to make progress on his softs once the Safety Car came out and he was back within range of other cars.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“The car felt great then after that. Really good pit stops from my guys in the garage and then good strategy.

“For us to get back to the podium, I never thought that that was going to be the case. But, of course, I’m really, really grateful that we managed to get back here.”

He said he will have an “open dialogue” with the team about the decision to start the race on slicks.

“We’ve definitely got areas that we need to improve and we know that, and we’re not in any denial of that.

“So I think we’ll have a constructive chat, we’ll regroup, we’ll take the positives from this weekend, which was the car was really good, and we’ll come back next week fighting. I thought today, as I said, was a chance for us potentially to try and fight Max for the win, but maybe we can do that next week.”

Sports.title: Conor Wallace Questions Referee After Ben Whittaker Loss
Sports.content:
Conor Wallace believes the referee made it harder for him to finish Ben Whittaker last Saturday, allowing him to hold while hurt and declining to count falls that Wallace felt deserved knockdowns.

The late trouble also gives Eddie Hearn a reason to think carefully about a rematch. Neither Hearn nor Whittaker has committed to facing Wallace again, and the promoter has mentioned other possible opponents.

“I do definitely feel like the referee didn’t do me any favors,” Wallace told talkSPORT’s White and Jordan show on Tuesday morning. “I definitely feel like one or possibly two of them should have been knockdowns, and he was holding on for dear life. “You need to be given a chance to get going, and I was trying to get the action going. Yes, I did smother myself a little bit. Maybe I was trying too hard to put him away. I should have shortened those shots when I look back at it, but hindsight is a wonderful thing.”

Wallace puts his complaint at one or possibly two knockdowns. There is a case for examining all three falls, along with Whittaker’s repeated holding. Counting those falls and deducting points could have changed the result. Enforcing the rules on holding could also have forced Whittaker to keep fighting when he was struggling to survive.

Wallace accepts that he contributed to the missed opportunity by crowding his punches. Shorter shots and a little more room could make him harder to contain if he gets Whittaker hurt again.

He also wants to start faster, having conceded the early rounds. That requires care against Whittaker’s counter right, but Wallace now has twelve rounds of experience against him and knows he can cause trouble late.

Hearn has talked about Whittaker as a generational talent. Putting him straight back in with someone who came close to stopping him would put that description to a serious test. Wallace may have his number, particularly if he improves his opening rounds and finishes more patiently.

Choosing another opponent would be understandable from Hearn’s side. Whittaker already has his IBF mandatory position, and another Wallace fight brings considerable risk. Wallace’s confidence alone will not get the rematch made; Hearn and Whittaker still have to decide whether they want to take that chance.

Sports.title: Osleys Iglesias Welcomes Christian Mbilli Unification Despite Shared Trainer
Sports.content:
Osleys Iglesias is willing to fight Christian Mbilli even if Marc Ramsey chooses the other corner, removing a potential obstacle to a super middleweight unification should both champions win their upcoming defenses.

The two fighters share Ramsey, but Iglesias will not allow that arrangement to prevent him from facing the WBC champion.

“Whoever’s in my corner is in my corner, but there are no excuses with me,” Iglesias told The Ring.

Iglesias defends his IBF title against Oliver Zaren this Thursday, October 8, in Quebec City on DAZN. Mbilli is scheduled to defend against Canelo Alvarez on October 31 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Iglesias views that fight as a 50-50 contest.

If both retain their titles, promoter Camille Estephan would have two champions at 168 pounds and an opportunity to arrange a unification. Iglesias has made clear that sharing a trainer would not be his reason for declining it.

The bigger obstacle could be business. If Mbilli beats Canelo, his next fight could attract considerably more attention. Matching him immediately against a dangerous puncher from the same stable would risk that opportunity.

Iglesias would have more to gain in recognition. Beating the man who had just defeated Canelo could transform his career, while Mbilli might have better-paying options. Having both champions under one promoter makes negotiations easier, but it does not guarantee Estephan wants the matchup.

Ramsey would also have a choice to make. If he stayed with Mbilli, his knowledge of Iglesias’s habits could help with preparation, although Iglesias only began working with him less than three months ago.

Inside the ring, Mbilli’s pressure could give Iglesias the exchanges he wants. Coming forward against a powerful southpaw creates opportunities for straight left hands and short counters.

That danger runs both ways. Iglesias would need to land enough to interrupt Mbilli’s attacks. If Mbilli takes his punches and keeps forcing exchanges, Iglesias would have to maintain his effectiveness through a demanding twelve rounds.

Iglesias must beat Zaren first. Beyond Thursday, his willingness puts the question to his promoter: would Eye of the Tiger match its champions if Mbilli returns from Riyadh with a victory over Canelo?

Sports.title: Floyd Schofield Questions Lucas Bahdi’s Boxing Skills
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield believes Lucas Bahdi is counting on one big punch to beat him this Saturday in Chicago, questioning whether the Canadian has the skills to win their vacant lightweight title fight any other way.

Schofield sees Bahdi’s knockout of Ashton Sylve as the approach he will try again: absorb punches, remain patient, and wait for Schofield to jump into something.

“I just think that they’re hoping I just jump in and he gets the same moment he had with Ashton,” Schofield said to Chris Mannix ahead of Saturday’s fight. “I would find it hard to believe that he thinks he’s a more skillful fighter than me or a better fighter than me. If so, then he’s crazy.”

Schofield described Bahdi’s patience and power as his best attributes, pointing out that Sylve hit him clean for six rounds without discouraging him. That is also the reason Schofield cannot afford to become careless if he builds an early lead.

Bahdi does not need to win every exchange to remain dangerous. Schofield could be landing the cleaner punches and controlling the fight, then give away everything by rushing forward with his head exposed. The temptation to force a stoppage could become Bahdi’s best opportunity.

Schofield also questioned Bahdi’s footwork and defense, saying he gets hit frequently and trips over his feet. Although Bahdi has changed trainers, Schofield doubts those habits can be corrected quickly at 31.

His father, Floyd Schofield Sr., believes his son has improved his distance control during camp and is picking his punches more carefully rather than jumping in.

That would be a useful change against Bahdi, but it has to last beyond the opening rounds. Schofield’s speed can help him score without staying in punching range. If he gets drawn into proving he can hurt Bahdi with every attack, he would be taking the very risk he believes the Canadian needs him to take.

Sports.title: Jaime Munguia Pursues Unranked Opponent Before Mandatory Defense
Sports.content:
Bektemir Melikuziev wants Jaime Munguia to defend his WBA super middleweight title against him, while the champion’s team reportedly negotiates a step-aside to squeeze in a fight with Keiber Gonzalez first.

That proposed opponent makes Bektemir’s frustration understandable. Gonzalez isn’t in the WBA’s published September top 15 at 168 pounds. Melikuziev is No. 1, yet he’s the fighter being asked to wait.

“The purse is not important, I am ready to fight for free. But please stop disrespecting me and the rules of the game!” Melikuziev wrote on Instagram. “Jaime Munguia, I was the mandatory for the title before you fought for it. You became the champion, respect me just like I would respect you or any other boxer if I was the champion.”

ESPN boxing reporter Salvador “Chava” Rodríguez reported on Instagram that Munguia’s team continues negotiating a step-aside with Melikuziev. According to Rodríguez, the negotiation window runs until October 21, with the aim of allowing Munguia to face Gonzalez before fulfilling his mandatory obligation.

Bektemir’s willingness to fight for free is an expression of how badly he wants the opportunity. It doesn’t establish that he has rejected every possible offer, but his message gives Munguia’s team little reason to assume money will settle this.

From Munguia’s side, Gonzalez looks like an easier defense before a more demanding fight. That may suit the champion, but it leaves Melikuziev waiting for a shot he had already earned before Munguia won the belt.

Even if Bektemir accepts payment to wait, that wouldn’t explain what Gonzalez has done to deserve the opportunity. The WBA would still have to justify approving an opponent outside its published top 15 while its leading challenger sits out.

Munguia has the title now. The responsibility that comes with it is facing the challenger who earned his turn. Asking Bektemir to watch Gonzalez get the next opportunity is a difficult sell, especially when Bektemir is publicly demanding the fight.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua Could Get Gassiev Next
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury or Anthony Joshua could face an easier opponent after their December 11 fight in Cardiff under a four-man WBA plan proposed by Eddie Hearn.

The proposal would pair Murat Gassiev with Jarrell Miller, with their winner facing whoever emerges from Fury–Joshua. That could provide a route to another heavyweight title victory without requiring either British veteran to beat Filip Hrgovic, Daniel Dubois, Fabio Wardley or Moses Itauma.

“I think any resolution would have to appease the parties involved. Then Jarrell Miller falls into that party as well because ultimately he’s number one,” Hearn said to Matchroom Boxing. “Is it a Gassiev v Miller, like two semifinals, AJ against Fury and the winners fight each other? So that’s something that’s possible, but we’ll have to see the official resolution from the WBA.”

Hearn said that there is no official WBA resolution yet. He also noted that putting a belt on Fury–Joshua would give Joshua the opportunity to become a three-time heavyweight champion.

A chance to become a three-time heavyweight champion gives Joshua a reason to back the plan. Facing Gassiev or Miller afterward would also look easier than taking on one of the division’s top contenders.

Gassiev has power, but his heavyweight record leaves him open to the paper-champion criticism. He has yet to demonstrate that he belongs alongside the best in the division. Miller, meanwhile, has not produced the kind of victory that would move the conversation away from his history of positive PED tests and toward his title credentials.

Neither would be harmless. Still, Joshua or Fury would have reason to like their chances against either man compared with the alternatives.

Dubois, Wardley, Hrgovic and Itauma would demand more physically from the two veterans. Those fights would offer a stronger test of whether the Fury–Joshua winner can still compete with the leading heavyweights.

That makes Hearn’s proposed WBA arrangement a good deal for Fury and Joshua. Either would have a good chance of beating the Gassiev–Miller winner, but selling that fight could be harder. A belt would give the promotion something to build around, while leaving more appealing opponents out of the picture.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Questions Zuffa’s Schedule and Spending
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn believes Zuffa Boxing has delivered too little for a promotion with substantial money, a broadcast contract, and access to Turki Alalshikh. His complaint is about the fights reaching fans, with the Matchroom promoter calling its first 10 months “absolutely abysmal.”

“With that money, with that contract, with those connections to Turki Alalshikh, the first 10 months have been absolutely abysmal,” Hearn told The Ariel Helwani Show.

Hearn identified July 26 as Zuffa’s last American show and questioned the lack of an announced U.S. return for the remainder of the year. Zuffa’s own results confirm that its July 26 New York event featured Edgar Berlanga against Steven Butler.

He pointed to Johnny Fisher against Pirotton and the upcoming Chris Billam-Smith–Chev Clarke fight as the promotion’s limited output during the following months. Billam-Smith and Clarke headline November 7 at London’s Copper Box Arena.

Billam-Smith against Clarke has competitive appeal, and Fisher has a following. But those are modest main events for a company whose resources invite expectations of something much bigger.

The American inactivity is the tougher part to explain. A promotion needs regular cards to give viewers a reason to keep watching. Signing recognizable fighters creates interest, but that interest can fade when there is no next date for fans to anticipate.

Shakur Stevenson’s situation adds to Hearn’s criticism. He claimed on X that Gary Antuanne Russell and Raymond Muratalla each want $3 million to face him, writing: “I would love to fight both them guys tho Zuffa gotta cough that 💰 up!”

Neither fight has been made. Shakur’s post does not establish that Zuffa refused to pay, but it identifies two opponents he wants and their asking prices, according to him. Signing Shakur gets Zuffa a recognizable name. Getting him into meaningful fights requires spending on the other side as well.

Hearn also took aim at White’s request to be judged over the next couple of years, describing it as a move away from an earlier 12-month timetable. That is Hearn’s interpretation, but it raises a fair question about how long Zuffa expects its launch period to last.

Hearn has an obvious commercial interest in making a rival look bad. Still, Zuffa needs an answer that comes through its schedule. More announcements could change the picture before December, but the money and connections only become useful to viewers when they produce fights worth watching.

Sports.title: Christian Mbilli Sees Age Catching Up With Canelo
Sports.content:
Christian Mbilli sees an older, slower Canelo Alvarez than the fighter in the knockout highlights, and his pressure could test how much the Mexican star has left. Canelo is scheduled to challenge for Mbilli’s WBC super middleweight title on October 31 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Thus far, the fight remains scheduled.

“He’s not the same guy right now,” Mbilli said while watching Canelo’s best stoppages in a video shared by DAZN Boxing.

Mbilli has a point. Canelo still has the timing to catch opponents, but his speed and activity no longer look the same. He attacks in shorter bursts, and his power at super middleweight hasn’t produced the stoppages he once delivered against smaller opposition.

Canelo’s last stoppage came against Caleb Plant in November 2021. He finished Plant in the 11th round to become undisputed at 168 pounds, but even that victory required patience against an opponent who made him work. Nearly five years later, those highlights show what Canelo could do then. Mbilli has to prepare for what he can do now.

There’s accumulated wear to consider, too. The first two Golovkin fights were demanding contests, while Dmitry Bivol repeatedly caught Canelo with combinations and forced him to work at a pace he couldn’t maintain successfully. Those fights may have contributed to the decline, although there’s no way to separate their effects from age.

The concern against Mbilli is what happens between Canelo’s attacks. If he needs longer pauses, Mbilli can use those stretches to throw combinations and make him defend instead of recover. Canelo could land the better individual punch and still lose rounds through inactivity.

Mbilli’s aggression also gives Canelo chances. Walking forward carelessly would leave him available for counters and body shots, and an older Canelo remains dangerous when opponents give him clean targets.

But Mbilli doesn’t need to prove Canelo has lost all his power. He needs to keep working after being caught. If Canelo can no longer discourage that pressure or match the pace, Mbilli’s observation could become the story of the fight.

Sports.title: Agit Kabayel’s Future Claim Looks Premature From Brown
Sports.content:
Agit Kabayel being described as the future of heavyweight boxing looks premature for a 34-year-old champion whose toughest tests could still be ahead. Spencer Brown offered that assessment at Tuesday’s kickoff press conference for Kabayel’s November 28 defense against Nelson Hysa.

“He is, for me, going to be the future of heavyweight boxing,” Brown said. “Since the day I met him, I knew greatness was coming. I really did. And he’s proved it to everybody.”

Brown also called Kabayel “the bogeyman of the heavyweights,” claiming nobody wants to fight him.

Kabayel has earned credit for his body punching, pressure, and ability to break opponents down. However, being at the top of his game now doesn’t mean he will stay there long enough to become the fighter Brown describes.

Zhilei Zhang exposed part of the concern last year. The 41-year-old dropped Kabayel with a left hand in the fifth round before being stopped in the sixth. Kabayel’s recovery showed toughness, but the knockdown also showed the danger of taking clean punches while trying to wear down a heavyweight.

Against an opponent who can keep throwing hard shots beyond the early rounds, that approach could become much more costly. Kabayel is hittable, and his pressure requires him to spend considerable time within punching range.

His best wins have come against Zhang, Frank Sanchez, Damian Knyba, Arslanbek Makhmudov and Derek Chisora. Sanchez’s knee trouble adds context to that victory; his co-manager subsequently disclosed that he underwent knee surgery.

It’s a useful collection of wins, but Kabayel still hasn’t faced Filip Hrgovic, Fabio Wardley, Daniel Dubois or Moses Itauma. Those fights would tell us considerably more about whether he can lead the division.

Beating the 42-year-old Hysa won’t settle that argument. Brown can talk about greatness, but Kabayel needs victories over the strongest available heavyweights to support it. At 34, he has less time to build that record than the “future” description suggests.

Ghana News.title: Police arrest suspect over jewellery theft during fire outbreak
Ghana News.content:
The Police in Koforidua have arrested Abubakar Abdul Latif, 32, for allegedly stealing female jewellery from a jewellery stand while firefighters battled a fire outbreak at Starlet 21 Street in Koforidua.

The suspect allegedly took advantage of the confusion surrounding the fire outbreak on October 4, 2026, at about 01:20 hours, to steal the jewellery from a stand near the scene.

Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) Augustine Asante Kusi, the New Juaben South Municipal Crime Officer, who disclosed this in an interview with the Ghana News Agency, said the suspect was arrested and was in Police custody assisting with investigations.

He said on October 3, 2026, at about 22:30 hours, the fire started in a room of a storey building at Starlet 21 Street, in Koforidua, and spread to other parts of the premises, prompting personnel of the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) and the Police to respond to the scene.

The personnel worked to bring the fire under control, secured the area and managed the crowd that had gathered at the scene.

ASP Kusi said Mrs Rita Akosua Adjei Awatey, the Eastern Regional Minister, together with Mr Ransford Owusu Boakye, the Municipal Chief Executive for New Juaben South, DCOP Joseph Owusu-Bempah, the Eastern Regional Police Commander, among others, visited the scene at about 23:10 hours on that same day.

He said the team assessed the extent of damage, commended the GNFS and Police for their swift response and assured the affected persons of Government support.

ASP Kusi said a fire officer, identified as STO Atuahene James of Metro-Koforidua, sustained injuries while fighting the fire and was rushed to the Eastern Regional Hospital for treatment.

He said that when the Police visited the officer at the hospital on October 4, 2026, at about 14:30 hours, he was stable and responding to treatment.

He said calm had since been restored, while investigations continued to determine the cause of the fire.

Ghana News.title: EOCO returns Hanan’s £6,700, GH¢2,750 and devices after defence challenge
Ghana News.content:
The Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) has returned £6,700, GH¢2,750, two laptop computers and at least six mobile phones seized from former Ghana Buffer Stock Company CEO Hanan Abdul Wahab Hanan, his wife, Hajia Faiza Wuni, and their driver.

The three are standing trial in a financial crimes case involving allegations of offences against the state.

Some of the items were seized during investigations in 2025, while the cash, one laptop and two mobile phones were seized on July 4, 2026, when Mr Hanan was arrested at the airport and detained for four days.

He had been due to travel abroad for medical purposes under a court order.

At the latest hearing on September 29, 2026, the prosecution indicated its readiness to call its first witness.

However, lead counsel for Mr Hanan, former Attorney-General and Minister for Justice Godfred Yeboah Dame, argued that the trial could not proceed unless the seized items were first returned.

He said the mobile phones contained information that was critical to the defence’s preparation for trial.

Mr Dame had filed a motion seeking an order compelling EOCO to release the items.

“The phones contain information necessary for the conduct of the trial and related to matters that are central to the subject matter of the proceedings.

"We need them to enable the first accused to prepare adequately for his defence, including raising objections to documents to be tendered by the prosecution, in accordance with Article 19(2)(e) and (g) of the 1992 Constitution,” he said.

Counsel for the second accused, Faizal Wuni, Augustine Obour, also told the court that his client had requested the release of her electronic devices.

He said the devices would form part of the basis of her defence.

The prosecution argued that the trial could proceed while the court determined the application for the release of the seized items.

The trial court, presided over by Justice Francis Achibonga, however, held that the prosecution could not commence its case or call its first witness until the application for the release of the phones and other property had been determined.

The court noted that counsel for the first accused might need access to the phones to adequately prepare his defence.

Following the proceedings, EOCO released the items to the accused persons on Monday, October 5, 2026.

Lawyers’ Petition Against EOCO

The return of the items follows a petition by lawyers for Mr Hanan, Messrs Dame & Partners, to the EOCO Executive Director, Raymond Archer, and the Attorney-General, Dr Dominic Ayine.

The lawyers asked the authorities to return what they described as their client’s property, which they said had been retained without legal justification.

According to the lawyers, when Mr Hanan reported to EOCO on July 9, 2026, to collect his belongings, he was handed an empty purse, a wristwatch and his boarding pass.

The lawyers said the investigating officer, Frank Cromwell, informed him that he had no authorisation to release the remaining items.

Those items, according to the petition, included two mobile phones and three envelopes containing £5,000, £1,700 and GH¢2,750.

“On 9th July 2026, when my client reported to EOCO to collect his items, he was handed an empty purse, a wristwatch and his boarding pass.

"The investigating officer, Frank Cromwell, reportedly informed him that he had no authorisation to release the remaining items, which included two mobile phones and three separate envelopes containing £5,000, £1,700, and GH¢2,750 respectively.”

Mr Dame said the cash belonged to his client and had been borrowed specifically to cover travel and medical expenses.

The defence also accused EOCO officials of violating Mr Hanan’s constitutional right to privacy.

The lawyers alleged that data on the two seized mobile phones was accessed without judicial authorisation on July 6 and July 7, 2026, while Mr Hanan remained in state custody.

They further argued that EOCO’s continued retention of his passport was contrary to a High Court order dated June 29, 2026.

According to the defence, the court had released the passport to facilitate his medical travel and directed that it be returned to the Registrar of the High Court upon his return.

The lawyers demanded a full account of the data allegedly accessed from the phones and threatened further legal action if the items were not released.

Withdrawal of Charges and Challenges to Prosecution’s Case

The return of the items comes against the backdrop of several developments in the prosecution of Mr Hanan.

In May 2026, the prosecution withdrew the initial charges against him before he was subsequently re-arraigned on new charges.

The prosecution also withdrew a significant portion of evidence previously presented to the court.

The new charges subsequently faced challenges from Mr Dame, who argued that aspects of the charge sheet were defective, leading to further amendments.

The latest dispute over the seized cash and electronic devices adds another development to the ongoing trial, as the prosecution prepares to present its case.

Ghana News.title: Opplift Youth Entrepreneurs Summit 2026 equips entrepreneurs with skills, mentorship and support
Ghana News.content:
The maiden Opplift Youth Entrepreneurs Summit 2026, an initiative of Opplift, took place on Friday at the British Council Auditorium in Accra.

The Summit, held under the theme "Build to Thrive: Equipping Young Entrepreneurs for Success in Ghana,” brought together vibrant young entrepreneurs, business leaders, industry experts, and key stakeholders in Accra to explore practical ways to build sustainable businesses and create economic opportunities for young people in Ghana.

The summit was designed to move beyond conversations about entrepreneurship by providing participants with practical knowledge, insights, mentorship opportunities, and exposure to support systems to help them build and grow sustainable businesses.

The summit seeks to curb persistent youth unemployment in Ghana by making the development of entrepreneurial skills and sustainable businesses an important part of the country's economic development agenda.

The programme commenced with a welcome message from Kris Asleson, Founder of Opplift, followed by opening remarks from Nana Mensah, Team and Country Lead for Opplift, which set the tone for a day focused on practical entrepreneurship and youth empowerment.

In their address, they both highlighted the potential young talents possess and the need to support and equip them with available resources and mentorship to help them build sustainable businesses.

The first session featured Guest Speaker Ekow Mensah, who urged entrepreneurs to become intentional about how they use their time and resources while recognising the value of their skills.

Among the key lessons shared were the importance of avoiding relationships and activities that do not contribute to one's purpose, understanding the value of time, mastering the art of selling and knowing when to engage professionals to handle specialised aspects of a business.

The second session focused on “Effective Use of Social Media by Startup Businesses” and was delivered by Stephen Naasei Boadi, a seasoned Marketing Consultant.

The session examined how startups can use social media more effectively as a tool for visibility, communication, customer engagement and business growth.

The third session featured a panel discussion involving business leaders and industry experts such as Richard Ohene Sika, Fashion Educationist and Talent Manager, Josephine Toudeka, Founder of Toudeka’s Enterprise and Eugene Wilson Ocran, Programs Manager at Opplift, who shared their entrepreneurial experiences and insights into the opportunities and challenges associated with building businesses in Ghana.

The panel session, moderated by Ms Valerie Danso, enabled panellists to share their journeys, challenges, and tips on what it takes to move from starting a business to building one that survives and grows.

A major highlight of the summit was the unveiling of 12 young beneficiaries selected to receive seed funding, logistical support, and mentorship to establish their ventures.

This intervention reinforces Opplift’s belief that youth entrepreneurship must be supported with practical resources and guidance if young people are to build sustainable livelihoods and contribute to job creation.

Beyond the summit, the event also created an avenue for young entrepreneurs to network, exchange experiences and connect with individuals and organisations within Ghana's entrepreneurial ecosystem.

The summit will be held annually, with subsequent editions continuing to provide young entrepreneurs with access to practical knowledge, mentorship, skills development, and opportunities to support business growth.

For Opplift, the objective is clear: youth entrepreneurship should not only inspire young people to start businesses but should equip them to build businesses that can survive, grow and create opportunities for others.

The success of the maiden summit therefore marks the beginning of a broader effort to support hardworking young people with the tools and opportunities needed to lift themselves out of poverty and contribute to Ghana's economic growth.

The summit was held with support from Immix Law Group, Flyrise, Launchava, Patch Pro and the Council of Entrepreneurs.

Ghana News.title: Rival clubs want range of punishments for Man City
Ghana News.content:
Manchester City CEO Ferran Soriano (left) and chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak have continued to insist the club are innocent despite the guilty verdicts

A number of Premier League clubs want Manchester City to face both "retrospective punishments" and future sanctions for their mass financial rule-breaking, sources have told BBC Sport.

An independent commission found City guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

City have appealed against the verdict, while the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) is poised to review the findings to determine whether there are any indications of potential misconduct.

However, there is said to be a consensus among a group of top-flight club executives that if City's appeal is unsuccessful, the sanctions should make reparations for the period when they broke the rules, while also limiting their powers in future.

There is also a feeling from at least four Premier League boardrooms that a "one-hit" points deduction resulting in relegation to the Championship would be an insufficient punishment given the severity of City's wrongdoing.

There is an understanding that there is nuance in exactly what clubs consider a fitting penalty for the eight-time Premier League champions, who were found guilty of all serious financial rule breaches in a damning verdict by an independent commission.

One senior club source said City should be stripped of their titles, and added there was "no great rush" among clubs to push for the redistribution of trophies, but rather to take honours away and leave them vacant.

The source warned that the Premier League's credibility would be lost if City were allowed to keep the eight major trophies they won during the period they were found guilty.

However, in a sign of a range of opinions across the league, BBC Sport was previously told there was little appetite among other clubs for City to be stripped of titles.

Regarding the timescale for future sanctions, there is concern among club executives that a sanction applied to just one season would merely provide City with a "bump in the road," given the likelihood of their returning to the Premier League at the first opportunity.

A number of Premier League figures therefore believe any points deduction should be split over multiple seasons, while there is also a sense that transfer bans spanning multiple windows would significantly hinder City's ability to regain their top-flight status as quickly as possible.

One club source also said it would be "bizarre, almost obtuse" if City were able to trade in the upcoming January transfer window, if this process is ongoing and sanctions have not been applied.

Some clubs cited feeling "in the dark" regards the Premier League, including around the chronology and timescales of the appeal and the sanctions hearing.

However, sources said there was "empathy" and "understanding" about the difficult position the Premier League is in, given the gravity of this situation and the ongoing legal process.

Regarding financial reparations, one idea that has been mooted - and which a club source found "merit" in - was to apply a "tariff-based system", whereby City's past league finishing positions would be altered via a points deduction.

Rival clubs could then be paid compensation by City based on where they would have finished versus where they did finish.

BBC Sport understands that Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca will speak to players collectively after they return from international duty on Thursday, before their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday (16:30 BST).

The trip to Anfield is their first game since the verdict was announced.

Merseyside Police says it has received queries in relation to the match, and when asked by BBC Sport if any special measures would be put in place the force said it will have "an appropriate policing operation in place on the day".

Sources at Liverpool have told BBC Sport that it is a case of "business as usual" and that no extra measures are being put in place. Conversations and meetings between the club, supporters and relevant authorities take place before every home game.

One source said while everyone "has the right to express their feelings" they hoped supporters would not overstep the mark.

Ghana News.title: Tear gas in Paris and Marseille as school protests grow across France
Ghana News.content:
Hundreds of thousands of people have taken to the streets across France, as a wave of protests by high-school pupils spread to their parents, university students and unions.

Crowds of teenagers marched from the Place de la République in Paris, calling for more resources for schools, and what they called less repression from police.

Police clashed with demonstrators in Lyon, used tear gas in Paris and Marseille and water cannon in Rennes, but there was little of the serious trouble that marred previous protests.

Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu condemned the earlier violence and said since the protests had begun, 215 students and 85 staff had been hurt, as well as 715 police officers.

The government said there had been disruptions in 891 high schools on Tuesday, almost a quarter of all lycées, and that more than 250,000 demonstrators had taken to the streets during the day.

Students' unions put the number at 450,000, and said the number of high schools blockaded was 1,800 on what the protesters dubbed "Act Three" of their movement.

In Marseille, thousands of demonstrators moved around this city, stopping momentarily to chant before moving on as police changed direction.

A group of masked protesters grabbed bollards and bins and tried to barricade themselves off from police. Riot officers fired tear gas, and the protesters dispersed.

"Most of us aren't violent," said Alissa, a student in Marseille. "We're going to the streets because they've closed our schools... schools are falling apart."

Her friend, Sacha, said the ceilings in Marseille's schools were leaking and conditions were generally rather poor, "so we can't really work a lot of time". "We will keep doing this until good measures are taken," he added.

In parliament, the prime minister accused the radical-left France Unbowed (LFI) party of seeking to "sow chaos" ahead of presidential elections in seven months' time.

President Emmanuel Macron is nearing the end of his second and final term in office, and LFI leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon is currently runner-up in the opinion polls behind Marine Le Pen of the hard-right National Rally.

Macron was due to chair a meeting with ministers at the Élysée Palace on Tuesday evening to assess the situation.

Education Minister Édouard Geffray said that from the start he had appealed for dialogue rather than school blockades and complained that "ultra-violent elements infiltrated the high-school student movements".

He is now under pressure to respond to the students' demands. What has been offered, including a website for students to express their grievances and an afternoon of internal discussion in schools on Friday, has made little impression so far.

There seems little chance of the protests coming to an end just yet. France's biggest union, the CGT, has said that further protests involving school and university students are being planned for Thursday.

The protests began in mid-September but have spread to high schools across France

There is widespread concern over allegations of "disproportionate force" by police, and France's IGPN police inspectorate has been investigating a number of cases.

One police officer who fired a tear-gas grenade at a high school student at Saint-Ouen-l'Aumône, north-west of Paris, last week has now been charged by prosecutors with "violence... resulting in mutilation or permanent disability".

Eden, 14, was part of a group blockading the Château d'Épluches lycée for 15-18-year-olds when he was hit in the face. His lawyer said he suffered a fractured jaw, and that his upper teeth were broken and four of his lower teeth were gone.

On Monday, a 15-year-old's hand was torn off after a so-called anti-encirclement grenade was fired in unclear circumstances near a school in the northern city of Lens.

Authorities say he picked up the "sting ball" grenade which then exploded, but students allege he was hit directly after an officer fired.

The grenade is considered a non-lethal weapon and the local prefect has said the incident took place when police were confronted by a group of 200-250 students throwing stones and fireworks.

What began with local anger at overcrowded classrooms, a lack of teaching staff and dilapidated school buildings in the northern Paris suburb of Seine-Saint-Denis in mid-September has since spread across the country, and extended to some universities too.

Late on Tuesday, the French interior ministry said a total of 6,547 had been stopped or arrested by police since 28 September.

Tuesday's protests drew people of all ages. One couple in their 70s, Alain and Michèle, joined the march in central Paris, to show their support for young students, explaining that as former teachers they understood the problems that France's education system was facing.

"We are the grandparents of three students who are all mobilised. They have protested peacefully in front of their respective high schools in Paris in recent days, but they were still tear-gassed," Alain told the BBC, his voice trembling.

Ghana News.title: Kane inspires England to win over Czech Republic in UEFA Nations League
Ghana News.content:
Harry Kane celebrates after scoring against the Czech Republic on his record-equalling 125th appearance for England

Harry Kane celebrated his record-equalling 125th England cap with two goals in a comfortable UEFA Nations League victory against the Czech Republic at Wembley.

Kane made it a remarkable tally of 91 goals for England on the night he drew level with Peter Shilton - and is now firmly on course to become the first player to reach a century for his country.

England built on the win against the Czech Republic in Prague and the outstanding 7-0 victory in Croatia with another convincing display to delight head coach Thomas Tuchel and the home support.

Kane had a hand in England's opener after 27 minutes, when his cross was turned into his own net by former West Ham United defender Vladimir Coufal.

The goal Kane and Wembley craved came five minutes before the break, England's captain applying a simple close-range finish to Morgan Rogers' excellent first-time delivery.

And Kane was on target again after 57 minutes, rising at the far post to head home Lewis Hall's corner.

Kane departed to a well-deserved standing ovation when he was replaced by Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the closing minutes.

England show signs of progress

England's Uefa Nations League campaign may have started with defeat against World Cup holders Spain at Wembley but three subsequent victories, all achieved in convincing fashion, hinted at progress and optimism.

Indeed, it could have been four wins from four had Kane scored the penalty that would have put England 3-1 up against Spain before the lost 3-2, but head coach Tuchel will have been highly satisfied with what he has seen since.

England, after winning 7-0 in Croatia, were a threat again against the Czechs at Wembley, although Eberechi Eze failed to make the most of his opportunity with in-form Anthony Gordon rested.

Tuchel's attacking force is now set in stone, led by captain Harry Kane, with Gordon and Bukayo Saka on either side and Jude Bellingham stamping his world-class in the number 10 position.

Trent Alexander-Arnold took his chance at right-back after being recalled by Tuchel following his World Cup exclusion, looking solid in defence - albeit not under huge pressure - while offering an extra dimension in attack.

Newcastle United's Hall now has strong claims to be first-choice left-back, while Jarell Quansah impressed with his versatility at right-back then in central defence against the Czechs, cementing his place as a vital part of Tuchel's squad.

England face Croatia next in November before their biggest test, away to Spain, but they have foundations to build on.

And it was fitting that Kane marked the night when he equalled that caps record with two goals, capping a pleasing international break for Tuchel and England.

Ghana News.title: Finland orders halt to work on two Google data centres
Ghana News.content:
One of Google's data centres is being built in Muhos, Finland

Finnish authorities have ordered a halt to building work at two planned Google data centres amid concerns over the clearance of more than 300 hectares of forest.

The sites form part of Google's record €13bn (£11bn; $15bn) investment in Finland, announced less than a month ago and described by the company as its largest single investment in Europe.

The Finnish Supervisory Agency (LVV) said work at one site was carried out without a mandatory environmental impact assessment and ordered measures that would "significantly alter the environment" to be suspended by 23 October.

Google said it had "fallen short of our own high standards in this instance" and would follow the agency's guidance.

The orders relate to preparatory work carried out at the planned data centre sites in Muhos and Kajaani.

According to LVV's head of environment Tommi Muilu, work at the sites included the removal of trees and topsoil, the construction of site roads and storage areas, and changes to ditches.

Tuike Finland, the company behind Google's data centre projects, has been asked to provide an explanation and set out how it intends to proceed by 14 October. The agency said it could begin "enforcement proceedings" if the company failed to comply with its demand.

Hanna Halmeenpaa, chair of the Finnish Association for Nature Conservation, had previously told the AFP news agency that "nature sites which should be preserved" had been felled. The conservation group had previously called for work to be halted while the environmental requirements were examined.

In a statement to the BBC, Google said: "We understand the concerns and have fallen short of our own high standards in this instance."

It said it had "acted in good faith under the Forestry Act", carried out nature surveys and put measures in place to protect areas of high environmental value.

"As we continue our long-term work in the region, we are advancing our landscaping and biodiversity plans, which include tree planting across 130 hectares at Muhos," the company added.

Google announced last month that it would invest at least €13bn (£11bn; $15bn) in Finland over 2027 and 2028. Its plans included new data centres in Kajaani, Muhos and Vaala, alongside investment in its existing facility in Hamina.

The company said the infrastructure would help it meet growing demand for services including Search, Maps and its AI assistant Gemini.

Google said the construction phase in 2027 and 2028 would support more than 37,000 jobs and contribute an average of €3.6bn a year to Finland's economy.

As part of its expansion, Google also signed a 22-year power purchasing agreement with Finnish energy company Fortum covering up to half the capacity of the Loviisa nuclear power plant. Fortum said the agreement would help support the plant's continued operation until 2050.

Finland has attracted growing interest in data centres, with its cool climate and low-carbon electricity among the factors making it attractive to developers. Lower temperatures can also reduce the energy required to cool facilities filled with computer servers.
