World.title: Sudan’s al-Burhan rejects talks, vows to retake all territory from RSF
World.content:
At least 10 civilians were killed in West Kordofan and 5,500 displaced in Blue Nile as clashes widened on Tuesday.

Share Sudan’s al-Burhan rejects talks, vows to retake all territory from RSF on social media

Sudan’s military chief, Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, has promised to seize “every inch” of territory under the control of the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), rejecting negotiations to end three and a half years of war.

Al-Burhan made the comments on Tuesday while addressing a gathering in Village 5, located in the northern Sudanese locality of Merowe, according to the Sudan News Agency.

He said the “military option” would continue until the RSF was removed from Sudan.

The Sudanese army and the RSF have been fighting since April 2023 after leaders of the groups fell out over plans to integrate the paramilitary force into Sudan’s army. The conflict has killed tens of thousands of people and displaced around 13 million, according to UN and international estimates.

Al-Burhan’s pledge to continue fighting came as 10 civilians were killed and several others were wounded in an attack by the RSF in Sudan’s West Kordofan state, according to a local charity group.

In a statement, the Dar Hamar Emergency Committee accused the RSF of multiple violations against civilians in Abu Ajal village in the southeastern countryside of En Nahud.

The RSF has been massing in West Kordofan as Sudan’s army advances towards the cities of En Nahud and Al Khuway after gains in neighbouring North Kordofan.

In Sudan’s Blue Nile state, more than 5,500 people were displaced from villages over three days amid deteriorating security, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) said on Tuesday.



Meanwhile, an envoy of US President Donald Trump said Sudanese parties must take the lead in talks to end the war.

In a post on X on Monday, Massad Boulos, the US senior adviser for Arab and African affairs, said peace could be achieved “through an inclusive Sudanese-owned and Sudanese-led national dialogue, transition toward a civilian-led government”.

The US State Department said last month that neither the Sudanese Armed Forces, the RSF, nor their respective leaders “represent legitimate, constitutional governance for Sudan”.

World.title: South Sudan’s aid crisis deepens as food stocks run low
World.content:
More than one million people could lose life-saving aid by October as funding shrinks and arrivals from Sudan continue.

Renk, South Sudan – The arrivals begin before dawn. Women carry children and plastic bags; men walk with almost nothing. Every week, about 3,000 refugees and returnees cross into South Sudan from Sudan.

Many arrive hungry, exhausted and with little or no money. But the food assistance they depend on is also running out.

More than one million vulnerable people could lose access to life-saving food and nutrition assistance by October unless additional resources are secured, according to the World Food Programme (WFP).

In Malakal, one of the agency’s key logistics hubs in the Upper Nile state, food stocks have fallen from 10,000 metric tonnes at this time last year to less than 300 tonnes now. The drop comes as humanitarian agencies face shrinking resources while needs continue to rise, WFP says.

WFP assistant executive director Matthew Hollingworth visited Renk and Malakal in Upper Nile and Pigi county in Jonglei state this month, where he witnessed firsthand the pressures facing communities already struggling with conflict, displacement, hunger and climate shocks.

Hollingworth told Al Jazeera that the war in Sudan had driven up prices and put additional pressure on a country already stretched by the influx of refugees.

“The war in Sudan has been catastrophic for the north of this country. Prices have gone so much higher due to the complexity of importing goods from Sudan,” he said. “Moreover, the influx of refugees [comes] to a country that is really stretched when it comes to helping them.”



In Renk, Hollingworth saw the effects of drought alongside areas still affected by flooding.

“It all comes at the time when the international community has a lot less to give, and we don’t have the same resources we used to have,” he told Al Jazeera.

“On the other side, the government of South Sudan has to consider the issue of illegal checkpoints that prevent us from being able to get everywhere. We need to reach vulnerable people across the country.”

Peter Maker, a displaced person in Pigi, said insecurity and the arrival of people displaced from other areas had made it difficult to farm or find work.

“We face major challenges due to national insecurity and an influx of people from other areas. Our main issues are insecurity and lack of access to farmland,” he told Al Jazeera.

“Although I am able-bodied and qualified to work, insecurity prevents me from travelling for opportunities or farming safely outside, leaving us heavily reliant on the UN and aid.”

Maker said longer-term solutions were needed and warned that further cuts or blockages to assistance would be devastating. He attributed much of the local suffering to political leadership and divisions between communities, while saying people currently survive by sharing resources, relying on God and receiving occasional aid.

A border under pressure

Renk, in Upper Nile state near the border with Sudan, has become a major entry point for people fleeing the war that erupted there in April 2023.

More than 1.4 million refugees and returnees have crossed into South Sudan since the war erupted in Sudan in 2023, according to the World Food Programme. Many arrive after journeys marked by checkpoints, extortion and violence, with little idea of what comes next.

Zainab Musa, a mother of six staying at a transit centre in Renk, recently crossed from Sudan. She said conditions were difficult and there was little food.

“The humanitarian situation is hard and there is nothing to eat, just hunger,” she told Al Jazeera. “I thought of moving from the border at Jodha to the transit centre to look for help.”

Musa said she planned to travel to her grandfather in Bunj, in Maban county, in Upper Nile.



The transit centres in Renk were not designed for the scale of arrivals they are now receiving. Families wait for onward transport to Malakal or other parts of South Sudan, while some remain for months.

The WFP has been forced to reduce rations and cut support as funding has dried up.

In August, the WFP and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) warned that more than 650,000 refugees and asylum seekers were at risk of losing food assistance. They said food and nutrition assistance for the most vulnerable 240,000 refugees was expected to run out in September without additional funding.

Nura Mohammed Ahmed, a Sudanese refugee, said hunger and a lack of adequate nutrition were already taking a heavy toll at the transit centre.

Malakal’s fragile refuge

Malakal has hosted families displaced by conflict and disaster for years.

The former Protection of Civilians site, redesignated as an internally displaced people’s settlement earlier this year, hosts nearly 40,000 displaced people across more than 6,000 households. Many have been displaced for years.

But basic services are also coming under pressure.

The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has warned that water, sanitation and hygiene services in Bentiu and Malakal are at risk because of funding shortfalls. Without drainage pumping and dyke maintenance, Malakal also faces a heightened risk of flooding during the rainy season.

Najah al-Tayieb al-Fadhul, a Sudanese refugee and mother of four, arrived at a transit centre in December 2023 after her husband was killed.

“My husband was killed by the Sudan armed forces in front of me, and I could not stay with my kids there because the situation was traumatising,” she told Al Jazeera.

“I entered South Sudan, and I have tried my best to hustle and earn some small job with the humanitarian organisations based in Renk.”

Al-Fadhul said hunger, sickness and malnutrition were part of daily life.

“There are massive cases of hunger, sickness and malnutrition among the children,” she said. “Even my child has a heart disease, and I cannot afford to treat him.”

She said she sometimes earned about $2.50 a day from work in the market, but struggled to find stable employment despite having a college degree.

“The humanitarian situation is worsening despite securing a job with one of the organisations,” she said. “WFP only helped us here with the small ration for the children in particular. Elders and most individuals lack energy to work due to hunger.”

The funding gap

The WFP says it faces an immediate $86m funding gap and a $416m shortfall over the next six months, threatening its ability to assist refugees, displaced people and vulnerable host communities.

For the wider population, the hunger crisis is already severe. The WFP says 7.8 million people, more than half of South Sudan’s population, face high levels of acute food shortage, while 2.2 million children are acutely malnourished.



The WFP’s current South Sudan emergency response also lists a $258m funding shortfall for the remainder of 2026.

For people arriving from Sudan, the crisis continues after they cross the border.

Nura Mohammed Ahmed put the choice facing some refugees in stark terms: “Many people died here because of hunger and lack of nutrition. There’s nothing, or food that can give us strength. The only solution is to return to war-torn Sudan despite the risks, or die here from hunger.”

World.title: French mayor tear-gassed after shielding protesters from police
World.content:
NewsFeed French mayor tear-gassed after shielding protesters from police

Saint-Denis Mayor Bally Bagayoko was tear-gassed after shielding student protesters from riot police. Police used water cannon and tear gas against demonstrators in Paris and Lyon, which drew tens of thousands of people demanding better funding for French high schools.

World.title: Electric car bursts into flames at charging station in Turkiye
World.content:
NewsFeed Electric car bursts into flames at charging station in Turkiye

Turkiye’s first domestically produced electric SUV, the Togg T10X burst into flames at a charging station. No one was injured and the operator says the car was not charging when the fire started. EVs reportedly accounted for 52% of new car sales in Turkiye so far this year.

World.title: ‘We are desperate’: Venezuela’s power cuts fuel growing public anger
World.content:
The hum of the kidney dialysis machine that Onasis Munoz is connected to suddenly stops. The fluorescent lights overhead flicker out, and his room at a clinic in Valencia, Venezuela, is plunged into darkness.

It is not the first time a power cut has interrupted one of the three weekly sessions Munoz needs to do the work his failing kidneys can no longer do, filtering waste and excess fluid from his blood.

For years, electricity would go out every couple of days across parts of Venezuela's Carabobo state.

But in recent months, Munoz said, the outages have grown to be daily, lasting around seven hours. The clinic's emergency batteries have since been depleted, and its backup generator no longer works.

He explained that the frequent power failures have disrupted his treatment. His health has slumped as a result.

"I arrive home, exhausted, as if I had run a marathon," the 34-year-old said.

But often there is no electricity there either, and recent weeks have been sweltering. "I can't switch on the air conditioning. I cannot rest because of the heat and the mosquitoes. There's no relief," Munoz said.

Across Venezuela, the prolonged outages are riling locals, as the electricity supply to homes, businesses and essential services becomes unstable.

Some of the cuts are deliberate, as the government of interim President Delcy Rodriguez rations electricity.

The resulting frustration has spilled onto the streets, where demonstrators hold "cacerolazos" – a traditional form of protest that involves banging pots and pans.

Some have gone as far as blocking roadways and setting tyres on fire. The electricity crisis has also raised concerns about how the government is managing the country's vast oil supply, a key source of income for the country.

"We are desperate. We cannot understand how a country so rich in resources can be practically left in the dark," said Patricia Cueva, a lawyer from Maracaibo, the capital of oil-rich Zulia state.

"We cannot rest. We cannot work. Our children cry."

World.title: Christa Pike lawyers say she is speaking one week after failed execution
World.content:
The 50-year-old has regained consciousness and is receiving care nearly one week after being sent to the hospital following a botched lethal injection.

Share Christa Pike lawyers say she is speaking one week after failed execution on social media

Lawyers for Christa Pike say she is awake and able to speak after her botched execution attempt by the state of Tennessee on September 30.

Tuesday’s statement marks the first public indication that Pike’s condition has improved after she was transported to a Nashville hospital after receiving two doses of pentobarbitol, lethal injections intended to end her life.

Her failed execution has sparked debate about the use of the death penalty in the United States. Pike is thought to be the first person to have survived such an injection in the country.

“Against all odds, Christa Pike is conscious, speaking, and continues to receive critical medical care,” Pike’s lawyers said in a statement.

“Despite the severe damage she endured to her arms, she is still handcuffed and shackled to the bed. Her recovery is medically unprecedented. Her prognosis remains unclear but, at a minimum, we expect a long recovery.”

The statement also expresses gratitude to medical workers who the lawyers say have “treated Christa like a human and have provided exceptional care to her”.

Pike’s lawyers had previously stated that she was unconscious and on a ventilator. They described her arms as “swollen, burned and blistered” by the failed execution.

Pike was convicted and sentenced to die in 1996 for her participation in the murder of a classmate, Colleen Slemmer, when she was 18 years old. Two co-defendants received lesser sentences.

Pike’s defence lawyers had pointed to her mental health struggles in their attempts to commute her sentence. But the Slemmer family had advocated for the death penalty, pointing to the violent nature of the 19-year-old’s murder.



Accounts of Pike’s failed execution describe her kicking off the sheet covering her body and, at one point, appearing to snore. She reportedly expressed feeling pain as the lethal injections were administered.

The incident has brought attention to the prevalence of botched executions in the US criminal justice system.

Critics have argued that botched executions — defined as those that deviate from established procedures through unforeseen issues, delays or administrative incompetence — can cause unnecessary pain and suffering for those being put to death.

Citing the researcher Austin Sarat, the Death Penalty Information Center, a nonprofit, estimates that 3 percent of executions in the US from 1890 to 2010 were botched.

World.title: Fans flood Buenos Aires ahead of Messi’s final international match
World.content:
NewsFeed Fans flood Buenos Aires ahead of Messi’s final international match

Thousands of Argentina fans poured into Buenos Aires’ Monumental stadium ahead of Lionel Messi’s final international match. The World Cup-winning captain and Argentina’s all-time leading scorer is ending a 21-year international career, saying it’s time for a new generation.

World.title: Houthis, Saudi-led forces claim victories as Yemen fighting rages on
World.content:
NewsFeed Houthis, Saudi-led forces claim victories as Yemen fighting rages on

Saudi Arabia’s Jazan and Najran airports were attacked as Saudi-led gov’t forces launched air strikes on Houthi sites in Yemen and claimed control of the Bab al-Mandeb strait. Houthi officials say the Iran-backed group maintains ‘firm control’ over recently captured territory.

World.title: US death row inmate Christa Pike awake and speaking after failed execution, lawyers say
World.content:
Dr Joel Zivot, an anaesthesiologist advising Pike's defence team, said on Tuesday that the likelihood of recovering from lethal injection is low.

"Most people who get lethal injection die from it," he told the BBC. "In fact, pretty well everyone, except Christa. So, the fact that she survived it ... was unusual."

But there remains a lot of uncertainty and many unknowns, he said, including how much of the pentobarbital got into her system, what her blood levels were after the injection and what her recovery will look like.

"I would not, in any way, say at this point that all the big risks are behind her," he noted.

Zivot had previously said the two doses of pentobarbital she received last week would have been enough that, had it entered her bloodstream in normal circulation, "she would have surely died".

Instead, Zivot said a possible explanation is that instead of entering Pike's bloodstream, the pentobarbital was more likely to have spread across the tissue under her skin.

Zivot said last week he thought her ending up with a brain injury was "very possible", due to the delays in resuscitating her. He also believed it would take about a week to truly understand her condition and do a neurological exam. It's now been six days since the failed attempt to execute her.

Pike's lawyers previously warned that her medical history and anatomy - including thrombocytosis (a blood-clotting condition) and small veins - meant there was a risk she would experience "unnecessary" pain and suffering during a lethal injection.

They said on Tuesday that she has endured "severe damage" to her arms.

In 2022, more than a third of executions across the US were botched or highly problematic, according to the Death Penalty Information Center, which tracks information about such cases.

For lethal injections, such incidents have typically occurred due to difficulty obtaining reliable IV access to the veins, though the underlying reason differs from person to person.

In cases the centre has documented, all failures happened before the lethal drugs could be administered. The last failed lethal injection that was tracked happened earlier this year - also in Tennessee.

The execution of Tony Carruthers, who was convicted of kidnapping and murdering three people in 1994, was postponed in May after staff were unable to find a vein for a lethal injection. He was granted a year's reprieve by the governor.

World.title: Tear gas in Paris and Marseille as school protests grow across France
World.content:
Hundreds of thousands of people have taken to the streets across France, as a wave of protests by high-school pupils spread to their parents, university students and unions.

Crowds of teenagers marched from the Place de la RÃ©publique in Paris, calling for more resources for schools, and what they called less repression from police.

Police clashed with demonstrators in Lyon, used tear gas in Paris and Marseille and water cannon in Rennes, but there was little of the serious trouble that marred previous protests.

Prime Minister SÃ©bastien Lecornu condemned the earlier violence and said since the protests had begun 215 students and 85 staff had been hurt as well as 715 police officers.

The government said there had been disruption in 891 high schools on Tuesday - almost a quarter of all lycÃ©es - and said more than 250,000 demonstrators had taken to the streets during the day.

Students' unions put the number at 450,000, and said the number of high schools blockaded was 1,800 on what the protesters dubbed "Act Three" of their movement.

In Marseille, thousands of demonstrators moved around this city, stopping momentarily to chant before moving on as police changed direction.

A group of masked protesters grabbed bollards and bins and tried to barricade themselves off from police. Riot officers fired tear gas, and the protesters dispersed.

"Most of us aren't violent," said Alissa, a student in Marseille. "We're going to the streets because they've closed our schools... schools are falling apart."

Her friend, Sacha, said the ceilings in Marseille's schools were leaking and conditions were generally rather poor, "so we can't really work a lot of time". "We will keep doing this until good measures are taken," he added.

World.title: Former German spy chief arrested for espionage and treason
World.content:
Former German spy chief August Hanning has been arrested on suspicion of espionage, treason and obtaining classified information for a foreign power, the German Federal Prosecutor's Office says.

Hanning headed the Federal Intelligence Service (BND) from 1998 to 2005 and has since been working as a private consultant.

Prosecutors allege that he used classified intelligence to "draft an analysis" for one foreign intelligence service and maintained contact with another foreign spying service. Investigators have not disclosed which foreign powers were involved.

Police also arrested former BND employee Manfred D, accusing him of passing Hanning about 2,000 classified documents for money.

Manfred D, who was Hanning's bureau chief and remained in the BND until this year, is charged with aiding and abetting attempted treason and treasonous espionage.

Local media reported Hanning was arrested at his home in Nordwalde near MÃ¼nster while Manfred D was arrested in Bavaria. Hanning is due in court on Wednesday and Manfred D will appear on Tuesday.

Prosecutors say Manfred D, who also served as the chief of staff for Hanning's successors between 2012 and 2026, used his role to gain access to highly confidential information which he then passed on to Hanning "in exchange for remuneration".

"The current findings suggest that, over the years, Manfred D provided Hanning with approximately 2,000 documents, many of which contained classified information to be used exclusively by the Federal Intelligence Service for internal purposes," the statement says.

"On one occasion, Hanning used classified intelligence ... to draft an analysis for an officer of a foreign intelligence service," prosecutors said, noting it was not clear if "the material reached the intended recipient".

Hanning is also accused of being "in close contact with a representative of another foreign intelligence service, to whom he passed on political information, partially based on material provided by Manfred D, for several years".

Local media say Hanning's alleged possession of intelligence documents came to light during a separate case relating to German steakhouse heiress Christina Block.

Hamburg public prosecutor's office accused Block of orchestrating the kidnapping of her two youngest children in 2023 due to a custody dispute. Investigators allege Hanning was involved in an earlier attempted kidnapping of the children, which he denies.

State criminal police officers reportedly discovered an electronic data storage device containing sensitive information including recent BND documents.

It is not the first time the BND has faced similar controversy. A high-ranking German intelligence officer was charged with treason in 2023 for allegedly passing state secrets to Russia.

Prosecutors alleged Carsten L shared intelligence about the war in Ukraine and the Wagner mercenary group and received roughly â¬400,000 ($450,000; Â£340,000). His trial is ongoing.

World.title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows
World.content:
A sharp increase in human activity is having an impact on the way a Himalayan bird lives and communicates, two studies by Indian researchers have found.

The monal, a pheasant native to Himalayan mountain forests, is deeply woven into the region's cultural, folklore and identity. The eye-catching monal - the male has distinctive green, blue and copper feathers - is the state bird of India's Uttarakhand state and the national bird of Nepal, reflecting its cultural significance across the Himalayas.

But studies show that infrastructure development and tourism are squeezing its habitat, while increasing noise is altering how it communicates with potential mates and rivals.

Researchers from Uttarakhand conducted two separate studies over five years which flagged key threats to the bird.

One study found that the birds are forced to move higher in the mountains as their natural habitat in the alpine meadows above the tree line get crowded. The other says the monal is changing its pitch to cut through human noise in a busy valley.

"These two studies give a useful warning for other more vulnerable species - if the monal is forced to change both its voice and its address, how are the more sensitive species responding?" says Vishal Singh, an environmental practitioner working on ecology and climate issues in the Himalayas.

Dr Rajeev Lochan, lead researcher of both studies, told the BBC that they chose to study the monal as the bird has a narrow habitat range - it moves seasonally between the lower montane zone - an ecological belt found on the lower slopes of the mountains - and high-elevation alpine zones. This, he says, makes it a key indicator of ecosystem health in the north-western Himalayas.

"If the species is facing issues on this particular landscape, there might be a chance that the ecological disturbances are affecting other birds too," said Lochan.

World.title: Lawyer for one of Cornell 7 calls for special prosecutor to be removed over previous comments
World.content:
A lawyer for one of the seven men accused of participating in a Cornell University gang rape has called for the special prosecutor on the case to recuse herself over past public comments.

The lawyer had said a social media post from New York Attorney General Letitia James throws into question her investigation's "integrity and independence".

In the 28 September post, James wrote that "what this young woman has been forced to endure is horrific and unacceptable" and told survivors that "we stand with you".

The university's administration is under fire over its alleged mishandling of the October 2024 incident and, according to US media, now faces a no-confidence vote by Cornell faculty.

The university's Faculty Senate, a governing body comprised of professors and other academic staff, will vote on a resolution of no confidence next week, according to reports. Cornell is an Ivy League university, alongside Harvard and Yale, and its faculty includes Nobel laureates and other distinguished researchers.

A majority no-confidence vote would be a largely symbolic gesture, signalling the broader faculty's discontent and applying pressure on university leadership to act.

Cornell University announced on Tuesday that it was hiring Sally Yates, a former deputy attorney general, to lead an independent review of the university's practices and procedures on sexual assault and related conduct.

"Yates and her team will conduct a detailed review of the University's response to the allegations involving Jane Doe", the university said in a statement, "including whether Cornell followed its policies and procedures in responding to the matter".

Allegations made in a lawsuit against seven men and the university have rocked the campus in New York state, with hundreds of students and faculty members gathering there on Monday in protest, and sparked anger across the country.

World.title: Finland orders halt to work on two Google data centres
World.content:
Finnish authorities have ordered a halt to building work at two planned Google data centres amid concerns over the clearance of more than 300 hectares of forest.

The sites form part of Google's record â¬13bn (Â£11bn; $15bn) investment in Finland, announced less than a month ago and described by the company as its largest single investment in Europe.

The Finnish Supervisory Agency (LVV) said work at one site was carried out without a mandatory environmental impact assessment and ordered measures that would "significantly alter the environment" to be suspended by 23 October.

Google said it had "fallen short of our own high standards in this instance" and would follow the agency's guidance.

The orders relate to preparatory work carried out at the planned data centre sites in Muhos and Kajaani.

According to LVV's head of environment Tommi Muilu, work at the sites included the removal of trees and topsoil, the construction of site roads and storage areas, and changes to ditches.

Tuike Finland, the company behind Google's data centre projects, has been asked to provide an explanation and set out how it intends to proceed by 14 October. The agency said it could begin "enforcement proceedings" if the company failed to comply with its demand.

Hanna Halmeenpaa, chair of the Finnish Association for Nature Conservation, had previously told the AFP news agency that "nature sites which should be preserved" had been felled. The conservation group had previously called for work to be halted while the environmental requirements were examined.

In a statement to the BBC, Google said: "We understand the concerns and have fallen short of our own high standards in this instance."

It said it had "acted in good faith under the Forestry Act", carried out nature surveys and put measures in place to protect areas of high environmental value.

World.title: Kenya confirms its first Ebola death as outbreak spreads
World.content:
Kenya has confirmed its first ever case of Ebola - a Kenyan citizen who has been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo for the past seven years.

Health Minister Aden Duale said the patient, who fell ill a month ago, and was treated in several hospitals in DR Congo, died days after arriving in the capital, Nairobi.

Duale said the patient boarded a flight on Saturday and underwent normal public screening at the main airport in Nairobi before he was transferred by a relative to a hospital in the city.

Kenya's health ministry says it has since stepped up surveillance at airports and border crossings.

More than 4,000 people have died from Ebola in DR Congo this year, in what is the second most deadly known outbreak of the disease.

Shortly after DR Congo declared an outbreak of Ebola in May, it was also reported in Uganda, where two people died. However, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared that county free of the disease in August.

Since then, all known cases of the highly infectious disease have been in DR Congo.

The virus spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.

World.title: AfD candidate elected speaker of German regional parliament for first time
World.content:
A month after Germany's far-right AfD scored a decisive victory in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt, the party's candidate Tobias Rausch has been elected as parliament speaker there too.

Not since World War Two has a far-right party secured the post of speaker, and protesters outside the building in Magdeburg held up banners saying, "Never again is now".

Although the AfD fell three seats short of a majority in last month's election, Rausch, 35, comfortably won Tuesday's vote with the support of 9 MPs from other parties.

"The days of political firewalls should be a thing of the past," Rausch said after the vote, rejecting a post-war consensus in German politics not to work with the far right.

This was the first time since last month's state vote that Saxony-Anhalt's newly elected representatives had gathered in parliament, and regional Greens party leader Susan Sziborra-Seidlitz said "a line has been crossed" with the election of a far-right speaker of parliament, and it was a watershed moment.

"We will not let ourselves be intimidated, and we will not sit by when rights are curtailed either here or for people in the state," she said.

The AfD is considered pro-Russian and anti-immigrant, with plans to segregate child refugees in schools, as well as intolerant towards the LGBT community.

Within Saxony-Anhalt it is also classed as "right-wing extremist" by domestic intelligence, a description rejected by party leaders. Until now its members have sat on the right fringe of the state parliament, but ahead of Tuesday's inaugural session it successfully argued that it should now sit in the centre.

World.title: Police arrest suspected kidnappers who collected ₦10.3 million ransom
World.content:
The police in Rivers State have arrested two suspected members of a six-man kidnapping syndicate who allegedly collected a ransom of ₦10.3 million for the release of a kidnap victim.

Operatives of the Violent Crime Response Unit (VCRU-AKU) arrested the suspects following an intelligence-led operation, the police said.

The police identified the suspects as Victor Ifeanyi, 24, alias Big Boby, from Aguleri Community, Otuocha Local Government Area of Anambra State, and Aniekan Michael, 36, alias Duff Man, from Ikot Ukpor, Essien Udim Local Government Area of Akwa Ibom State.

The state police spokesperson, Blessing Agabe, disclosed this in a statement posted on Facebook on Monday.

According to the police, the victim, identified as Mr Hassan, a resident of Rivers State, was abducted on 6 September 2026 near Fidelity Bank, Garrison, Port Harcourt.

The kidnappers allegedly took him to Igbugulu Waterside, Borikiri, Port Harcourt, where he was held captive for three days.

The police said the victim was released after his relatives paid a ransom of ₦10.3 million.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Police launch investigation

The command said it received credible information about the abduction on 7 September and immediately deployed operatives of the VCRU-AKU to investigate the incident.

The intelligence-led operation subsequently led to the arrest of the two suspects.

“Preliminary investigation revealed that the suspects confessed to their alleged involvement in the operation,” the police said.

The suspects reportedly told investigators that the gang consisted of six members and that they used a white mini-bus, popularly known as a Keke bus, during the operation.

The police said efforts were ongoing to arrest the four other members of the syndicate.

READ ALSO: Police commissioner in Bayelsa orders crackdown on cult groups

Police intensify anti-kidnapping operations

The arrests come amid other recent police operations against suspected kidnappers in Rivers State.

In one recent case, police arrested four suspected kidnappers and rescued an abducted woman in the state. This newspaper reported that the operation was part of efforts by security agencies to dismantle kidnapping networks operating in the region.

In another operation, police rescued a kidnap victim and apprehended a suspect, PREMIUM TIMES reported.

The Police Commissioner in the state, Olugbenga Adepoju, urged residents to provide credible information that could help the command identify and arrest criminal elements.

Mr Adepoju assured the public that the command would treat such information in confidence.

He said the command would continue to deploy intelligence-led operations to disrupt kidnapping syndicates and other criminal networks across the state.

The commissioner also urged residents to remain calm and cooperate with security agencies.

World.title: PNC 2026: NCDMB, DMG affirm collaboration with Bayelsa govt, unveil new activities
World.content:
As preparations intensify for the 2026 edition of the Practical Nigerian Content (PNC) Forum, slated for 30 November – 3 December 2026, the Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board (NCDMB) and its partner, DMG Events, have strengthened their long-standing collaboration with the Bayelsa State Government, to ensure seamless hosting of the flagship industry gathering.

This commitment was affirmed on Tuesday during a strategic engagement between officials of NCDMB and DMG Events with the Deputy Governor of Bayelsa State, Peter Pereotubo Akpe, at the Government House in Yenagoa.

The meeting was convened to appreciate the State Government for its close partnership in convening the PNC over the past 15 years and to solicit continued assistance for the 15th edition, which will hold at the NCDMB Conference Centre, Yenagoa, Bayelsa State.

Leading the delegation to the meeting, General Manager, Corporate Communications Division, NCDMB, Obinna Ezeobi, highlighted the economic impact of the PNC Forum, as well as other NCDMB’s activities and programmes in Bayelsa State.

He conveyed the appreciations of the Executive Secretary of NCDMB, Felix Omatsola Ogbe to the Bayelsa State Government for its significant contributions to the PNC, particularly in hosting the opening banquet and supporting the Youth PNC segment, which exposes young persons in the Niger Delta region to emerging opportunities in the oil and gas industry and core competencies for successful careers in other key sectors of the economy.

Ezeobi also alluded to new initiatives introduced for the 2026 PNC Forum, designed to invigorate the conference and enhance value for participants, while Senior Manager, Zonal Coordination, NCDMB, Mr Adebayo Joseph, spoke on plans for the Youth PNC.

Leader of the DMG team, Ms Olamide Oloko, outlined the main PNC programme and the new ideas such as the Local Content Roundtable for November 30 and the twoday programme for Local Community Contractors (LCCs), to help scale their operations.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Other innovative initiatives at this year’s PNC include the breakout session, designed to gather stakeholders’ perspectives that will shape the trajectory of Nigerian Content over the next decade, and the Townhall Session with key industry leaders, including the Executive Secretary of NCDMB, the Group CEO of NNPC Ltd, the Chief Executive of NUPRC, the Chairman of OPTS, and the Chairman of PETAN.

In his response, Deputy Governor Akpe pledged Bayelsa State’s continued collaboration, assuring delegates of adequate security and reaffirming the State’s tradition of hosting the gala dinner and actively participating in the main conference as well as the Youth PNC. He commended NCDMB for integrating some participants from the 2025 edition of the Youth PNC into its capacitybuilding programmes, and demanded for increased participation of senior oil and gas industry officials in the welcome gala dinner.

The Practical Nigerian Content Forum, hosted annually by NCDMB and DMG Events, serves as a strategic platform to review and track local content implementation and chart new directions for investment and growth in Nigeria’s oil and gas industry. The 2026 edition is expected to deepen collaboration, strengthen local participation, and enhance value retention across the sector.

World.title: Otti mourns Abia-born Squadron Leader Man-Ugwueje, commiserates with FG over plane crash
World.content:
The Governor of Abia State, Alex Otti, has expressed deep sadness over the death of Abia-born Squadron Leader Ahamefule Aham Man-Ugwueje, one of the pilots of the Nigerian Air Force ATR-42 aircraft, NAF 931, which crashed in Igbokoda, Ondo State, on Monday, 5 October.

In a statement on Tuesday by Ferdinand Ekeoma, his special adviser on media and publicity, Mr Otti described Squadron Leader Man-Ugwueje’s death and those of other military personnel aboard the Nigerian Air Force plane as painful and devastating.

According to the Governor, “This accident is both painful and devastating, because it has brought untold sorrow and anguish to the victims’ families, their friends and loved ones, the Nigerian Air Force, and the nation at large.”

Governor Otti regretted that Squadron Leader Man-Ugwueje perished in the air disaster just about two weeks after he wedded his beloved wife, Flight Lieutenant Damilola Adekunle, in Abuja, a sad development that has robbed the couple of the opportunity to spend their lives together as husband and wife.

Governor Otti, on behalf of his family, the Government and people of Abia State, sends his deepest condolences to the families of the victims, the people of Umuahia where Squadron Leader Man-Ugwueje hailed from, the Nigerian Air Force and the Federal Government of Nigeria, and prays for the peaceful repose of their souls in God’s bosom.

World.title: Nigeria has reduced reliance on oil revenue – Tinubu
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu says Nigeria has significantly reduced its reliance on oil revenue as his administration pushes to diversify the economy and attract more investment into other sectors.

He said the government would continue to develop the petroleum industry but use its resources to support broader economic activity rather than depend on crude oil as the main driver of growth.

The President, represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima, spoke on Tuesday in Abuja at the fifth anniversary of the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC).

“We have already reduced our dependence on oil revenue, and we intend to go further,” President Tinubu said.

He said the government’s diversification strategy was focused on agriculture, manufacturing, digital and creative industries, while the oil and gas sector would continue to provide energy, foreign exchange and revenue for the country.

The claim comes as the administration continues to pursue reforms aimed at increasing oil production, improving revenue remittances and attracting fresh investment into the petroleum sector.

In February, President Tinubu issued an executive order directing oil and gas revenues due to the Federation to be paid directly into the Federation Account.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The order also ended certain deductions previously retained by NNPC Limited, including a 30 per cent management fee on profit oil and profit gas.

Oil remains important to Nigeria’s finances

Despite the government’s push to reduce dependence on oil, petroleum remains an important source of public revenue and foreign exchange.

The sector has, however, faced challenges including fluctuations in crude production and oil prices, as well as security and operational problems.

PREMIUM TIMES reported in March that oil and gas revenue remittances had fallen significantly below projections in the first two months of 2026. While N937.10 billion was budgeted as oil and gas revenue for the period, actual remittances stood at N137.41 billion.

President Tinubu said improved security and cooperation among oil producers, host communities, security agencies and the NUPRC had helped stabilise production.

He said the government’s efforts had also helped attract investors who previously left Nigeria, adding that the country had ranked first among Africa’s leading destinations for upstream investment for two consecutive years.

Push for more oil and gas investment

The Minister of State for Petroleum Resources, Oil, Heineken Lokpobiri, said Nigeria currently produces about 1.7 million barrels of crude oil per day and has more than 37 billion barrels of oil reserves.

Mr Lokpobiri said more investment, additional licensing rounds and increased exploration were needed to unlock the country’s petroleum resources.

The NUPRC has also reported increased investment activity in the upstream sector.

In August, the regulator said it had approved more than $57 billion in Field Development Plans since 2024, with 22 major offshore projects expected to come on stream between 2026 and 2030. The projects are estimated to attract between $30 billion and $50 billion in investment.

Nigeria’s oil and condensate reserves stood at 37.01 billion barrels as of January 2026, while gas reserves increased to 215.19 trillion cubic feet, according to NUPRC data.

Tinubu declares decade of gas

President Tinubu said gas would be central to the government’s energy strategy, describing the period ahead as a decade of gas.

“With the largest gas reserves in Africa, we will expand gas supply for power, industry and clean cooking, reduce flaring and methane emissions, and grow renewable energy alongside it,” he said.

He added that the government would pursue an energy transition suited to Nigeria’s circumstances, arguing that the country should meet its climate commitments without compromising energy access and economic development.

He also noted that a stronger upstream industry could create jobs for Nigerian engineers, fabricators and oilfield service companies.

President Tinubu said the Petroleum Industry Act had provided a foundation for reforms in the sector but noted that legislation alone could not guarantee investment.

According to him, investors had raised concerns about high costs, lengthy contracting processes and uncertainty around fiscal terms for complex projects.

He urged the NUPRC to maintain clear regulatory processes, provide reliable timelines and work with other government agencies to reduce overlapping requirements.

The President also said operators benefiting from government incentives must meet their obligations on work programmes, local content, environmental protection and host communities.

He urged the commission to remain independent and accountable in its regulatory decisions.

World.title: What I’ll do with my ₦90m cash prize — BBNaija season 11 winner Temi Nkem
World.content:
Big Brother Naija Season 11 winner, Temi Nkem, has revealed how she plans to spend and invest her ₦90 million cash prize after winning the “Show Ya Sef” edition of the reality television show.

Temi won the finale with 25.87% of the votes, defeating Aikou, who finished as first runner-up with 23.68%, while Sheba placed third with 9.80%. Her victory made her the fifth female winner in Big Brother Naija history.

Her ₦160 million prize package includes ₦90 million in cash, a brand-new SUV and other sponsored prizes. The cash prize was reduced from the original ₦100 million after ₦10 million was allocated to the season’s Most Influential Player of the Week (MIPOW) fund.

Temi said she plans to invest a substantial portion of the money, support her parents, complete her university education and set aside some money for herself.

Investment

Speaking in an exclusive interview with PREMIUM TIMES at the official prize presentation ceremony in Lagos on Tuesday, the Accounting and Finance student said she had already started thinking about how to divide the money before leaving the Big Brother house.

“I will be investing a very big sum of my money because obviously, if everybody already knows, I already said that I studied a degree in Accounting and Finance, and I took an extra degree called Treasury.

“So, yeah, that’s finance. So I know how to work with my money. And honestly, I want to get my money to grow. I’m going to finish my uni. I’m going to go back to my studies,” she said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The London-born Nigerian added that she would support her parents with part of the money while also allowing herself some personal enjoyment after her 70-day stint in the reality show.

“I’m also going to give my parents, and then obviously I’m also going to spend on myself. I need a little treat for myself. I need a holiday. I do, a few,” she said.

‘I thought I wouldn’t win’

Reflecting on her victory, Temi said she did not expect to win the competition, particularly because of perceptions surrounding housemates who were born or raised abroad.

She said comments from people who told her that contestants from abroad rarely win the show made her lower her expectations.

“It shows you that you have a chance. Coming into the show, if you guys heard it a lot of times, people were telling me that people who come from abroad don’t really win the show. You might not have a chance.”

According to her, the perception only strengthened her resolve to enjoy the experience and remain true to herself.

“So that dawned on me. So as I was hearing that, I was thinking, you know what? Might as well have my fun.

“Still, the show was called ‘Show Ya Sef’, so I might as well still show myself. So that’s what I did. And guess what? I still won,” she said.

Temi, who was born and raised in London before coming to Nigeria, said her victory should encourage young Nigerians who may feel that their background could prevent them from succeeding.

“If that is not determination to you guys, courage for you guys to do this, just do whatever you want to do. Do whatever you put your heart on. Keep doing what you need to do. Pray, everything. You’ll be sorted. You’ll be good,” she said.

‘70% was me, 30% the game’

Temi also addressed how much her behaviour in the house was part of a deliberate strategy.

According to her, much of what viewers saw was her personality, not a carefully constructed game plan.

“I would say maybe 30 per cent was a game, 70 per cent was actually me genuinely being curious,” she said.

She explained that she often asked questions in the house because she genuinely wanted to understand situations, rather than because she was deliberately creating a character for the cameras.

However, she admitted that she also understood the importance of not appearing too threatening to her fellow housemates.

“In the house, I didn’t want anyone to think I was a threat,” she said.

Temi said she sometimes doubted whether viewers would keep supporting her, especially because she believed she spent a lot of time sleeping and relaxing in the house.

“I really thought I was boring, I’m not going to lie. But guys, I was giving you guys quality content. But yeah, it doesn’t stop here. It only starts.

“I thought I was Sleeping Beauty,” she joked. “I thought I was sleeping a lot, waking up, going to the arena, sleeping again. I thought you guys hated that. But it seems like you guys were still finding something.”

Biggest moment

Asked which moment from her time in the house she would like to relive, Temi immediately pointed to her victory in the betPawa Friday Night Arena Game.

The 21-year-old said she entered the competition simply intending to participate and give her best, without expecting to win.

“I feel like that was my own bonus, and I felt amazing after that. I went, I screamed, I told everybody that I got them,” she said.

Temi said the experience helped change her perception of what she was capable of achieving in the house.

House relationships

Temi also reflected on the friendships and romantic situations that became part of her BBNaija story.

She identified Bluethopia, Bells, Shibi, Godessa and Araga among the housemates with whom she developed genuine connections, although she acknowledged that some friendships developed later in the competition.

She also addressed her much-discussed relationships with Barry, Kivo and Tram.

According to Temi, she initially found Barry attractive but stopped pursuing the connection after she felt he was not taking enough initiative in their conversations.

She said she was also attracted to Kivo when he entered the house but eventually became frustrated by what she described as his attempts to tell her what she should or should not do.

On Tram, whose relationship with Temi drew significant attention during the season, she said she was physically attracted to him but did not develop romantic feelings for him.

“I’ve been telling the people that I’m here for fun,” she said.

Beyond BBNaija

Temi said her immediate plans include returning to her studies and building a future around finance, while also exploring opportunities created by her new public profile.

She revealed that although her university studies are in the UK, she can complete the programme online.

“I do want to stay here for a minimum of two years. See what Africa has for me. See what Nigeria has for me. Build on that. And the sky’s the limit. I got good content, good vlogs,” she said.

Temi was crowned winner of Big Brother Naija Season 11 on Sunday, 4 October, after 70 days in the house. Her victory earned her the ₦160 million grand prize package, comprising ₦90 million in cash, a brand-new SUV and other sponsored prizes.

The ₦90 million cash component and the SUV were formally presented to her at the prize-giving ceremony in Lagos on Tuesday.

World.title: Russia 3-3 Nigeria: Late Akor Adams goal rescues Super Eagles
World.content:
The Super Eagles fought back from two goals down to secure a 3-3 draw against Russia in an entertaining international friendly at the Nizhny Novgorod Stadium on Tuesday.

Nigeria looked set for another disappointing result after Russia established a 3-1 lead early in the second half, but the Super Eagles produced a spirited late comeback to rescue a draw.

Kelechi Iheanacho put Nigeria ahead after 10 minutes, giving the Super Eagles an early advantage.

Russia responded through Lechi Sadulaev in the 30th minute before Matvey Kislyak completed the hosts’ turnaround with a goal in first-half stoppage time.

The hosts extended their advantage nine minutes into the second half when Aleksei Miranchuk found the net to make it 3-1.

Nigeria, however, refused to surrender and continued to push forward in search of a way back into the contest.

Their persistence paid off in the 78th minute when Peter Edokpolor reduced the deficit to 3-2, setting up a tense finish.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Super Eagles then completed their remarkable comeback deep into stoppage time when Akor Adams scored in the 94th minute to level the scores at 3-3.

The draw gives Nigeria a measure of redemption after their recent 3-0 defeat to Guinea-Bissau and ends the international window with the Super Eagles showing character to recover from a difficult position.

Russia, who had entered the game on the back of a 6-0 victory over Namibia, will be disappointed to have surrendered their two-goal advantage.

For Nigeria coach Eric Chelle, the match provided another opportunity to assess his squad, while the late fightback offered encouragement ahead of the team’s next competitive assignments.

World.title: Kenya confirms first imported Ebola case linked to DRC outbreak
World.content:
Kenya has confirmed its first imported case of Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus, as the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to spread across the region.

According to a statement published Tuesday by the World Health Organisation (WHO) Regional Office for Africa, the patient was a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the DRC and fell ill there.

The patient travelled by road to Kampala, Uganda, before flying to Nairobi, where the patient was isolated after developing symptoms. Samples tested positive for Bundibugyo virus at Kenya’s National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute.

Despite supportive care, the patient died on the night of 5 October and was buried on Tuesday in line with Kenya’s Ebola safe and dignified burial protocol, according to WHO.

“The government of Kenya notified WHO of the case in line with the International Health Regulations (2005) on 6 October 2026,” it noted.

Kenya becomes fourth country affected

According to WHO, Kenya is the fourth country to confirm a case of Bundibugyo virus disease in the current outbreak.

The DRC continues to battle the largest outbreak, while Uganda, where the virus was first detected in 2007, ended its latest outbreak in August. France also reported a travel-related case in June.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

WHO noted that most of the cases reported in Uganda were imported from the DRC, while a smaller number were locally acquired among contacts and health workers linked to imported cases.

In the DRC, the outbreak has continued to expand. As of 23 September, the country had recorded 7,890 confirmed cases and 3,799 deaths, giving a case fatality ratio of 48.1 per cent.

The outbreak had affected 63 health zones across seven provinces, with two of the latest affected areas bordering other countries. WHO said the expansion had increased the risk of cross-border transmission.

Kenya traces contacts

Following confirmation of the case, Kenyan health authorities have listed 28 contacts, including family members and health workers who cared for the patient.

They are also tracing 23 passengers and four crew members who were on the same flight as the patient.

WHO said Kenya had been on high alert since May, when Ebola outbreaks were declared in the DRC and Uganda.

As of Tuesday, Kenya had screened more than 652,000 travellers entering the country, tested 267 suspected samples and trained about 5,000 health workers on Ebola prevention and management.

WHO said it has also supplied about 1,000 Ebola tests and 1,000 personal protective equipment kits to high-risk counties in Kenya.

Nigeria on high alert

Nigeria has also strengthened surveillance in response to the regional outbreak.

The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) said in a public health advisory issued in September that the country was on high alert and had activated enhanced surveillance measures.

It introduced a health declaration system under which travellers from countries with active or relevant Ebola transmission may be required to complete a form before boarding.

The form requires travellers to provide information about their recent travel history, transit countries, destination in Nigeria and health status.

The NCDC said the measures are intended to strengthen surveillance and prevent the importation of Ebola into Nigeria.

World.title: Police commissioner in Bayelsa orders crackdown on cult groups
World.content:
Police Command in Bayelsa State has ordered intensified operations against cultism and cult-related violence across the state as part of efforts to sustain peace and prevent killings and reprisal attacks.

This is contained in a statement signed by the command spokesperson, Musa Muhammad, a deputy superintendent of police, on Monday.

The Commissioner of Police, Adewale Ajao, directed divisional police officers and tactical commanders to increase patrols in vulnerable areas, identify emerging threats and act promptly on credible intelligence concerning planned clashes, initiation ceremonies and recruitment activities.

The directive, according to the command, is part of renewed efforts to prevent killings, cult clashes and retaliatory attacks and to sustain peace across Bayelsa.

Mr Ajao directed police formations to increase patrols in flashpoint areas, strengthen intelligence gathering and act swiftly on credible information concerning planned cult clashes, initiation ceremonies and recruitment activities.

The commissioner also ordered closer engagement with community leaders and other stakeholders to enable the police detect emerging tensions before they escalate into violence.

The command warned cult groups contemplating attacks or reprisals that the police would pursue not only those who carry out such acts but also individuals who finance, organise or facilitate them.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It also declared that there would be “no sacred cows” in the ongoing crackdown, stressing that the law would be applied without regard to an individual’s status, influence or connections.

According to him, anyone reasonably suspected of organising, financing, facilitating or participating in cult-related crimes would be investigated, while suspects against whom sufficient evidence is established would be prosecuted before the appropriate court.

The police also drew the people’s attention to the Bayelsa State Secret Cults/Societies and Similar Activities (Prohibition) Law, 2012, as amended in 2018, which prohibits membership and sponsorship of secret cults and prescribes criminal penalties upon conviction.

The command warned residents against taking the law into their own hands following any cult-related attack.

READ ALSO: Police in Akwa Ibom probe alleged extortion of operatives by commanders

The police urged the public to avoid reprisal attacks, harbouring suspects and spreading unverified information capable of inflaming tensions.

“Parents and guardians are also advised to closely monitor their children and wards and warn them against being lured into cult groups.

The police called on residents, community leaders and other stakeholders to provide timely intelligence on planned attacks, recruitment drives, initiation ceremonies and other suspicious activities.

“The message from the Command is clear: report threats before they become bloodshed. Do not wait for violence to erupt before speaking up.

“Members of the public are encouraged to report suspicious activities or imminent threats to the nearest police station or contact the police command.”

(NAN)

World.title: Lagos to deepen creative industry support — Hamzat
World.content:
Hamzat

By Olasunkanmi Akoni

Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, has pledged continued government support for the creative industry through skills development, expanded training opportunities and provision of infrastructure to drive the sector’s growth.

Hamzat spoke on Tuesday at the official commissioning and grand opening of Euphoria360 Hub, established by actor and filmmaker Femi Adebayo, in Oregun, Lagos.

He said the state was committed to developing a sustainable pipeline of skilled creative professionals capable of competing and earning in the global market.

According to him, Lagos has no shortage of creative talent but needs the right structures and opportunities to harness its potential.

“The state is already investing in creative infrastructure, which includes the development of theatres in Ikorodu, Badagry, among other divisions.

“Besides, the government is exploring further opportunities to expand training in areas such as filmmaking, acting, photography and other creative disciplines, as well as training up to one million Lagosians across various fields,” he said.

The deputy governor said the government’s focus should go beyond training young people to creating a sustainable pipeline of globally competitive talent and linking skills development directly to employment opportunities.

He said the objective was to create an enabling environment where creative professionals could showcase Nigerian culture to the world while earning commensurate economic value from their work.

Citing the growing global influence of Nigerian films and storytelling, Hamzat said the country’s productions had become an important means of projecting Nigeria’s identity and culture across Africa and beyond.

“I want to challenge you, our elders and stakeholders in the creative industry, to identify the major barriers limiting growth and work with the government to develop practical solutions, particularly in areas such as intellectual property, contracts and skills development,” he said.

Hamzat congratulated Adebayo, the Chief Executive Officer of Euphoria360, on the establishment of the mega audio-visual project, describing it as an important contribution to the growth of Lagos’ creative ecosystem.

Also speaking, Special Adviser to the President on Media and Public Communication, Mr Sunday Dare, described Nigeria’s entertainment industry as a powerful force that had significantly enhanced the country’s visibility and global influence.

Dare said government needed to support and strengthen the creative sector, noting that the industry had significant economic potential and could create jobs for a large number of young people.

Earlier, Adebayo said the vision behind Euphoria360 Hub was to establish a one-stop facility where producers, filmmakers, creators, film enthusiasts and event planners could access quality facilities and professional services needed to bring their projects to life.

He said the hub was designed to bring everything required to produce and deliver world-class projects under one roof, adding that it would become a landmark destination for creativity, collaboration and excellence in the entertainment industry.

Adebayo said the facility brought together key players across the entertainment value chain while providing access to modern facilities and professional services needed to develop and deliver world-class productions.

World.title: NSITF exposes fake recruitment scam, cautions Nigerians against fraudsters
World.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA —The Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF) has issued a public warning over the spread of fraudulent employment s and forged appointment letters being used by scammers to deceive job seekers.

The warning was contained in a public notice issued by the Fund and circulated to regional and branch managers via a memorandum dated October 5, 2026, signed by Samaila Abdu, Esq., Executive Director, Administration.

According to the notice, the NSITF said it is not currently recruiting for any position and described employment s circulating on social media, particularly Facebook, as fake

The Fund stated that the fraudulent s reflect a growing trend of individuals and groups falsely claiming to represent the NSITF in recruitment exercises.

NSITF urged members of the public to disregard such s and avoid making payments to anyone over purported employment opportunities.

The Fund emphasised that it neither charges fees for employment nor conducts recruitment through unofficial social media platforms or channels.

It added that any genuine employment opportunities would be announced through its official channels.

“Stay alert, stay safe,” the Fund urged, advising members of the public who encounter suspicious recruitment s or requests to avoid responding and report them to the appropriate NSITF authorities.

As part of measures to protect the public and safeguard the integrity of its recruitment process, NSITF management has directed all Regional and Branch Managers to prominently display the public notice at strategic locations within their offices.

The directive covers reception areas, main entrances and exits, notice boards, SERVICOM desks and other conspicuous locations accessible to staff and members of the public.

The Fund said the notice should be displayed immediately and kept visible to ensure that members of the public are adequately informed and protected from fraudulent recruitment activities.

NSITF urged Nigerians, particularly job seekers, to exercise caution and verify every recruitment claim through the Fund’s official communication channels before taking any action.

The development comes amid growing concerns over fraudulent online recruitment schemes targeting unemployed Nigerians with promises of government jobs in exchange for money or personal information.

NSITF’s latest warning underscores the need for job seekers to remain vigilant, as legitimate public-sector recruitment does not require applicants to pay individuals or unofficial agents for employment.

World.title: 50-year-old murder suspect slumps, dies during trial in Bayelsa
World.content:
A 50-year-old murder suspect, Bethlehem Nwanlia, reportedly slumped and died shortly after proceedings began at the Bayelsa State High Court in Yenagoa on Tuesday.

Nwanlia was standing trial alongside two other defendants over alleged conspiracy, kidnapping and multiple murder when the incident occurred at Court 11.

He reportedly collapsed in the court’s holding area shortly after Justice Amadise Michael Ekadi adjourned judgment in the case to October 27, 2026.

According to people who witnessed the incident, Nwanlia suddenly clutched his chest before collapsing.

Officers of the Nigerian Correctional Service, police personnel and lawyers reportedly attempted to revive him, but their efforts were unsuccessful.

A medical personnel was subsequently called to examine him, after which his body was taken to a hospital for further confirmation.

The Bayelsa State Judiciary’s Public Relations Officer, Mr Enoch Okunobo, confirmed the incident to newsmen on Tuesday evening.

He said the deceased’s body had been deposited at the Federal Medical Centre (FMC) mortuary.

“Somebody collapsed and died today. He was a murder suspect, who had been coming to court. His corpse has been deposited at the Federal Medical Centre (FMC),” Okunobo said.

Nwanlia and the two other defendants were facing allegations linked to the 2022 killing of three people in Kalaba community, Yenagoa Local Government Area of the state.

The allegations against the defendants had not been finally determined by the court before Nwanlia’s death.

Reports also indicated that the deceased had experienced health complications while in custody.

However, authorities had yet to establish the cause of his death as of the time of filing the report.

The incident reportedly caused confusion among court officials, lawyers, security personnel and others present at the court premises.

When contacted, the Bayelsa State Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Musa Mohammed, said he was not aware of the incident.

Mohammed, however, promised to make inquiries and revert, but had yet to do so as of the time of filing the report.

World.title: Christa Pike awake, talking after botched execution attempt – Report
World.content:
This handout picture dated January 12, 2023 provided by the Tennessee Department of Correction shows convicted US murderer Christa Pike. A US court on September 30, 2026, halted the execution of Pike shortly before she was due to die from lethal injection, three decades after she murdered a classmate. The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals issued a last-minute ruling to stay until further notice the execution of Christa Pike, in what would have been the first execution of a woman in Tennessee in more than 200 years.
