World.title: Mayor from Colombia’s north claims De la Espriella’s armed men intimidated him
World.content:
The mayor of Sincelejo claimed Sunday that armed men intimidated him during a meeting with Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella.

In a video message, Sincelejo Mayor Yahir Acuña said that armed men positioned themselves behind him while the president accused the mayor of corruption and threatened to pull municipal funds.

The accusations were partly published on the social media pages of the president, who accused Acuña of being “a person who, like you, faces 13 corruption charges, has a video in which he explains how to embezzle funds from the PAE, and, on top of that, is set to stand trial in the Supreme Court of Justice on charges of illicit enrichment.”

So let’s see what we do with Sincelejo, but I do not work under your scheme of corruption. And if you think you can continue engaging in those practices, know that someone has arrived who is going to prevent it and that I am going to concentrate on it. This money, mister mayor, I will take care of it, and to take care of it I have to keep it away from your control. President Abelardo de la Espriella

In his response, Acuña claimed that De la Espriella’s video “has been edited and digitally manipulated.”

I ask you, please, to show the full video, where you can see how disciplinary and criminal codes are being violated in Colombia, where you can see how a mayor is being intimidated with rifles in the hands of civilians. How can a mayor be constantly flanked—for the entire duration of an event—by a person armed with a rifle, with the sole purpose of intimidating him? Sincelejo Mayor Yahir Acuña

Investigative journalist Laura Ardila said on social media platform X that sources from the province confirmed Acuña’s allegations.

Sources from the department who were present say—fearing they might be named—that they left the scene terrified. They claim that Acuña was indeed surrounded by heavily armed men in civilian clothing, that the president’s office was recording the entire time, and that, based on details like these, they believe it was a scene staged in advance to go viral. Journalist Laura Ardila

The mayor subsequently pointed out that the investigations into his alleged corruption existed before the presidential campaign, during which the De la Espriella campaign may have violated electoral laws, according to Acuña.

Among other things, the mayor said that he had been approached by De la Espriella’s parents to support the far-right president’s campaign and that local print shops may have received unreported campaign funds.

Since this needs to be clarified, mister President, it would be a good idea for the oversight agencies to investigate whether any printing shops in Sincelejo incurred campaign expenses that have not yet been reported to the National Electoral Council, whether there was campaign financing, and where that campaign financing came from, Mister President. Sincelejo Mayor Yahir Acuña

The mayor also pointed out that two members of the De la Espriella administration are being investigated on corruption charges and that the president had ties to the now-defunct paramilitary organization AUC.

The president has repeatedly used corruption allegations to target political enemies.

World.title: Colombia’s top corporate lobbyist resigns over reported tensions with president
World.content:
The director of one of Colombia’s most powerful business associations, Bruce Mac Master of the ANDI, resigned amid tensions with President Abelardo de la Espriella.

In a letter to the ANDI, Mac Master said that “it is time for me to step down from my role as head of the National Association of Entrepreneurs of Colombia.”

According to the former ANDI boss, “unexpected and troubling circumstances” made working for the association “particularly complex” and ‘multiple pressures have affected its ability to act freely and carry out its functions autonomously.”

In recent weeks, unexpected and troubling circumstances have arisen that have made the Association’s operating environment particularly complex, with potential adverse effects on its members and staff. Multiple pressures have affected its ability to act freely and carry out its functions autonomously. In the face of these challenges, I have sought to act with firmness and prudence, always prioritizing institutional channels and placing the interests of the ANDI above any personal considerations, in an effort to resolve this situation. Bruce Mac Master

Mac Master’s resignation followed news suggesting that De la Espriella instructed his cabinet of boycotting the ANDI chief.

According to political news magazine La Silla Vacia, the rift between the ANDI and the government was because De la Espriella’s law firm was never allowed to join the ANDI and the association’s donations in response to the august 10 earthquake bypassed the First Lady’s newly founded and very controversial foundation.

“The General Board of Directors, its Executive Committee, and I did everything in our power to facilitate a solution and create conditions that would allow the Association to fully fulfill its role, seeking to keep channels of dialogue open and to continue contributing,” but “all of those attempts were unsuccessful.”

I deeply regret this, because I have always believed in collective intelligence and in the need for the government, the private sector, and institutions to work together—even in the face of differences—with respect, independence, and a sense of national responsibility. We tried, but we were unsuccessful. Bruce Mac Master

Mac Master said that he hoped that his resignation would restore “collaboration between the national government and the business community—as represented by the General Board of Directors, the members, and the various divisions of the Association.”

The former ANDI chief had been trying to represent the business interests of its approximately 1,600 members since 2013.

World.title: Colombia seeks to tighten checks on public protests
World.content:
Colombia’s government published a draft decree that seeks to tighten regulations on public protests.

The draft was published weeks before labor unions and social organizations plan regional anti-government protests ahead of a national strike that is set for November.

The draft seeks to update the Decree #3 of 2021, which was issued months before a national strike that was violently repressed by the police and the military.

In an attempt to prevent another bloodbath, the decree seeks to regulate authorities’ response to protests and the coordinated use of force in response to acts of vandalism and violence.

The decree regulates dialogue between the protesters and law enforcement authorities to promote the peaceful nature of protests.

The decree additionally limits the use of police intelligence against those organizing and participating in the protests.

Last but not least, the decree seeks the effective prosecution of those arrested during protests through increased surveillance and a permanent police presence.

The decree comes amid social tensions that surged after the far-right President Abelardo de la Espriella took office in August and announced counterrevolutionary measures that seek to undo reforms by his leftist predecessor, former President Gustavo Petro.

Swelling student protests have been publicly accused of being fueled by insurgencies and De la Espriella has warned that police may enter universities if they find evidence they are used to prepare acts of vandalism or terrorism.

World.title: Colombia breaks diplomatic ties with Iran
World.content:
Colombia’s Foreign Ministry said Thursday that it had broken diplomatic ties with Iran and designated the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organization.

The foreign ministry made the announcements in two separate statements that were published in its website.

In the first statement, the government claimed that the decision claimed to defend “national and hemispheric security, and the fight against transnational crime.”

According to the foreign ministry, the Iranian government has “alleged ties to international terrorist groups and other narco-terrorist groups that threaten [Colombia’s] security.”

Colombia also took into account the documented human rights violations committed by the Iranian government on its territory, the verified attacks against countries not involved in the Middle East conflict, the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, and the authorities’ obstruction of the International Atomic Energy Agency’s (IAEA) efforts to verify the scope of Iran’s nuclear program. Foreign Ministry

In regards to the IRGC, the foreign ministry claimed that the Iranian armed force “poses a serious threat to international peace and security” through “covert operations beyond Iran’s borders.”

“Colombia will strengthen its control and security measures to prevent individuals associated with the IRGC from entering its territory,” said the foreign ministry in a second statement.

In his 2017 book “Watch Your Backyard,” Foreign Minister Omar Bula claimed that “Iran and Islamic extremist groups such a Hezbollah and Al Qaeda have profusely penetrated Latin America.”

As part of his foreign policy, President Abelardo de la Espriella has renewed ties with the United States, Israel and the United Arab Emirates.

In a response, the Iranian government said that the accusations of the De la Espriella government go “against the principles of mutual respect” and damage both countries’ “interests and benefits.”

“It is clear that none of the arguments put forward by the Colombian government to justify this decision are valid or logical, and that this measure was adopted solely under the influence of the Zionist regime and the United States,” said Iran’s foreign ministry.

World.title: ACSN extends lockdown of Colombia’s Caribbean coast to Friday morning
World.content:
Santa Marta-based organized crime group ACSN said Wednesday that the lockdown it has imposed on parts of Colombia’s Caribbean coast will be lifted on Friday morning.

In its first formal statement, the ACSN said that “the armed strike announced for 72 hours will end at 7:00AM on Friday 25 September 2026.”

The lockdown, which was initially called for 48 hours on Monday, has devastated the legal economy in the port city, particularly after ACSN assassins uploaded videos of them opening fire at stores that ignored the order to social media.

The online videos and half a dozen burnt buses and taxis all but cleared the streets of Santa Marta, which became a ghost town on Tuesday.

“We have never seen anything like this,” one Santa Marta resident told news program El Reporte Coronell.

President Abelardo de la Espriella announced the militarization of Santa Marta, but this was barely visible in the city’s downtown area and in the majority of Santa Marta’s neighborhoods.

“There are no police or soldiers in the streets, the people feel unprotected and are in panic,” said journalist Javier Manjarres on social media platform X.

“The current situation is a consequence of the behavior of the security forces and the decisions taken by the National Government in regards to our organization,” the organized crime group said in their statement.

The ACSN admitted that the clandestine lockdown was the result of the killing of Jose Luis Perez, a.k.a. “Cholo,” one of its commanders in the region around the Sierra Nevada mountain range just outside the city.

According to the group, security forces executed Cholo in front of his wife after his arrest.

An 18-year-old farmhand with no ties to the organization was also executed by the security, his family told media.

The lockdown has been imposed throughout the Magdalena and La Guajira provinces, a region where the group dominates organized crime and controls drug trafficking route to the Caribbean.

World.title: Colombia withdraws support for ICJ genocide case against Israel
World.content:
Colombia has withdrawn its participation in South Africa’s genocide case against Israel, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) said Tuesday.

In a statement, the court in The Hague said that Colombia’s government “decided to withdraw the Declaration of intervention that it had filed… on 5 April 2024 in the case concerning Application of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide in the Gaza Strip.”

The decision of the administration of President Abelardo De la Espriella is part of a wider attempt to restore ties with Israel and its main sponsor, the United States, and appease its Evangelical Christian support base.

In response to the ongoing genocide in Palestine, former President Gustavo Petro took a leading role in diplomatic efforts that sought to isolate Israel and seek justice for Israel’s victims through the world court.

In a response, the US Government put Petro on a blacklist and actively campaigned for the election of De la Espriella to prevent another leftist victory in elections earlier this year.

The new president, who took office in August, immediately restored diplomatic ties to Israel and lifted a ban on coal exports to the country in West Asia.

World.title: ACSN crime group shuts down parts of Colombia’s Caribbean coast
World.content:
Santa Marta-based crime group ACSN shut down parts of the city and the surrounding region after Colombia’s armed forces killed one of their commanders.

Jose Luis Perez, a.k.a. “Cholo,” and six of his comrades were killed during an offensive on Monday.

The son of Fredy Castillo, a.k.a. “Pinocho,” who is one of the alleged bosses of the crime group, was reportedly among those killed during the operation.

Shortly after, a pamphlet that was signed by the ACSN ordered an “armed strike” of 48 hours because of the “the fierce attacks that the government has been launching against our organization in the Sierra Nevada since this afternoon.”

Multiple buses were incinerated in the region around Santa Marta.

We hereby declare a 48-hour armed strike throughout the province of Magdalena, particularly along the Troncal del Caribe highway, in the city of Santa Marta, and in the banana-growing region. We do not want any businesses to remain open for a period of 48 hours. ACSN

According to President Abelardo de la Espriella, who traveled to the city, “they are trying to intimidate the public by promoting an armed strike.”

“I will not allow any criminal organization to subjugate citizens through threats and terror,” the president added.

Notwithstanding, multiple shop owners in Santa Marta and along the highway kept their shops closed on Tuesday, afraid to challenge the authority of the local crime bosses.

The district government closed public schools in neighborhoods where the ACSN is believed to have a strong presence. Public transport was suspended as videos of armed men opening fire on shops that failed to close voluntarily were posted on social media.

The ACSN control much of drug trafficking to the port of Santa Marta and to the coastline of the neighboring La Guajira province.

De la Espriella ended attempts to negotiate the group’s surrender and ordered a military approach after taking office in August.

World.title: Colombia’s war crimes tribunal warns ICC that De la Espriella supports “worst attack in history”
World.content:
Colombia’s war crimes tribunal JEP said that it would warn the United Nations and the International Criminal Court about plans of President Abelardo de la Espriella to cut its budget.

In a statement, JEP president Alejandro Ramelli raised the alarm warned about a pending proposal by far-right Senator Enrique Gomez (National Salvation) to reduce the tribunal’s budget by COP100 billion ($31.6 million), which received De la Espriella’s support.

A second proposal by another far-right party, the Democratic Center, sought to push all sentences against members of the security forces to military justice for revision.

According to Ramelli, the two bill proposals “prove the existence of a strategy to block the JEP’s functioning” and called on the international community to “put a stop to this effort to dismantle our financial system and calls for the essential resources needed for our operations to be guaranteed.”

These initiatives constitute a combined strategy of economic strangulation and the subjugation of the JEP to military criminal justice. It is the most serious attack we have ever faced against our independence and autonomy. JEP president Alejandro Ramelli

The president , who vowed to get rid of the JEP on campaign, said that the 2027 national budget “does not constitute any threat to any judge, it’s the Constitution at work.”

I do not have a policy of retaliation against the JEP. I have a duty to manage spending, demand results, and allocate the State’s limited resources to a justice system that serves everyone, not to a court that part of the country perceives—for reasons debated in Congress and in public opinion—as a system of privileges rather than an effective end to impunity. President Abelardo de la Espriella

Since March of 2018, the JEP has played a key role in clarifying crimes committed during the armed conflict that erupted in response to the insurgency of the now-defunct guerrilla group FARC.

Among other things, the JEP found that the guerrillas recruited more than 18,000 children and that the security forces assassinated more than 7,800 civilians to inflate their combat kills.

Hundreds of former guerrillas and former members of the armed forces are taking part in a transitional justice system that seeks to solve as many as possible of the hundreds of thousands of crimes committed during the decades-long armed conflict.

World.title: British Airways restores non-stop London-Buenos Aires flights and adds a daily Santiago service
World.content:
British Airways restores non-stop London-Buenos Aires flights and adds a daily Santiago service

6th Tuesday, October 2026 - 22:31 UTC Full article

According to the airline, it will be the only non-stop flight between London and Buenos Aires

British Airways will operate a daily non-stop flight between London Heathrow and Buenos Aires from March 28, 2027, continuing on to Santiago, Chile. A direct route between the British and Argentine capitals has not operated since October 2023.

The service, flights BA245 and BA244, will use a Boeing 777. According to the airline, it will be the only non-stop flight between London and Buenos Aires. The Argentine capital is currently served via Rio de Janeiro; from March, the daily London–Rio flight will no longer continue to Buenos Aires, freeing seats for the Brazilian market.

For Chile, the change means a new daily one-stop service via Buenos Aires, in addition to the non-stop London–Santiago flight the airline operates three times a week, according to the release and specialist aviation media.

“Buenos Aires has always been a key part of our South American network, and we are delighted to strengthen our commitment with a daily non-stop service from London,” said Neil Chernoff, British Airways' director of network planning and strategy, as the airline marks 80 years of flights to the region.

The announcement, made on September 17, is part of a 25% increase in the airline's Latin American capacity for the European summer 2027 season, which also makes its San José, Costa Rica route year-round and adds new routes to Tanzania from May.

Chile's air traffic shows a market in decline. According to the Civil Aeronautics Board, 2,188,070 passengers flew in August, down 2.1% year on year; international traffic fell 2.8% and arrivals from Europe 2.2%.

World.title: Lula targets non-voters and over-70s to overturn the first-round result
World.content:
Lula targets non-voters and over-70s to overturn the first-round result

6th Tuesday, October 2026 - 22:15 UTC Full article

Since Brazil returned to direct presidential elections in 1989, no candidate who came second in the first round has won the runoff.

Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will focus his campaign for the October 25 runoff on mobilising those who did not vote on Sunday, particularly people over 70, and on winning over centrist voters, after finishing almost two points behind Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round.

The challenge is historic. Since Brazil returned to direct presidential elections in 1989, no candidate who came second in the first round has won the runoff.

From the age of 70, voting is no longer compulsory in Brazil, and in 2022 abstention in that group was around 60%, according to figures cited by the newspaper El País. The last Datafolha poll before the vote gave Lula an 11-point lead among older voters. The president had already appealed to them in the final stretch: “Don't think that because you're 70 you shouldn't vote. Go, get up and vote.”

According to Reuters, Lula is also considering announcing that his vice president, Geraldo Alckmin, a centre-right figure, would be his finance minister in a new term, as a gesture to business. The Workers' Party is also hoping Congress will this week approve its proposal to cut working hours to guarantee two days off a week without a pay cut.

“The runoff is another election. It involves a direct clash of projects,” party president Edinho Silva told Globo, adding that Lula would attend “all the debates he can”. On election night, the president linked his rival to organised crime in Rio de Janeiro; Bolsonaro is under investigation in the Banco Master case, without formal charges, and there is no known case against him for organised crime.

Bolsonaro, of the Liberal Party, appeared in Brasília on Tuesday alongside São Paulo governor Tarcísio de Freitas, re-elected on Sunday, and is seeking the backing of his Republicanos party and other right-wing groups. The candidates eliminated in the first round won around 8% of the vote. The senator said he would attend the debates if Lula does: “I want to compare government programmes.” Neither took part in a debate in the first round. The first runoff debate is scheduled for Sunday 11.

World.title: UK agrees £190m Airbus deal to boost RAF's strategic airlift fleet of A400M Atlas
World.content:
UK agrees £190m Airbus deal to boost RAF's strategic airlift fleet of A400M Atlas

6th Tuesday, October 2026 - 09:08 UTC Full article

The British Forces South Atlantic Islands command utilizes the A400M's long-range capabilities to secure and monitor the remote British Overseas Territory.

The UK Ministry of Defence has signed a £190m contract extension with Airbus to deliver a 30% improvement in the availability of the Royal Air Force's tactical and strategic airlift fleet.

The 31-month extension to the medium-term contract will see Airbus continue its maintenance, repair and support for the RAF's A400M Atlas fleet from its UK Support Centre at RAF Brize Norton.

The contract extension through to April 2029 will mean that there will be a significant boost to operational capability and will increase the number of fully capable aircraft available each day from 10 to 13 by the end of next year.

One of them is permanently stationed at MPC in the Falkland Islands as part of No. 1312Flight

Defence Readiness and Industry Minister Luke Pollard said that the deal was a “vote of confidence” for the industry and Brize Norton.

“By boosting availability, we're strengthening the RAF's ability to conduct global operations and deliver on Nato commitments when it matters most,” Mr Pollard said.

The deal comes after “intensive” negotiations led by a small team from the A400M In-Service Support Delivery Team within the NAD Group at Brize Norton with the RAF, industry partners and Airbus.

The A400M Atlas is a cornerstone of the UK's air mobility capability, which is involved in supporting operations ranging from humanitarian relief to rapid troop deployment.

The continued support at Brize Norton will mean that the fleet is ready to meet the demands required without interruption.

“Airbus is proud to be a trusted partner to the Ministry of Defence, and this contract extension reinforces that commitment,” Kata Escott, Airbus Defence and Space UK's managing director, said.

“The A400M Atlas is the backbone of air mobility. Our highly skilled teams work side by side with Royal Air Force personnel and are fully focused on enhancing operational readiness, keeping the fleet mission-ready.”

The A400M Atlas, which has a 42.4m wingspan, is a strategic airlift aircraft powered by its four turboprop engines. The aircraft entered into service with the RAF more than a decade ago, and it is designed to go where other aircraft cannot.

It can fly at up to 40,000ft, while it can hold anything from a Chinook helicopter to 37 tonnes of freight. It can take off and land on beaches or rough terrain meaning it is indispensable for missions in remote areas.

World.title: On first Monday in October Falklands celebrates Peat Cutting Day
World.content:
On first Monday in October Falklands celebrates Peat Cutting Day

6th Tuesday, October 2026 - 09:04 UTC Full article

Peat for decades was used in Falklands to heat homes and cooking food

Monday 5th October has been a public holiday in the Falkland Islands. This is because the first Monday in October every year has been declared Peat Cutting Day, which is a way of celebrating a long standing tradition and recalling the primary fuel that for decades kept Islanders and their homes warm.

October was the time of the year when Islanders wnet out to cut cubes of surface-soil peat, predominant in the Islands, and was used as fuel for heating homes and cooking food in the Islands.

In 2002, the Executive Council of the Falkland Islands made it an official public holiday to be celebrated on the first Monday in October every year. Little peat cutting takes place in modern times, since the Islands have other sources of energy, fossil fuels, electricity (mostly eolic) and other green alternatives.

For decades the smell of peat heating was a distinctive pattern of Stanley and Camp settlements.

World.title: Paraguay's opposition takes Asunción from the Colorado Party and holds Ciudad del Este
World.content:
Paraguay's opposition takes Asunción from the Colorado Party and holds Ciudad del Este

5th Monday, October 2026 - 22:09 UTC Full article

In Ciudad del Este, Daniel Pereira Mujica of the opposition Yo Creo party won with 72.83%, keeping the city in the hands of the party previously led locally by Miguel Prieto

Paraguay's opposition won the mayoralty of Asunción and held that of Ciudad del Este, the country's two most populous cities, in Sunday's municipal elections, according to preliminary results from the electoral authority. The ruling Colorado Party, however, won the vast majority of districts.

With 99.92% of polling stations counted, civil engineer Soledad Núñez of the Alianza Juntos por Asunción won 47.78% of the vote to 45.98% for Colorado candidate Camilo Pérez, president of the Paraguayan Olympic Committee, a margin of 5,024 votes. Núñez was backed by the Patria Querida and Authentic Radical Liberal parties. “Asunción voted, Asunción won. Today the people who don't give up, who resist, who can't be bought, won,” she said on election night.

In Ciudad del Este, Daniel Pereira Mujica of the opposition Yo Creo party won with 72.83%, keeping the city in the hands of the party previously led locally by Miguel Prieto. Prieto has expressed interest in running for president in 2028.

The Colorado Party, to which President Santiago Peña belongs, was winning in 187 of 263 districts and 11 of 17 departmental capitals, and regained the mayoralty of Encarnación. The figures from the preliminary results transmission system must be confirmed by the official count.

After the vote, Núñez said the opposition would file a complaint with prosecutors over the publication of exit polls during election day. A consultancy posted trends for several cities on social media an hour before polls closed, without naming candidates. The Electoral Code prohibits publishing such polls until an hour after closing. “This goes against electoral participation,” said Núñez, who argued the publication may have discouraged voters. Liberal senator Celeste Amarilla called the poll “illegal” and said she would file a complaint if no one else did. The consultancy was not publicly identified and did not comment. Turnout in Asunción was 61.75%, up from 59.65% in 2021.

Municipal elections serve as a political barometer ahead of the 2028 general election.

World.title: São Paulo stocks jump 8% and the real firms after Bolsonaro's first-round win
World.content:
São Paulo stocks jump 8% and the real firms after Bolsonaro's first-round win

5th Monday, October 2026 - 17:30 UTC Full article

Bolsonaro won 47% of valid votes to Lula's 45%, and the two will face each other in the October 25 runoff

Brazilian markets rallied sharply on Monday in response to the first round of the presidential election, in which Senator Flávio Bolsonaro finished ahead of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, contrary to what polls had predicted. The São Paulo Stock Exchange's Bovespa index rose as much as 8% in early trading, above 208,000 points.

Banks led the rally. In New York, before the open, Bradesco's depositary receipts were up 15.2%, Itaú's 14.4%, Nu Holding's 12.2%, Petrobras's 10.3% and Vale's 6.4%. The real gained 1.4% against the dollar, which traded at 5.14 reais.

Bolsonaro won 47% of valid votes to Lula's 45%, and the two will face each other in the October 25 runoff. Investors see the Liberal Party senator as more likely to push through fiscal tightening that would allow high interest rates to come down; Lula avoided committing to spending cuts and expanded social programmes in the final stretch of the campaign. “The market wants change, it wants reforms, it doesn't want a large public deficit,” Pedro Galdi, an analyst at AGF Investments, told Reuters.

Not all assessments were unconditional. Bryan Harris, a partner at political risk consultancy Sabio, warned that the market would look for “clear signals” that Bolsonaro is “serious” about tackling the country's problems, and said the senator had shown little aptitude for economic policymaking.

Precedent suggests caution. Four years ago, the real gained more than 4% and the Bovespa rose 5.5% the day after Jair Bolsonaro outperformed expectations in the first round; weeks later he lost the runoff to Lula.

The Bovespa had already risen 5% in dollar terms in September as the senator's prospects improved, despite reports about his ties to Daniel Vorcaro, former owner of Banco Master, who has been arrested and charged with fraud. Flávio Bolsonaro is under investigation for alleged money laundering in that case, without formal charges, and denies any wrongdoing.

World.title: "The end of the PT era is decreed," says Flávio Bolsonaro after winning the first round
World.content:
“The end of the PT era is decreed,” says Flávio Bolsonaro after winning the first round

5th Monday, October 2026 - 17:18 UTC Full article

The senator pledged to cut the number of ministries and end presidential re-election, a measure that would require a constitutional amendment; he said one term would be enough for him

Senator Flávio Bolsonaro celebrated his first-round victory in Brazil's presidential election in Brasília with a message focused on change. “Change, the word is change. Brazil can't take any more. The end of the PT era is decreed,” he told reporters outside his campaign headquarters.

With almost 99% of votes counted, the Liberal Party candidate took 47.08% of valid votes to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's 45.10%, so the two will face each other in the October 25 runoff. Bolsonaro thanked “almost 56 million” voters and hit back at the pollsters: “The polling institutes had us behind and we grew.” The final Datafolha survey had given Lula 45% and Bolsonaro 42% of valid votes, and AtlasIntel 47% to 44.1%. In 2022, polls also underestimated Jair Bolsonaro's first-round vote.

The senator pledged to cut the number of ministries and end presidential re-election, a measure that would require a constitutional amendment; he said one term would be enough for him. He also said he would appoint at least four justices to the Supreme Federal Court, the same court that sentenced his father to 27 years in prison for attempting a coup. Those appointments depend on vacancies arising and require Senate approval.

Bolsonaro described Lula's government as a series of “records” in violence against women, taxes and business closures, campaign claims the government rejects. Lula, for his part, questioned his rival's record and linked him to the Banco Master case, in which the senator is under investigation without formal charges.

World.title: Lula bets on education and non-voters to overturn the result in the runoff
World.content:
Lula bets on education and non-voters to overturn the result in the runoff

5th Monday, October 2026 - 17:08 UTC Full article

“The result is often unexpected. You never get everything you wanted,” the president said from a hotel in São Paulo

Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has set education, research and industrial policy as the pillars of his campaign for the October 25 runoff, and urged the more than 30 million Brazilians who abstained on Sunday to vote, after finishing behind Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round.

With 99.9% of votes counted, Bolsonaro took 47% of valid votes and Lula 45%. “The result is often unexpected. You never get everything you wanted,” the president said from a hotel in São Paulo. “The second round is the moment to show the true picture of today's Brazil and the Brazil we want.”

Lula pledged to maintain investment in universities, federal institutes and secondary education, and to expand the Pé-de-Meia programme, which gives students a financial incentive to reduce school dropout. “It is through education that we will change this country,” he said, linking that commitment to increasing Brazil's productive and technological capacity.

The 80-year-old president again questioned his rival's record, citing “very serious suspicions” over alleged links to organised crime and to the Banco Master case. Bolsonaro is under investigation in that case, without formal charges, and has denied any wrongdoing.

Abstention will be key. Votes for the candidates eliminated in the first round, around 8% in total, come largely from centre-right and right-wing voters, while those who do not vote are disproportionately from lower-income groups, Lula's electoral base.

World.title: Iván Cazarín, regional CJNG boss known as ‘El Tanque,’ is captured in Zapopan
World.content:
Iván Cazarín Molina — the alleged regional leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) — was captured on Monday by federal authorities, Security Minister (SSPC) Omar García Harfuch confirmed in a social media post.

The detention was the result of a joint operation carried out by Army special forces and the SSPC’s Operations Group, with information from the National Intelligence Center. The National Guard also collaborated, Harfuch said, as did Criminal Investigation Agency investigators from the Federal Attorney General’s Office (FGR), who identified his movements and located him.

Cae en Jalisco Iván N, alias “El Tanque”, presunto operador del CJNG El titular de la Secretaría de Seguridad y Protección Ciudadana (SSPC), Omar García Harfuch, informó sobre la detención en Zapopan de Iván N, alias “El Tanque”, presunto operador regional del Cártel Jalisco Nueva Generación en Veracruz, Oaxaca, Tabasco y Puebla. El operativo conjunto incluyó al Ejército, la SSPC, la Fiscalía General de la República y el Centro Nacional de Inteligencia. El detenido está vinculado a homicidios y al atentado contra un helicóptero militar en 2015. #seguridadpublica #harfuch #jalisco — NX Noticias (@NXNoticias) October 6, 2026

Cazarín, aka “El Tanque” (“The Tank”), was apprehended in Zapopan, Jalisco, part of the greater Guadalajara metropolitan area and the same city in which the authorities captured alleged fuel smuggler Miguel Ángel Solano Ruiz, aka “Capitán Sol,” just three days earlier.

Prosecutors say Cazarín — whose area of ​​operation covered Veracruz, Oaxaca, Tabasco and Puebla — ran a massive fuel theft network and say they have sufficient evidence to charge him with homicide, kidnapping, money laundering and drug trafficking, as well.

Harfuch identified “El Tanque” as a target related to various criminal activities — including 6.8 tons of marijuana seized in Veracruz in July 2024 and the August 2026 kidnapping for ransom of an employee of the state-owned utility company.

El Tanque was also allegedly involved in the rocket-propelled grenade attack on an Army helicopter in Jalisco in 2015, in which nine law enforcement officers lost their lives.

Six months later, federal authorities announced the capture of Cazarín, identifying him as one of the main operators of the CJNG. However, he was only charged with possession of illegal weapons.

The Latinus website says El Tanque was in prison at least through May 2016 when he was transferred from the Altiplano Maximum Security Prison in México state to Puente Grande in Jalisco, but reported that “it is unknown when he was released.”

By 2021, El Tanque was in Tabasco, where he had allegedly established links with “La Barredora,” a crime gang linked to then state Security Minister Hernán Bermúdez Requena.

In September 2024, the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) identified him as the leader of a fuel-smuggling network and tax evasion scheme in which at least eight other people and 26 companies were involved.

The OFAC said the fuel theft operation generated tens of millions of dollars annually for the CJNG.

With reports from La Jornada, El País, CBS News and Proceso

World.title: Nuevo León Gov. García announces US $600M in data center infrastructure investment
World.content:
Nuevo León Governor Samuel García said he has secured US $600 million in investment to develop industrial facilities, primarily data centers, in his state.

The governor made the announcement during his most recent working tour of New York, which concluded Friday. The source of the investment was not given, but it is known that it will go to projects in the cities of Apodaca and Pesquería, expanding on the ongoing investment boom in the border state that has led to the recent inauguration of several tech, data processing and manufacturing facilities.

Como parte de nuestra gira de trabajo en Nueva York, ayer junto a @eloo2 nos reunimos con @Macquarie, grupo global de servicios financieros de Australia que cuenta con áreas industriales y reservas para parques industriales en Apodaca y Pesquería. Juntos, seguiremos explorando nuevas oportunidades para el desarrollo industrial, infraestructura, energía y tecnología entre Nuevo León y Estados Unidos. ¡Ánimo! 🇺🇸🦁👊🏻 — Samuel García (@samuel_garcias) October 2, 2026

The new capital brings total foreign investment in Nuevo León in 2026 to $136.6 billion, according to the governor. “I have no doubt that by December we’ll reach $140 billion,” he said.

García said that Nuevo León is attractive to investors thanks to its strong infrastructure, energy and water availability, the industrial parks in Apodaca and the tax-free Colombia Customs Office.

“Also coming… are the Volvo industrial facility in Ciénega, the Bobcat industrial facility… the Unilever facility in Salinas Victoria, and we just inaugurated the LEGO facility,” García said. “The most important thing is that multinational companies are building their largest facilities, their biggest factories in the world, in Nuevo León.”

The restrictions of a stressed power grid

Though Gov. Gacría insists that his state’s energy supply attracts investment, power grid limitations are a growing problem across the nation. Querétaro state is a case in point.

Investors have announced several multimillion-dollar data center projects in the Bajío state in recent years, drawn by its proximity to the United States, with tech majors such as Amazon, Cloud HQ, Equinix, Microsoft and Ascenty opening facilities.

But the growth of the data center industry has revealed major bottlenecks in Querétaro’s transmission infrastructure.

In Querétaro, the aging electrical grid has proven insufficient for industrial development, and neighboring towns often experience power outages despite the inauguration of a natural gas-fired power plant in December 2025.

Meanwhile, research from the Mexican Institute for Competitiveness (IMCO) suggests that the grid limitations must be addressed to support the expansion of the data center industry.

With reports from México Industry and El Economista

World.title: Mexico’s fixed capital investment grew 6% in July, the fastest pace in 2 years
World.content:
Fixed capital investment in Mexico — money spent by the private and public sectors on long-term assets such as houses, factories and machinery — increased 6% annually in July, the strongest growth of any month in two years.

The national statistics agency INEGI reported the seasonally adjusted growth rate on Monday in its monthly report on gross fixed capital formation, a measure of fixed capital investment (FCI).

It is the product of a 5.9% year-over-year increase in private sector FCI and a 6.9% increase in public sector FCI.

Annual private sector FCI growth increased 2 percentage points from June to reach its highest level in 30 months, a sign that businesses’ confidence in their long-term economic prospects is improving.

However, public sector FCI growth slowed markedly from June, a month in which the annual expansion was 17.3%.

The overall FCI growth rate was up slightly from a 5.9% annual expansion in June. The month-over-month increase in FCI was 1.4%.

In an X post, Gabriela Siller, director of economic analysis at Banco Base, wrote that despite the growth in July, FCI was still 2.35% lower than the all-time high reached in July 2024.

In a separate post, she wrote that the FCI growth in July is “good news for Mexico,” but added that the data “is still insufficient to speak of a sustained recovery of investment flows and confidence to invest.”

In the first seven months of July, annual FCI growth was a more modest 1.7%. Siller is predicting 2% year-over-year growth in FCI in 2026.

Mexico recorded annual economic growth of 1.9% in the second quarter of 2026 and 3.3% in July. The economy grew just 0.4% annually in Q1.

Spending on construction projects drives FCI growth in July

INEGI data shows that investment in construction projects increased 6.9% annually in July. Investment in residential projects grew 9.2% compared to a year earlier, while spending on non-residential projects such as factories and industrial parks increased 4%.

Investment in machinery and equipment grew 4.9% annually. Spending on imported machinery and equipment increased 9.9% compared to a year earlier, while spending on “Made in Mexico” machinery and equipment declined 3.1%.

In the first seven months of 2026, investment in construction projects increased 4.1% annually. Investment in machinery and equipment fell 1% in the same period.

Eduardo Valle, an economist at Coppel, said that the increase in investment in machinery and equipment in July is a “good sign” as it “signifies that companies are modernizing or expanding their productive capacity.”

However, the annual decline in spending on Mexican machinery and equipment is concerning, especially given that it occurred at a time when the federal government is aiming to strengthen Mexican industry with its Plan México economic initiative. Spending on “Made in Mexico” machinery and equipment declined 8% annually between January and July, while investment in imported machinery and equipment increased 3.5%.

With reports from El Financiero

World.title: Activists condemn felling of ancient trees for border wall
World.content:
Federal contractors felled a centuries-old cottonwood on the U.S.-Mexico border Monday after U.S. Border Patrol agents removed protesters who had spent about 70 days trying to save it from President Donald Trump’s border wall expansion.

The tree in Lochiel, Arizona, known to activists as the “grandmother” tree, was the last of four old cottonwoods targeted for removal at the site. Conservation groups estimated its age at 200 to 250 years, the newspaper La Jornada reported.

Just brutal to see. DHS contractors just plowed through the last of the four ancient cottonwood trees in Arizona–a tree older than the border itself–to make way for a double border wall through critical jaguar habitat. A dozen protestors were arrested today trying to stop this travesty. — Laiken Jordahl (@LaikenJordahl) October 6, 2026

Activists told the media that 10 people were arrested and another 10 were cited and released. They said agents used a cherry picker to forcibly remove one protester from the cottonwood — álamo in Spanish — before contractors brought it down.

Protesters said the camp was on private property, while U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) said the trees stood on federal land. The agency did not answer media questions about whether agents had a warrant to enter the encampment, which they did near sunrise on Monday.

Protesters alleged officers tackled demonstrators, kicked people in handcuffs and pushed others into barbed-wire fences. CBP did not respond to The Washington Post’s questions about those allegations.

The Tohono O’odham Nation, an Arizona-based Indigenous tribe whose members and ancestral lands extend into Sonora, condemned the operation in a statement reported by El Universal. Its territory is a popular route for migrants crossing into the United States.

“This is yet another demonstration of the federal government’s reckless disregard for cultural and natural resources in its hasty pursuit to build this useless wall,” the nation said.

CBP said the four cottonwoods had been identified for removal to make way for the wall. The agency said environmental monitors were present before the work and that preconstruction surveys found no active migratory bird nests.

The protest began in late July after contractors removed three neighboring cottonwoods. Activists rotated through a plywood platform in the remaining tree, receiving supplies by bucket and rope. Their occupation stalled construction immediately around it.

The project includes two parallel steel walls through the San Rafael Valley, across from the state of Sonora in Mexico. Conservationists describe the area as an important wildlife corridor, with the cottonwoods providing food, shelter and habitat for migratory birds near the Santa Cruz River.

Erick Meza, the Sierra Club’s borderlands coordinator, said that contractors also intended to remove another cottonwood straddling the border.

Organizer Kate Scott said resistance would continue, with a rally organized by the Tohono O’odham Nation scheduled for Wednesday.

“We are resolute,” she said. “This movement is not going anywhere. They have cut down our grandmother, but her roots are within us.”

With reports from La Jornada, El Universal, KJZZ, Washington Post and Lookout

World.title: Even more security reinforcements are coming to Mazatlán as crime keeps climbing
World.content:
After multiple deployments of troops to Mazatlán over the summer to combat the port and resort city’s escalating cartel-related violence, the federal government has taken a new approach by forming an elite Special Operations Group comprising 29 highly trained Defense Ministry soldiers who will operate within the municipal police department.

The most recent security reinforcement comes during a wave of homicides, armed attacks and explosive-based assaults across the city that led municipal Public Security Minister Gabino Ulises Jacobo Guerrero to urge the public to exercise extra caution between 3 p.m. and 10 p.m., the time period with the highest rate of criminal activity.

The elite force members are said to be highly skilled in night work, explosives handling, parachuting, sharpshooting and urban operations. They will be equipped with armored vehicles, weaponry, reconnaissance drones and technology to detect threats posed by unmanned aircraft.

During a ceremony Monday introducing the Special Operations Group at the Citizen Security Center, municipal Public Security Minister Sinuhé Téllez López explained that this addition stems from agreements reached during a visit by the federal Security Cabinet on Sept. 18. The deployment aims to strengthen coordination among the institutions responsible for addressing insecurity.

Mazatlán Mayor Estrella Palacios Domínguez added that its members will utilize intelligence and investigative work to carry out precision interventions.

In another security move, the City Council provided, at a cost of more than 457,000 pesos (US $25,437), 50 bicycles to Army and National Guard members to bolster preventive patrols in the coastal area, the Historic Center and tourist and commercial areas where vehicle access is difficult.

“These are bicycles designed for preventive patrolling, enabling soldiers and National Guard members to efficiently monitor the coastal area and the Historic Center,” Estrella said.

Minister Guerrero addressed a video showing armed men allegedly heading toward the port, though he clarified that its authenticity, date and destination had not been confirmed. Therefore, he said the recording does not constitute evidence of an incursion.

“Let’s hope it doesn’t happen, but if it does, well, we’ll be here waiting for them,” Guerrero said.

With reports from Debate, Uno TV and Grupo Animal

World.title: After Chihuahua CIA controversy, Querétaro police academy raises new questions about US involvement at state level
World.content:
Listen to this article

Querétaro Governor Mauricio Kuri notified Foreign Affairs Minister Roberto Velasco of U.S. Ambassador to Mexico Ronald Johnson’s Oct. 2 visit to Querétaro, but he didn’t say that the ambassador would be laying the cornerstone of a new International Police Training Academy in the Bajío region state.

The existence of Kuri’s Sept. 23 letter to Velasco came to light after President Claudia Sheinbaum indicated at her Monday morning press conference that her government knew little about the police academy project.

She declared that such an academy — which Kuri called “a home” for “cooperation between the United States and Querétaro in the area of specialized police training” — can’t be established without federal authorization, and questioned why the Querétaro government didn’t invite the Mexican military, the federal Security Cabinet or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to participate in the cornerstone-laying ceremony.

(Contrary to Sheinbaum’s suggestion, federal officials did in fact attend the event, according to the newspaper El Universal.)

After Kuri’s letter was leaked on Monday, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (SRE) released an “informative note” acknowledging its receipt of the governor’s communication, while highlighting that as the International Police Training Academy is “a project involving security cooperation with a foreign government,” it is subject to “prior” federal approval — approval that has not been granted.

Sheinbaum said on Tuesday that a federal security group approved nine “cooperation projects” between the state of Querétaro and U.S. law enforcement agencies between December 2021 and October 2026. However, the International Police Training Academy was not one of them, she said.

In some ways, the United States’ collaboration with Querétaro on a police training academy is similar to the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency’s alleged participation with state forces in a drug lab raid in the northern state of Chihuahua in April. The federal government didn’t approve the CIA’s participation in the domestic security operation, just as it didn’t authorize collaboration between Querétaro and the U.S. government on a new police training academy. Another similarity between the two cases is that they occurred in states governed by the opposition National Action Party (PAN), a party that includes politicians who would like to see the U.S. take a more active role in combating organized crime in Mexico.

U.S. involvement in Mexican affairs — or “interference” as Sheinbaum has put it — has been a hot-button issue this year amid ongoing speculation that the Trump administration could unilaterally use the U.S. military to combat Mexican cartels on Mexican soil.

While the Mexican president has been resolute in rejecting U.S. meddling in Mexican affairs, there are signs that her government doesn’t want to make a major issue of the unauthorized cooperation between Querétaro and the United States. Officials from the Sheinbaum and Trump administrations continue to speak positively about bilateral security cooperation, even though there are a range of tensions in the security relationship, including ones related to U.S. prosecutors’ drug trafficking accusations against Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya and other Mexican officials.

Kuri appears to contradict himself

In his letter to Velasco, Kuri wrote that on Oct. 2, “the executive power of the state of Querétaro” would host a visit by Johnson, “with whom various topics of common interest will be dealt.”

“It is important to point out that the interaction of local public servants and the [U.S.] diplomatic agent in the framework of said visits will be ceremonial in nature and in no way implies the establishment of direct mechanisms of international cooperation in the areas of security or administration of justice, nor the participation or intervention of foreign agents or governments in activities of investigation, prosecution of crime or roles reserved for the Mexican state or which correspond to Mexican authorities,” he wrote.

Despite writing that sentence in his letter to Velasco, Kuri wrote on social media on Oct. 2 that “the cooperation between the United States and Querétaro in the area of specialized police training now has a home in our state: the International Police Training Academy.”

Such cooperation would certainly appear to be an example of international cooperation in the area of security.

In his X post last Friday, Kuri also wrote:

“Today we laid the cornerstone of this space where we will continue the effort we’ve been making for years: investing in the preparation of our police, raising our standards and seeking experiences that allow us to better defend and serve the families of Querétaro. I am enormously grateful to the U.S. government and the Ambassador Ronald Johnson for the collaboration we’ve built and for the trust placed in our state, chosen to establish this international academy, the only one of its kind in Latin America.”

La cooperación entre los Estados Unidos y #Querétaro en materia de formación policial especializada, tiene ahora una casa en nuestro estado: la Academia Internacional de Capacitación Policial. Hoy colocamos la primera piedra de este espacio donde continuaremos con el esfuerzo que hemos estado realizando por años: invertir en la preparación de nuestros policías, elevar sus estándares y buscar experiencias que nos permitan defender y servir cada vez mejor a las familias queretanas. Agradezco enormemente al gobierno de los Estados Unidos, y al señor Embajador Ronald Johnson, por la colaboración que hemos construido y por la confianza depositada en nuestro estado, elegido para establecer esta academia internacional, única en su tipo en América Latina. — Mauricio Kuri (@makugo) October 3, 2026

The title of a statement released by Ambassador Johnson on Saturday provided additional — and very clear — support for the view shared by the federal government and others that Querétaro and the United States are indeed collaborating on security via the establishment of an International Police Training Academy.

That title? “The United States and Querétaro Expand Security Cooperation with New State Interdiction Academy.”

“On behalf of President Trump, I joined Governor Kuri for the groundbreaking of Querétaro’s State Interdiction Academy. This facility highlights that confronting cartels and terrorist groups requires action, resources, and strong institutions, as Querétaro is demonstrating by investing in this academy,” Johnson wrote.

“Querétaro is an example of what we can accomplish when we work together. Over the past decade, the United States has invested more than $10 million in training support and equipment in Querétaro,” he wrote.

“The new academy builds on that cooperation as the first facility of its kind in Mexico and Latin America dedicated specifically to training law enforcement authorities to detect and interdict dangerous drugs, weapons, illicit bulk cash, and other contraband. Officers trained at the new academy will be able to take those capabilities back to their units, states, and communities throughout Mexico,” the ambassador wrote, suggesting that police from across Mexico could receive training at the facility.

On Monday, Sheinbaum questioned why Kuri was collaborating with Johnson rather than the federal Security Cabinet on an international academy focused on training police to combat organized crime.

Organized crime-related offenses are “federal crimes,” Sheinbaum emphasized.

“These are examples where I believe the limit between what should be and what shouldn’t be is reached,” she said.

SRE offers to assist Querétaro in seeking approval for police academy

In its information note, the SRE wrote that “in accordance with the National Security Law, any training or security cooperation project with a foreign government requires prior approval from the High-Level Security Group (GANSEG), an auxiliary body of the National Security Council.”

“The Foreign Ministry assists state and municipal governments in seeking that approval,” the ministry said.

In point No. 3 of a four-point statement, the SRE wrote that the International Police Training Academy in Querétaro is “a project involving security cooperation with a foreign government, so it must be submitted to GANSEG.”

“On the instruction of President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, Secretary Roberto Velasco Álvarez spoke directly with Governor Mauricio Kuri González and sent him an official letter offering the foreign ministry’s assistance in seeking that approval, in a spirit of institutional coordination,” the ministry said.

The offer of assistance suggests that the federal government is prepared to authorize the International Police Training Academy in Querétaro, provided state authorities make a commitment to adhere to all relevant Mexican laws.

In point No. 2, the SRE acknowledged its receipt of Kuri’s letter, noting that the governor “specified” that the visit ‘in no way implies the establishment of direct mechanisms for international cooperation on security or law enforcement.”

In point No. 4, the Foreign Affairs Ministry made it clear that Mexico’s cooperation with the U.S. government on security issues is a federal responsibility.

“Mexico and the United States maintain strong security collaboration, based on respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, mutual respect and trust, shared and differentiated responsibility, and cooperation without subordination. This collaboration is conducted through the institutional channels of the Government of Mexico, in coordination with the states,” the information note said.

Sheinbaum: Querétaro government must ‘follow the procedures’

In addition to pointing out that cooperation between Querétaro and the United States on the International Police Training Academy hadn’t been authorized by GANSEG, Sheinbaum on Tuesday also said that her government was aware that U.S. agencies were slated to “participate” in the academy. Such “participation” would violate Mexican law if the involvement of U.S. authorities wasn’t authorized by the Mexican government.

Sheinbaum said her government “knows” that U.S. agencies were slated to “participate in the academy,” as Querétaro Security Minister Iován Pérez said as much at last Friday’s event.

“It’s not an assumption,” she said before asking for a video of Pérez’s remarks to be played.

“This international training center represents an important step,” the state security minister said.

“It is designed to receive specialized training from U.S. agencies and put it within the reach of Mexican public security institutions,” Pérez said.

Sheinbaum said that “the only thing” being asked of the Querétaro government is that it “follow the procedures” and ask GANSEG and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to authorize the police training academy.

“If it’s going to receive support from the U.S. government, it should request authorization from the high-level group. Why? Because it’s the law,” she said.

“… Can [the Querétaro government] have this international academy? Yes. [But] under what conditions can it have the involvement of U.S. agencies? Under the authorization of the high-level [security] group and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs — if they believe it’s within the framework of our constitution,” Sheinbaum said.

With reports from Sin Embargo, Reforma and El Universal

World.title: Nov. 22 match-up of Vikings vs. 49ers in CDMX sees extraordinary ticket demand
World.content:
The return of the National Football League to Mexico after a four-year absence has prompted extraordinary ticket demand.

The Minnesota Vikings and the San Francisco 49ers will square off in a Week 11 match-up on NBC’s Sunday Night Football at Mexico City’s Estadio Banorte (formerly Estadio Azteca). More than seven weeks before the Nov. 22 game, nearly 840,000 fans had registered to acquire the highly sought-after ducats, according to Ticketmaster.

The ticket sales company said that an average purchase is typically 2.6 tickets per person, thus calculating that the potential demand for the game would be 2.2 million. Ticketmaster said the NFL would have to stage 27 games to accommodate the estimated demand.

Breaking down the data further, Ticketmaster said 45% of ticket requests came from people outside of Mexico City, while 14% of the total came from abroad, including folks from the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, Slovakia and France.

The Vikings-49ers game will be the sixth regular-season NFL game in Mexico, which hosted the first NFL regular-season game outside the United States in 2005 with 103,467 spectators in attendance.

The 49ers — along with the Dallas Cowboys and Pittsburgh Steelers — are among the most popular NFL teams in Mexico.

According to the league itself, Mexico is home to the biggest NFL fan base outside of the United States, estimated at between 23 and 40 million aficionados.

The NFL is contracted to hold single games in Mexico next year and in 2028, as well, with those games also scheduled to take place in Estadio Azteca.

The game promises to be an attractive contest as both the Niners and the Vikings are undefeated through the first four weeks of the season. Tickets range in price from 2,108 pesos (US $177) to 11,656 pesos ($649).

The NFL announced last month that ranchera singer Majo Aguilar and MXKA, an African American singer-songwriter of Mexican descent, will perform the national anthems of Mexico and the United States, respectively.

The halftime entertainment will be supplied by The Warning, a hard rock and alternative rock band formed by three sisters from Monterrey.

With reports from Forbes México, EFE and Aristegui Noticias

World.title: Doctors, nurses have made more than 27 million visits thanks to free home healthcare program: Tuesday’s mañanera recapped
World.content:
Sheinbaum’s mañanera in 60 seconds

🏥 Sheinbaum says universal healthcare card rollout is still limited to seniors: The president said the cards, which include each person’s CURP and will be linked to medical files with their consent, are the “first step” toward the Universal Health Service. She said authorities will gradually expand the card rollout to the entire population. A limited version of the new universal healthcare scheme begins Jan. 1, 2027.

The president said the cards, which include each person’s CURP and will be linked to medical files with their consent, are the “first step” toward the Universal Health Service. She said authorities will gradually expand the card rollout to the entire population. A limited version of the new universal healthcare scheme begins Jan. 1, 2027. 🏠 Salud Casa por Casa has provided more than 27 million home consultations: Welfare Minister Leticia Ramírez said the free home healthcare program, which began in June 2025, serves seniors and people with disabilities. Of the consultations, 12.8 million were first visits, just over 8.3 million were second visits and 5.94 million were third visits.

Welfare Minister Leticia Ramírez said the free home healthcare program, which began in June 2025, serves seniors and people with disabilities. Of the consultations, 12.8 million were first visits, just over 8.3 million were second visits and 5.94 million were third visits. 🍺 Sheinbaum says government has no plans to cut alcohol taxes: Asked about a Labor Party bill to reduce the IEPS excise tax on alcoholic beverages, the president said the Finance and Health ministries would have to review it, but “for now we don’t intend to make any change.”

Why today’s mañanera matters

At her Tuesday morning press conference, President Claudia Sheinbaum spoke about the upcoming commencement of the Universal Health Service and the issuance of universal healthcare cards.

As Mexico News Daily reported in April, the long-term goal of the Universal Health Service is to allow Mexicans (and eligible foreigners) to seek treatment at any public health institution — IMSS, IMSS Bienestar or ISSSTE — regardless of affiliation.

A limited version of the new universal scheme is set to commence in January 2027, with additional healthcare services to be universalized in the coming years, according to Sheinbaum.

The establishment of the Universal Health Service is one of various government healthcare initiatives. Another is the Salud Casa por Casa program, in which seniors and people with disabilities receive periodic visits from healthcare personnel in their homes. Welfare Minister Leticia Ramírez provided an update on the program on Tuesday morning.

Also of note at today’s mañanera were the president’s remarks about a legislative proposal to reduce the IEPS tax on alcoholic beverages, which currently applies at a rate of 26.5%-53% depending on the alcohol content of the drink.

Sheinbaum: Universal healthcare card rollout still limited to seniors

Sheinbaum told reporters that the universal healthcare cards currently being issued to seniors include people’s CURP, or Unique Population Registry Code. She said that the CURP will be linked to people’s medical files, provided they give their consent.

With the linking of medical files to universal healthcare cards, it becomes possible to commence the standardization of “healthcare services in the different institutions,” Sheinbaum said.

The “first step” in the process toward the commencement of the Universal Health Service is the issuance of universal healthcare cards, she said.

Sheinbaum said that authorities are currently issuing cards to seniors and will gradually extend the rollout to the rest of the population.

“We’re beginning with seniors and little by little we’re going to expand this to the entire population,” she said.

She said that when people are issued their universal healthcare cards, they will receive information about “which services will be universal” and how the system will work.

Sheinbaum displayed a slide with images of the card people will receive. Text on the same slide said that the Universal Health Service will commence on Jan. 1, 2027.

“This is the card that everyone will receive,” Sheinbaum said.

“… From Jan. 1 some services are going to be universal and we’re going to increase the [universal] services so that at the end of the six-year term of government, you can go to any healthcare center, doctor’s office or hospital regardless of which institution you are a beneficiary of,” she said.

Salud Casa por Casa program has provided more than 27 million free medical consultations

Ramírez told reporters that the Salud Casa por Casa program is “the largest health [promotion and disease] prevention program in the world.”

She said that more than 27 million free medical consultations have been provided in people’s homes since the Salud Casa por Casa program began in June 2025.

The welfare minister presented data that showed that 12.8 million consultations were first visits to the homes of seniors and people with disabilities. Just over 8.3 million consultations were second visits, while 5.94 million consultations were third visits.

Ramírez said that the data show that the Salud Casa por Casa program doesn’t entail the provision of single “isolated” medical consultations.

“It’s accompaniment, follow-up and prevention,” she said.

“This is possible because health professionals — nurses and doctors — go from street to street, neighborhood to neighborhood, knocking on the doors of adults aged above 65 and people with disabilities,” Ramírez said as a video showing health workers making home visits played on screen.

They provide “personalized care” on behalf of the federal government “for our mothers, grandparents, fathers, families and neighbors,” she said.

Disease prevention “is also social justice,” Ramírez said.

Sheinbaum says her government has no plans to cut alcohol taxes

A reporter noted that there is a legislative proposal to reduce the IEPS excise tax on alcoholic beverages. She asked the president her opinion about the bill, which, if enacted, could encourage higher levels of alcohol consumption and impact federal tax collection.

Sheinbaum said that the government has no plans to modify the IEPS tax that currently applies to alcohol.

The bill was presented by Francisco Javier Guízar Macías, a deputy with the Labor Party, an ally of the ruling Morena party. Sheinbaum appeared to indicate that Morena — which has a majority in both houses of Congress — won’t support the bill.

“The Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Health will have to review [the proposal], but for now we don’t intend to make any change,” she said.

World.content:

PANAMA · CORRUPTION

Key Facts — The country Panama uses the US dollar as its currency and runs the Panama Canal, a vital route for US trade.

— What happened Anti-corruption prosecutors and the National Police arrested former social security chief Enrique Lau Cortés early on Tuesday 6 October.

— The suspicion Prosecutors are investigating alleged illicit enrichment and money laundering, with possible damage to the state of about US$500,000.

— The raids Officers searched his home in Santa María and sites in Paitilla, Dos Mares, Chanis and Playa Blanca, seizing two apartments and two vehicles.

— The fund The Social Security Fund pays pensions and runs a public hospital network, and Panamanian law requires foreign employees in Panama to join it.

— Next step Lau Cortés is to be brought before a judge of guarantees, who reviews the legality of the arrest. He is presumed innocent.

Prosecutors in Panama arrested Enrique Lau Cortés, the former head of the country’s social security fund, early on Tuesday 6 October. The operation, code-named Muralla, targets alleged illicit enrichment and money laundering, La Prensa reported.

The case reaches into the fund that every worker in Panama pays into, foreigners included. Panama uses the US dollar, so the sums under investigation are dollars from the start.

How Operation Muralla Unfolded

Anti-corruption prosecutors and the National Police’s intelligence directorate arrested him at his apartment in Santa María, La Estrella de Panamá reported. Officers raided other properties at the same time.

Those searches covered the Paitilla, Dos Mares and Chanis neighbourhoods of Panama City and Playa Blanca, a beach resort on the Pacific coast. Investigators seized a beach apartment, a city apartment and two vehicles, according to La Estrella.

The Anti-Corruption Prosecutor’s Office belongs to the Public Ministry, the prosecution service led by Attorney General Luis Carlos Gómez Rudy. Prosecutors put the possible damage to the state at about US$500,000.

He first had a medical check at a health centre in El Chorrillo, Panamá América reported. He was then taken to the Judicial Investigation Directorate, the police detective unit, in Ancón.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Panama Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Who Is Enrique Lau Cortés

Lau Cortés took over the Social Security Fund, the Caja de Seguro Social or CSS, in 2019 under former President Laurentino Cortizo. Cortizo’s term ended in July 2024, and Lau Cortés stayed on into the current government of José Raúl Mulino.

The fund pays retirement benefits to insured workers. It also runs its own network of hospitals and clinics, separate from the Ministry of Health’s public hospitals.

The Audits Behind the Case

The arrest follows more than a year of scrutiny of his management. The Comptroller General’s Office, Panama’s state auditor, had already ordered his assets, bank accounts and vehicles frozen up to US$2.9 million.

That order, a resolution dated 25 November 2025 according to La Estrella, followed an audit that found alleged irregularities involving medicines and medical supplies. An asset freeze is a precautionary step and does not by itself prove wrongdoing.

In May 2025, the fund’s legal director, Franklin Castrejón, confirmed a formal complaint over his management, La Prensa reported. It concerns US$400 million moved to the central government.

According to that complaint, US$300 million went in 2023 and US$100 million in 2024. The transfers were booked as loans or advances due back within 30 days, which were never repaid.

It is not clear whether Tuesday’s arrest draws on that complaint or on the Comptroller’s audit. Prosecutors have so far described the case only as illicit enrichment and money laundering.

What It Means for You

Panama’s 2005 social security law requires all workers in the country, Panamanian or foreign, to join the fund. Americans employed in Panama therefore pay into it.

Insured workers, foreign or Panamanian, are treated in the fund’s own hospitals and clinics. Foreign retirees who do not work in Panama fall outside that legal obligation.

Our guide to health care in Panama explains how coverage works for foreigners. No authority has announced any change to the fund’s hospital services or pension payments because of the case.

What Is Not Known

Prosecutors have not published the evidence or the exact source of the alleged US$500,000 loss. No date for the hearing before the judge of guarantees had been reported by Tuesday afternoon.

His lawyer, Kathia Quiel Carreira, told the broadcaster Telemetro on Tuesday that the defence is worried about his health. No response to the allegations themselves has been reported.

Under Panamanian law he is presumed innocent until a court rules otherwise.

More: Panama news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Enrique Lau Cortés?

He headed Panama’s Social Security Fund, the Caja de Seguro Social, from 2019, under former President Laurentino Cortizo. He was arrested early on Tuesday 6 October in an anti-corruption operation.

What is he accused of?

Prosecutors are investigating alleged illicit enrichment and money laundering, with possible damage to the state of about US$500,000. No court has ruled, and he is presumed innocent.

Do Americans in Panama pay into the social security fund?

Yes, if they work in Panama, because the 2005 social security law requires every worker, Panamanian or foreign, to join the fund. Retirees who do not work there fall outside that obligation.

What happens next in the case?

He is to appear before a judge of guarantees, who reviews the legality of the arrest. At that hearing, prosecutors can also present charges and ask for measures such as pretrial detention.

World.content:
